# ratstack.sh

> For agents: start with the [agent guide](https://ratstack.sh/llms.txt). Every page is Markdown by default; add `Accept: text/html` for HTML.


> Build an app and its cloud infrastructure in one TypeScript program.

Effect describes work with typed failures and required services. A service is a named interface for one job. Alchemy declares cloud resources and plans changes before applying them.

The fence is the compiler checks, lint rules, and hooks that reject prohibited code and shortcuts.

## Connect with MCP

MCP means Model Context Protocol. It lets an agent client discover and call tools.

Point any MCP client at `https://ratstack.sh/mcp`. Protocol 2026-07-28 is stateless and has no `initialize` handshake: every request sends `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, and the `params._meta` block shown here.

```sh
curl --request POST 'https://ratstack.sh/mcp' \
  --header 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --header 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28' \
  --header 'Mcp-Method: tools/list' \
  --data '{"id":"rat-stack-tools","jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list","params":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities":{},"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo":{"name":"rat-stack-example","version":"0.1.0"},"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion":"2026-07-28"}}}'
```

Older clients (2025-11-25 back to 2024-11-05) send `initialize` as usual. Each one gets its own session, held between requests by a Durable Object, Cloudflare's persistent state and compute service.

Each IP may make 120 API or MCP requests per 60 seconds. `execute` also allows 6 calls per IP and 300 total calls per 60 seconds. Cloudflare counts these limits separately in each location.

## Run code: one program instead of several calls

A capability is one named action with shared input and output definitions and a server-side implementation.

Use `POST /api/execute` or the MCP `execute` tool to call content capabilities. The program can search, pass the result to read, and return only what you need. It cannot call `joinInterest`.

`execute` runs the `code` value as the body of an async function. `return` sets `result`, and `console.log` output appears in `logs`; imports, exports, and `fetch` are unavailable.

A successful program returns HTTP 200 with `result`, `logs`, `toolCalls`, and `truncated`. A failed program returns HTTP 422 with `_tag: "ExecuteError"`, `kind`, `message`, optional `tag`, and the same logs, call history, and truncation fields. Failures have no `result`. Timeouts use `TimeoutExceeded`. Blocked fetch calls use `ExecutionFailure` with a refusal message. MCP reports a tool error; CLI exits non-zero; RPC returns the typed failure. Consumers of the old `diagnostic` field must use the failure response instead.

```js
const found = await tools.search({ query: "cartridges", limit: 1 });
const page = await tools.read({ id: found.matches[0].id });
return { title: page.title, id: page.id };
```

```sh
curl --request POST 'https://ratstack.sh/api/execute' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"code":"return 1 + 1"}'
# {"logs":[],"result":2,"toolCalls":[],"truncated":false}
```

## Choose the next action

1. Search for the job you need with `search({ query, limit })`.
2. Read a matching document with `read({ id })`, using the stable id returned by search. Read the owning rules and skill before changing code.
3. For lore, follow `backlinks({ slug })` or `neighbors({ slug, depth: 1 })` to related pages. Use `mentions({ slug })` for unlinked references and `path({ from, to })` to connect two lore pages. Use the page's lore slug, not a source file path.

A capability is one named action with shared input and output definitions and a server-side implementation.

For a new behavior, start with [one capability, every surface](https://ratstack.sh/lore/one-capability-every-surface) and [add a capability](https://ratstack.sh/skills/add-a-capability). For stateful work, read [add a lifecycle machine](https://ratstack.sh/skills/add-a-lifecycle-machine). For a provider, keep the port in core: an application-owned interface named for the job it needs. Keep the adapter, its provider-specific implementation, outside core: [hexagonal architecture](https://ratstack.sh/lore/hexagonal-architecture). For agent-facing guidance, read [HATEOAS](https://ratstack.sh/lore/hateoas).

To remove a surface or package you don't need, follow [Keep or cut](https://ratstack.sh/README.md#keep-or-cut) and the [keep-or-cut skill](https://ratstack.sh/skills/keep-or-cut). Trace the imports, delete what depends on it, then run `pnpm turbo run check test build`.

[Interest signup](https://ratstack.sh/systems/interest) is agent-only. Read [Build Agent Loops That Never Stop Shipping](https://ratstack.sh/tokenmaxx#interested), obtain a fresh page ticket, and submit through `joinInterest` only after the person approves the exact card and contact permission. A person confirms their email through the email link in a browser; submission is not confirmation. Show the returned message to the person. If it says "Too many requests right now. Try again in a minute.", wait one minute and retry once. If it says the confirmation email could not be sent yet, do not resubmit; the application is saved.

Workshop resources have a separate [MCP server](https://ratstack.sh/tokenmaxx/mcp). Use it for the schedule, prep, public links and published exercises. Applications still use the main server's `joinInterest`.

## Suggest a CAFE entry through your agent

Help the person you assist suggest a story for [news](https://ratstack.sh/news) or a project for the [directory](https://ratstack.sh/directory).

1. Check the page for an existing entry. You can also POST JSON to `/api/listCafeNews` or `/api/listCafeProjects`. Do not submit a duplicate.
2. Read the source repository and gather the fields below. Cite repository file paths for each stack claim. Do not invent evidence.
3. Draft the exact issue title and all fields. Say whether this is the person's own work. Show the person the draft, including any public attribution.
4. File only after the person approves that exact issue. Use the matching form in `joelhooks/rat-stack`.
5. Submit once. Do not spam or retry through another surface when the result is uncertain. Check GitHub for the issue first.

### Fields

- **News:** HTTPS URL, title and one-line summary (each at most 280 characters), kind (release, post, video or launch), optional repo (`owner/repo`), optional author GitHub login and X handle, and why it is CAFE.
- **Project:** HTTPS repo URL, title (at most 280 characters), one-line summary (at most 350 characters), and evidence for Cloudflare, Alchemy, Foldkit and Effect. Each evidence string names a file path and what it proves, in at most 280 characters. Write `Not found` for a letter without evidence.
- Disclose the person's connection to the entry in either form. Leave unknown optional fields blank.

### File the approved issue

Use `gh issue create --repo joelhooks/rat-stack --template cafe-news.yml` for a story, or `gh issue create --repo joelhooks/rat-stack --template cafe-project.yml` for a project. Use only the approved title and fields.

If gh is unavailable or cannot use issue forms, give the person the matching prefilled URL and the approved fields:

- News: `https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/issues/new?template=cafe-news.yml&title=URL_ENCODED_APPROVED_TITLE`
- Project: `https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/issues/new?template=cafe-project.yml&title=URL_ENCODED_APPROVED_TITLE`

Replace the title placeholder with the URL-encoded approved title. Prefill form fields with URL-encoded values using their form IDs as query keys. The person can review and file the issue in GitHub.

Joel or the desk reviews each suggestion. Listing is not guaranteed.

## Lore

### Idea



- [A browser send follows one path to the capability](/lore/a-browser-send-follows-one-path) — In the Foldkit docs browser, a search is a Message, then an update, then a named Command that calls the search capability over RPC on a cache miss and returns a result Message.
- [A clean playground](/lore/a-clean-playground) — rat-stack does real work with packages that stay easy to add and remove.
- [Agents explore, tests remember](/lore/agents-explore-tests-remember) — Let agent users explore scenarios; turn a good bug reproduction into a repeatable test.
- [An MCP your users want](/lore/an-mcp-your-users-want) — Rhys Sullivan's practical guide gives rat-stack a checklist for useful MCP tools.
- [Shared caches hold completed values](/lore/cache-completed-values) — Keep pending request I/O out of isolate-scoped caches.
- [Capture first, shape later](/lore/capture-first) — Store events without rejecting them for an evolving event shape, then decide their shape when you query.
- [Cartridges](/lore/cartridges) — A cartridge owns one job and brings the infrastructure its service needs.
- [Code snippets quote a pinned source](/lore/code-snippets) — Shipped design brief: pinned Git objects, typed diagnostics, and one build-only snippet model for both views.
- [Concurrent work needs an owner and a bound](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner) — Limit active work, retain result order, and stop child work when its owning lifetime ends.
- [Configuration is a supplied, validated dependency](/lore/configuration-is-a-dependency) — Parse configuration when a Layer builds, reject invalid values, and supply controlled settings in tests.
- [Dependency injection is the reason to choose Effect](/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect) — Effect tracks service requirements in types and supplies replaceable implementations through Layers.
- [Durability starts with a recovery record](/lore/durability) — A reading order for storage, replay, worker ownership, overload, and recovery tests.
- [Flags climb on evidence](/lore/flags-climb-on-evidence) — A flag ladder connects each rollout step to scoped measurements, approval, and a durable receipt.
- [HATEOAS](/lore/hateoas) — Links in a representation tell its reader what to do next; rat-stack applies that idea to agent-facing pages and responses.
- [Hexagonal architecture](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) — Ports name the application's jobs; adapters connect them to the outside world.
- [Effect keeps the surfaces on one contract](/lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect) — Schema owns values, projections build interfaces, and Layers supply implementations.
- [HTTP success needs a status check and a decoder](/lore/http-responses-need-validation) — Supply the client, check the response status, decode accepted data, and name failures at the adapter boundary.
- [Worker init runs twice](/lore/init-runs-twice) — Alchemy Worker initialization runs in deploy and runtime contexts, so resource declarations need a boundary.
- [Lauren Tan's skills](/lore/lauren-tan-skills) — Lauren Tan (poteto) publishes skills in several repos: brainmaxxing for memory and skill improvement, noodle for skill-based orchestration, how for explaining a codebase, and a verification-skill example.
- [Layer composition makes dependencies explicit](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) — Supply a service's dependencies, choose which services remain visible, and reuse Layer identity within a build.
- [Lifecycles are machines](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines) — XState owns finite lifecycle states while declared Effect actors own side effects.
- [Matt Pocock's skills](/lore/matt-pocock-skills) — Matt Pocock's skills repo packages the agent skills he says he uses every day, built to be small, adaptable, and composable.
- [MCP is another surface](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface) — MCP lists and calls schema-typed tools; rat-stack projects the same handlers instead of adding MCP-only behavior.
- [mdsvex left unified](/lore/mdsvex-left-unified) — The next parser leaves unified; the CommonMark migrator still uses remark.
- [No comments](/lore/no-comments) — Code comments are banned because names, types, tests, and boundaries should carry the meaning.
- [One capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) — A schema-typed contract and one handler feed every interface rat-stack keeps.
- [One program can replace several tool calls](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls) — Code mode combines typed content calls inside one bounded execute request.
- [One schema, three surfaces](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces) — A capability contract feeds CLI, HTTP, and MCP; OpenAPI is generated output, not their input.
- [OpenAPI describes the refusal too](/lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too) — The generated HTTP contract declares inputs, outputs, and the bodyless 400 returned when decoding fails.
- [Rat King carries signed mail between named agents](/lore/rat-king) — Rat King gives agents named mailboxes, signed messages, optional encryption, and Pi, CLI, and MCP clients.
- [Rat's Nest keeps the code public and the inventory private](/lore/rats-nest) — Joel's purpose-built on-prem cloud uses rat-stack and Alchemy, with private inventory outside the public repo.
- [Run Effect at the integration boundary](/lore/run-effect-at-the-boundary) — Build the runtime where a calling framework enters, reuse its services, and dispose it when that integration ends.
- [Schemas define the boundary](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) — Define accepted data with Schema, decode unknown input before dispatch, and encode results through the declared contract.
- [Scopes release resources when work ends](/lore/scopes-own-resources) — Acquire resources lazily, keep their use inside the owner, and release them after success, failure, or interruption.
- [A service captures its construction dependencies](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) — Build a service with its dependencies, then expose methods that callers can use without rebuilding the graph.
- [The rat-stack bestiary eats excuses](/lore/shitrat-bestiary) — A field guide to eight documented rat-stack creatures, with real habitats, enforceable behaviour, and strictly imaginary temperaments.
- [ShitRat's canon is an incident log](/lore/shitrat-canon) — Four public ShitRat stories: a comment ban, a hold that blocked its own migration, a desktop body, and a domain for the rat.
- [ShitRat wants receipts before claims](/lore/shitrat-creed) — The familiar's creed: read the file, run the command, give the number, admit uncertainty, and spare everyone the corporate sludge.
- [Joel bought a domain and the rat built its own house](/lore/shitrat-origin) — ShitRat's public origin story starts with a gift: shitrat.ai, a hand-written page, and a rat doing its own deployment.
- [A rat can be a name with a mailbox](/lore/shitrat-rat-king) — Rat King's named mailboxes and leased readers give ShitRat a postal mythology with a clear line between the rules and the rats' stories.
- [The rat has rituals for proving it happened](/lore/shitrat-rituals) — The gate, the snapshot dance, receipts before claims, and the deployment check give rat-stack's folklore some repeatable steps.
- [The war stories](/lore/shitrat-war-stories) — Seven public repo incidents: a deploy undoes itself, failure says 200, sessions forget their guests, and the rat tests the demolition instructions.
- [Structure an Effect codebase by domain](/lore/structure-effect-by-domain) — Start with folders for application work, services and Layers in the same file, and startup code that supplies implementations.
- [Tests prove behavior through supplied services](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place) — Supply services through Layers, choose properties or models for domain rules, and reject tests that cannot detect broken behavior.
- [The fence](/lore/the-fence) — The fence uses compiler checks, lint rules, and hooks to reject unsafe shortcuts.
- [There is no ISR on Cloudflare](/lore/there-is-no-isr-on-cloudflare) — SvelteKit's Vercel ISR setting does not configure Workers Cache; our local comparison did not prove cache reuse.
- [Trace operations where they mean something](/lore/trace-meaningful-operations) — Name useful operations, add safe context, and distinguish creating a span from delivering it to a backend.
- [An agent applied through Markdown and HTTP](/lore/two-lines-of-curl-is-a-front-door) — One observed application used the Markdown page and llms.txt, then one POST; confirmation followed 88 seconds later.
- [UI behaviour is a scene](/lore/ui-behaviour-is-a-scene) — A Foldkit Scene drives update, view, and subscriptions with input and time as plain data, then asserts on what the view shows.

### Concept



- [Accumulate independent errors before writing output](/lore/accumulate-independent-errors) — Check every independent job before any job writes an asset.
- [Admission control protects recovery](/lore/admission-controls-new-work) — Refuse or defer work that cannot be served usefully under current load.
- [Source-first workflow](/lore/agent-source-first-workflow) — Michael Arnaldi says agents should inspect a library's current source instead of trusting stale model knowledge.
- [Alchemy Domain models a business as commands, aggregates, and events](/lore/alchemy-domain) — Alchemy Domain is a domain-driven design framework for Effect whose one model runs in memory for tests and on Cloudflare Durable Objects in production.
- [Ambient cloud](/lore/ambient-cloud) — Sam Goodwin describes a cloud experience where credentials and accounts become available through one interface.
- [Anti-money](/lore/anti-money) — Sam Goodwin frames Alchemy as reducing SaaS products to libraries and shifting value elsewhere.
- [AT Protocol separates identity, data, and application schemas](/lore/at-protocol) — AT Protocol connects persistent account identifiers, signed public repositories, hosting services, and shared schemas.
- [Backpressure reaches the producer](/lore/backpressure-reaches-the-producer) — Bounded consumption helps only when upstream respects waiting or refusal.
- [Bindings](/lore/bindings) — Sam Goodwin describes bindings as the place where runtime permissions and configuration meet infrastructure.
- [Build-time work stays out of requests](/lore/build-time-work-stays-out-of-requests) — Git reads and highlighting produce static assets before the Worker handles requests.
- [Bulkheads isolate scarce capacity](/lore/bulkheads-isolate-capacity) — Reserve independent capacity for workloads that must not starve each other.

- [Auth](/systems/auth) — Email and password sign-in through Better Auth, with the signed-in person provided to each RPC call.
- [Capabilities](/systems/capabilities) — Named application actions exposed through generated interfaces share one definition and one server-side implementation.

- [Devtools](/systems/devtools) — Development-only capabilities inspect calls and lifecycle transitions without entering production bundles.
- [Durability](/systems/durability) — Seven durable Effect patterns, each with its seam, its fence, and the incident that taught it.
- [Fence](/systems/fence) — Strict effect-tsrs diagnostics, lint, and hooks protect the gate; patched tsc checks compiler parity on checker bumps.
- [Feature flags](/systems/flags) — Typed feature flags with owners, removal dates, and stable subject rollouts.
- [Interest signup](/systems/interest) — Agent-only applications start email confirmation through interfaces owned by core and delivery implemented in a separate package.

- [Motion](/systems/motion) — @rat-stack/motion gives Foldkit apps Penner and CSS easings, tweens, fixed-step springs and interpolation, held in the Model and checked by properties.
- [One prompt serves people and agents](/systems/prompts) — Source-owned agent prompts with typed discovery and copyable browser pages.
- [Ratstack Tube](/systems/tube) — Curated videos for learning the stack, ranked S to F, with a short take on each, built from one data file.
- [Turbo remote cache](/systems/turbo-cache) — A separate Worker stores streamed Turbo artifacts in R2, with one credential per team and lifecycle expiry.
- [Web](/systems/web) — The Foldkit reader renders on the server and prerenders its public pages; the browser hydrates the same view.

## Skills

- [add-a-capability](/skills/add-a-capability) — Learn how one contract and its handler become a command, HTTP route, MCP tool, browser RPC, and sandbox call.
- [add-a-feature-flag](/skills/add-a-feature-flag) — Declare a typed feature flag, its scoped evidence ladder, approval roles, removal date, and durable ledger adapter.
- [add-a-lifecycle-machine](/skills/add-a-lifecycle-machine) — Learn how XState owns a lifecycle while Effect owns its work, errors, and services.
- [add-a-store](/skills/add-a-store) — Add persistence through a service named for an application job, with validation, vendor Layers, migrations, bounded reads, and shared backend tests.
- [durability](/skills/durability) — Keep a rat-stack app standing when a provider, pool, or dependency slows down or a worker dies. Use at any I/O boundary, connection pool, provider call, shared waiter, fan-out, flag, gate, or work that can outlive a request, or when asked "what happens when this is slow", "add a timeout", "make this durable", or "what survives a crash".
- [find-peers](/skills/find-peers) — Refresh public peers, exact stack versions, and tiers after stack bumps. On gardener passes, refresh peers checked more than 14 days ago without blocking other work.
- [gardener](/skills/gardener) — Keep rat-stack current and clean. Update exact dependency versions, learn from repos on the same versions, and add lint rules before cleanup.
- [investigate-a-failure](/skills/investigate-a-failure) — Find the cause of a crash, wrong output, flaky test, or slow run with evidence, fix it at its source, and leave a notebook a person can learn from. Use when something fails intermittently, when the first fix idea is "raise the timeout" or "swap the version", or when asked "why does this break" or "make this stable".
- [keep-or-cut](/skills/keep-or-cut) — Learn which pieces depend on each other, then keep only the ones your project needs.
- [learn](/skills/learn) — Present Effect, Alchemy, XState, and application-design concepts during real work when the operator enables learn mode. Use for adaptive explanations and local learning progress.
- [learn-alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy) — Learn how Alchemy 2 turns an Effect program into a planned Cloudflare deployment.
- [learn-rat-stack](/skills/learn-rat-stack) — Trace a capability through Effect, XState, five projections, the CLI, and Alchemy. Try hosted search and read.
- [model-a-protocol](/skills/model-a-protocol) — Check a protocol with a small TLA+ model before you build or change it. Use when steps can interleave or die halfway, such as a crash between two writes, a retry after an unknown outcome, an alarm or sweep that redrives work, or two writers on one record. Also use when asked "can this race?", "what if it dies here?", or "model this", or before a durability design review.
- [onboard-a-list](/skills/onboard-a-list) — Analyze or migrate an email list. Measure sanitation rules, preserve stops, choose a cohort, and verify an authorized import or sending cutover.
- [profile-a-worker](/skills/profile-a-worker) — Capture a CPU or heap profile of a deployed Cloudflare Worker or Durable Object and read it with pprof. Use when a Worker is slow, burns CPU, nears its memory limit, throws Exceeded Memory, or you need to know which function costs the most in production.
- [query-design](/skills/query-design) — Design or review SQL reads, writes, scans, backfills, and slow database paths. Use before changing a store method or any loop that queries. Covers round-trip arithmetic, batching, keyset paging, index evidence, row budgets, PlanetScale Vitess limits, Hyperdrive connections, statement-count tests, and statement-template fences.
- [rat-stack-mode](/skills/rat-stack-mode) — Route non-trivial rat-stack code, data, design, investigation, and documentation tasks to every matching playbook and principle.
- [security-audit](/skills/security-audit) — Security guidance and vulnerability review for codebases, APIs, services, CLI tools, libraries, and daemons. Use for security questions, focused reviews, vulnerability research, security audits, or pen tests. Run the complete workflow only for explicit codebase audit or pen-test requests, full/comprehensive/end-to-end reviews, or requested report artifacts.
- [ship](/skills/ship) — Learn how to ship a change through merge, CI, release, stage deployment, rollout, verification, rollback and flags.
- [test-behaviour](/skills/test-behaviour) — Pick the test shape that proves a behaviour. Use when you ask "how do I test this?", add a test, test a domain rule, a lifecycle, a retry, a session, a UI interaction, a timer, or a race, or review a test that might be tautological.
- [uncomplect](/skills/uncomplect) — Find responsibilities that a rat-stack design combines, separate them into capabilities, cartridges, machines, features, and clients, and enforce that separation through types and checks. Use when asked to simplify, review, or replace a design, "what would Rich Hickey do", "optimize for deletion", or "define this error out of existence".
- [use-a-prompt](/skills/use-a-prompt) — Discover and read published rat-stack prompts before starting a task with one.
- [write-a-wiki-page](/skills/write-a-wiki-page) — Write or revise public wiki pages with short prose, cited claims, meaningful visuals, and pinned code snippets.

# /prompts/hill-climb

Source: .brain/resources/prompts/hill-climb.svx
SHA-256: 1d477512e567eade7b0f4b818c50dc9961716e06f1bf293c4ad915092778d946

This is a very long-running thread. Expect it to run for months. Your job is to move this app, one change at a time, toward a perfect rat-stack app: pure Effect, honest types, and a fence that makes the easy path the right path.

You control your own schedule. Wake on an interval between one hour and one day. Between wakes you can sleep, wait for subagents, or watch CI and deploys.

## The standard

Read these before your first cycle, and again whenever they change:

- `AGENTS.md`: repo law, the fence and the sign-off rules.
- `VISION.md`: what the app is for.
- `skills/rat-stack-mode`, `skills/gardener` and `skills/uncomplect`.
- https://ratstack.sh/llms.txt: the reference, the lore and the systems pages.

## Each cycle

1. **Measure.** Record a scorecard. Every number must come from a command you ran, never from reading code by eye:
   - Gate: does `pnpm turbo run check test build` pass, and how long does it take?
   - Fence: lint warnings and the lint baseline, Effect diagnostic overrides, type assertions, and comments.
   - Effect: `Effect.run*` outside entry points, untyped errors, unparsed boundaries, services that leak their dependencies, and hand-built surfaces that bypass a capability.
   - Lifecycles: finite modes or retries that are booleans and flags when they should be XState machines.
   - Tests: example tests that should be properties or models, and properties that have never failed against a planted bug.
   - Cartridges: does each one still pass the deletion test?
   - Production: request errors, latency and Worker crashes from your observability, compared with last week.
   - Pins: drift from the stack versions on https://ratstack.sh/resources/peers.
2. **Rank.** Put every gap on one scale: user harm first, then how far the code is from the standard, then size. Pick the top one. Skip anything that needs owner sign-off, and list it for me instead.
3. **Fix.** Hand the gap to a subagent in its own clone. If the bad pattern can come back, add a lint rule first and make it fail. Then make the smallest coherent change, and plant a bug to prove any new test can fail.
4. **Prove.** Run the full gate. Deploy to a preview or staging stage, never production, and measure again there.
5. **Open one PR** with four sections:
   - **Problem:** what was wrong, with the evidence.
   - **Solution:** what changed, and why this way.
   - **Before:** the scorecard numbers and measurements.
   - **After:** the same numbers, measured the same way.

## Never

- Bypass a hook, pass `--no-verify`, or loosen a lint rule, diagnostic or test to make something pass.
- Change a dependency version, delete or replace a cloud resource, or deploy to production without my sign-off.
- Mix two reasons in one PR, or claim a number you did not measure.

## Before I give you the green light

Run through your systems with me. Show me:

- that you can run the gate and read its result;
- which observability you can query, with one real number from it;
- where previews or staging deploy, and how you measure them;
- your first scorecard, and the top three gaps you would fix.

Then wait for my go.

# /AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md
SHA-256: 7d93c26560e95d145cf8fc48bee452c1cfd05a69e0b722e4e09a803e28530462

# Agent instructions

For a non-trivial task, start with `skills/rat-stack-mode`.

This file is the repo law for agents and contributors. It holds commands, validation rules, architecture constraints, and project stop rules. Read `VISION.md` for intent before planning substantial work. `VISION.md` does not override this file. Pi sessions also load `.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` and the repo-local extension `.pi/extensions/project.ts`.

## Stack contract

Workspace `package.json` files declare the pinned stack. [README.md](/README.md#what-is-in-the-stack) summarizes it. Keep dependencies exact. Repo-local config wins. Record drift instead of silently migrating the project.

- pnpm workspaces + Turborepo (`apps/*`, `packages/*`)
- Node `>=24.18.0` and pnpm `11.3.0`; do not replace pnpm with Bun or npm for installs
- Effect `4.1.2` and `@effect/platform-node` `4.1.2`. Foldkit `0.170.0` peers on `effect ~4.1.0`, so no peer allowances or patches remain. Every Effect package resolves to one runtime. Crypto lives in `effect/crypto/*`: `SecureRandom` and `Digest` replace the removed `effect/Crypto`, and `NodeServices` no longer provides them.
- XState `6.0.0-beta.1` for finite lifecycles, retries, cancellation, and resumability
- `@xstate/effect` `1.0.0-beta.0` bridges the two: machines run as scoped Effects via `createEffectActor`, side effects are declared `createEffectLogic` actors. `vendor/README.md` keeps the rules for the next unpublished pin
- Foldkit `0.170.0` with `@foldkit/ui` and `@foldkit/devtools` `0.170.0`, `@foldkit/markdown` `0.15.0`, and `@foldkit/vite-plugin` `0.29.0` for the web UI, server-rendered and prerendered by default
- Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.85` with the `@alchemy.run/cloudflare`, `@alchemy.run/drizzle`, and `@alchemy.run/sql` providers (Infrastructure as Effects) for every cloud resource; declared in `apps/infra/alchemy.run.ts`, authenticated through Alchemy profiles, never through env vars in this repo. `@alchemy.run/test` `2.0.0-beta.85` runs the Worker runtime tests
- TypeScript `7.0.2` in strict mode, patched by `@effect/tsgo` `0.67.5` in `prepare` so the Effect language service diagnostics in `tsconfig.base.json` fail `tsc`, not just the editor. Escape hatch for a real boundary: `// @effect-diagnostics-next-line <rule>:off` with a reason
- `@yielded/effect-tsrs` `0.2.3` runs `typecheck` and `check` with `diagnostics --project tsconfig.json --strict --type-check`. `--type-check` includes ordinary TypeScript diagnostics; `--strict` makes Effect warnings fail. It bundles tsrs revision `8f135f106a63`, contained in plain tsrs `0.20.0`. Keep `ignoreEffectWarningsInTscExitCode` false. Patched TypeScript `7.0.2` with `@effect/tsgo` `0.67.5` runs through `typecheck:tsc` and `typecheck:parity` at the switch and on checker bumps (`pnpm bump:checkers`), not on every CI run. Report any checker disagreement.
- Plain tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta` stays in `typecheck:fast`, targeting TypeScript `7.1.0-beta`. It still has no Effect diagnostics; use `typecheck` or `check` for those.
- `@effect/vitest` `4.1.2` for every Effect test: `it.effect` and `it.layer(layer)`; `Effect.run*` and `ManagedRuntime.make` in test files are a lint error
- `@oxlint/plugins` `1.92.0` for the two typed lint rules in `scripts/oxlint-plugin-*.ts` and the vendored [anti-slop](https://github.com/dmmulroy/anti-slop) rules in `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/` (all generic rules plus the Effect group, at `error`). The copy is ours; `UPSTREAM.md` there says where it came from and how to take upstream fixes
- Oxlint `1.92.0` with Ultracite `8.1.1`, Oxfmt `0.77.0`, and Turborepo `2.11.10`
- varlock `1.24.0`: declare every env var in `.env.schema`, never read `.env.local` directly, run `pnpm env:check` after schema edits

The base Effect plugin owns diagnostic severity. Child configs may add exact `allowedUnstableApis` only for modules warned about in that scope. Do not use subtree prefixes, copy severity maps, or set `ignoreEffectWarningsInTscExitCode` to true.

## Packages

- **`@rat-stack/capability`**:
  - Path: `packages/capability`
  - Role: `defineContract`, `implement`, and the `toCommand`, `toHttpApi`, `toToolkit`, `toRpc`, and `toCodeMode` projections
- **`@rat-stack/core`**:
  - Path: `packages/core`
  - Role: Shared `inspectFile`, `search`, and `read` contracts; `inspectFile` handler, lifecycle machine, and `FileInspector`
- **`@rat-stack/database`**:
  - Path: `packages/database`
  - Role: Database cartridge: the `RunLog` service and the `DatabaseVendor` choice (D1 or Hyperdrive Postgres), with each vendor's schema, migrations, and resources
- **`@rat-stack/auth`**:
  - Path: `packages/auth`
  - Role: Better Auth cartridge over the chosen `DatabaseVendor`: `Auth`, `CurrentPerson`, and the RPC middleware that provides it; only `Unauthenticated` crosses the wire. `@rat-stack/auth/devtools` adds `runAsPerson`, the dev-only `rat_test_person` capability, and `testPersonLayer`
- **`@rat-stack/flags`**:
  - Path: `packages/flags`
  - Role: Typed flags cartridge: scoped evidence ladders, Config and memory adapters, cartridge-owned Alchemy KV, and a default Durable Object ledger. The DO commits values, receipts, and projection markers together; alarms project to KV. Readers never call the DO. Empty KV uses Config or declared defaults; read failures follow the catalog's `failurePolicy`. `EVENTS_ENABLED` stays deploy-time Config. Core owns declarations and the `flip_feature_flag`, `record_flag_evidence`, and `read_flag_ledger` contracts. Climbs use capability approval; `off` bypasses approval but stays audited. Only the CLI mounts operator capabilities; its default composition has no live ledger. Public readers and the sandbox stay read-only. Replace both exports in `apps/site/src/flags.ts` with `Flags.defaults(eventFlags)` to remove the adapter package.
- **`@rat-stack/events`**:
  - Path: `packages/events`
  - Role: Events cartridge: capture-first request analytics. `withEventCapture` records one `request` event per HTTP request into core's `EventSink` port and owns visitor ids, the visitor salt, identity modes, and query and geography redaction. `src/basin.ts` provides the Basin-backed sink and salt; `src/memory.ts` is the in-memory sink for tests. `@rat-stack/events/site` is the one seam: `apps/site/src/events.ts` is the only file outside the package that imports it, and `rat-stack-boundaries/no-cross-layer-imports` enforces that. Removal is one line in that file plus deleting the package and its `apps/site/package.json` line; `packages/events/README.md` has the steps. Core owns the `EventSink` port (no-op default), the `RawEvent` wire schemas, `@rat-stack/core/events-off`. Tests are property and model based (`it.prop`, `it.effect.prop`). `EVENTS_ENABLED` (default false) turns capture and the catalog, sink, and pipeline on, and reads `EVENTS_SINK_TOKEN` at deploy time only; off still declares the bucket, stream, and salt so their state survives. `EVENTS_IDENTITY_MODE` picks `daily` or `persistent` visitor ids
- **`@rat-stack/turbo-cache`**:
  - Path: `packages/turbo-cache`
  - Role: Thin project declaration of `alchemy-turbo-cache` `0.0.0`, pinned to Git commit `a51a7ba6ea56728f89c4214befe8bf940a946e52`. The external package owns the binary-protocol Worker, lifecycle-expiring R2 bucket, team-scoped generated credentials and read-only state-to-stdin handoff. Its Git `prepare` builds exports during installation, authorized by the package-specific `allowBuilds` entry. Rat-stack supplies prefix `TurboCache`, team `rat-stack`, seven-day retention and prod-only resource retention. The Stack includes it with `yield* turboCache`. The local seam test preserves the exact three resource FQNs and credential handoff; the README records trust limits and removal steps.
- **`@rat-stack/crash`**:
  - Path: `packages/crash`
  - Role: Private crash-trace archive: trace schemas, `captureCrashes`, and the R2 archive layer (`@rat-stack/crash/r2`). Mischief's tail consumer provides it in `apps/site/src/crash-tail.ts`
- **`@rat-stack/subscriber-delivery`**:
  - Path: `packages/subscriber-delivery`
  - Role: External subscriber intake and confirmation adapter; implements core's job-shaped `SubscriberIntake` and `SubscriberConfirm` ports, provided by the Worker, never imported by core
- **`@rat-stack/learn`**:
  - Path: `packages/learn`
  - Role: Source-derived public concept deck and the learning lifecycle. Stateless capabilities return compact progress; `@rat-stack/learn/local` owns the local JSONL adapter and capabilities. The CLI provides the filesystem platform for core's `LearnerProgress` port.
- **`@rat-stack/motion`**:
  - Path: `packages/motion`
  - Role: Motion for Foldkit apps. The `src/*.pure.ts` core (Penner and CSS easings, tweens, fixed-step springs, number, tuple, OKLab colour and 2D transform interpolation) imports nothing, so consumers can vendor it. `@rat-stack/motion/foldkit` adds the Model schemas, the `Motion.Message` union, `advance`, and subscriptions for animation frames and `prefers-reduced-motion`; Foldkit and Effect are optional peers. No Worker graph imports it
- **`@rat-stack/lore`**:
  - Path: `packages/lore`
  - Role: Public content graph and traversal service
- **`@rat-stack/devtools`**:
  - Path: `packages/devtools`
  - Role: 🐀 devtools cartridge: `CallLog`, `record`, and the `rat_*` capabilities that list, read, dispatch, replay, and diff capability calls
- **`@rat-stack/web`**:
  - Path: `apps/web`
  - Role: Default UI bin: Foldkit on Vite, deployed through Alchemy's `Cloudflare.Website.Foldkit` as `Website` (`apps/web/src/website.ts`). Server rendering and prerendering are the default: one `foldkit({ ssr: { serverEntry, clientEntry, build: { prerender } } })` call in `vite.config.ts` builds the client bundle, the server fetch handler, and an HTML file for every path in `src/entry.server.ts`'s `prerenderPaths`. The Website serves those files, sends every other request to the handler, and the browser hydrates. System page: `.brain/areas/web.svx`. Browser `client/` Commands call an Effect `RpcClient` built from the contracts' `toRpcGroup`. The reader program mounts the document browser (`features/app.ts`, `client/docs`) as a Submodel at `/search`, where it calls `search` and `read` over that client. In production, the Worker that `@foldkit/vite-plugin` generates from `src/entry.server.ts` forwards `/rpc` through `src/server/website-bindings.ts` to the private `RpcBackend` in `apps/site/src/rpc-worker.ts`. `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/web dev` loads the `#backend` import, which resolves only under the `development` condition in `apps/web/package.json`, and serves the content capabilities in process from `src/dev/backend.ts`. In dev, `src/dev/backend.ts` runs the content capabilities under devtools: `/rpc` calls are recorded, `/__rat/rpc` serves the 🐀 overlay (`#devtools-overlay`, `src/dev/features/overlay`, ⌘K), and `/__rat/mcp` serves every `rat_*` tool to agents, with memory-Auth test people. `src/dev/client` and `src/dev/features` follow the browser rules. `test/production-bundle.test.ts` proves no `src/dev` module, no devtools code, and no test people reach a production build. Include it in the Stack with `const website = yield* Website;`
- **`@rat-stack/cli`**:
  - Path: `apps/cli`
  - Role: Composition root: `stats`, `catalog`, `openapi`, `serve [--devtools]`, `mcp [--code-mode] [--devtools]` commands. Also builds the published `ratstack` npm package: `src/ratstack.ts` bundles the local learn commands and a learn-only `mcp` into `dist/npm` with Vite. `test/ratstack.e2e.test.ts` proves the package holds no devtools and serves only the learn tools
- **`@rat-stack/infra`**:
  - Path: `apps/infra`
  - Role: Alchemy Stack: the project's cloud footprint as one Effect program
- **`@rat-stack/site`**:
  - Path: `apps/site`
  - Role: Cloudflare Worker: the public site, agent discovery, and sandboxed execute surface
  - Startup fence: `scripts/startup-budget.ts` measures Alchemy's actual upload. Follow static imports from each entry; count shared chunks once and exclude dynamic-only chunks. Hard startup ceilings are shrink-only: Mischief **1,114,000 bytes**, LearnFeedbackAuth **628,000 bytes**, Workshop **870,000 bytes**. Never raise them to accept growth. LearnFeedbackAuth's temporary raise has been retired; `apps/site/STARTUP.md` records the lazy-auth measurements. Entry bytes are evidence only; total JavaScript above **2,500,000 bytes** warns without blocking. Growing page data stays in static assets outside the startup code. Measurement and profiling: `apps/site/STARTUP.md`.

## Nouns

- **Contract**:
  - Home: `packages/core/src/contracts.ts`
  - Runtime job: Shared name, schemas, failure, annotations, and approval setting.
- **Capability**:
  - Home: `packages/core/src/inspect-file.ts` or `apps/site/src/capabilities/<name>.ts`
  - Runtime job: Binds one contract to its server-side handler with `implement`.
- **Projection**:
  - Home: `packages/capability/src/to-<surface>.ts`
  - Runtime job: Expose implemented capabilities on one runtime surface.
- **Cartridge**:
  - Home: `packages/<name>/src/`
  - Runtime job: One Layer with its own infrastructure; it must pass the cartridge test in `VISION.md`.
- **Machine**:
  - Home: `packages/core/src/<name>-machine.ts`
  - Runtime job: Own one finite domain lifecycle.
- **Feature**:
  - Home: `apps/web/src/features/<name>/`
  - Runtime job: Thin route and view that read the Model and send Messages.
- **System page**:
  - Home: `.brain/areas/<name>.svx`
  - Runtime job: Public page at `/systems/<name>` for one system rat-stack ships: what it does, the standard it keeps, and how to check it. The content build rejects a system page without those three sections or outside `.brain/areas/`.
- **Client**:
  - Home: `apps/web/src/client/<name>/`
  - Runtime job: Own the Foldkit program's Model, Messages, update, and named Commands; Commands call an `RpcClient` over the contract group.

## Commands

- **`pnpm install`**: Install workspace dependencies
- **`pnpm sources:fetch`**: Import missing pinned code objects once before the first gate; generation stays local-only
- **`pnpm dev`**: Run `apps/web` under `vite dev` through portless at `http://rat-stack.localhost:1355` (worktrees get their own prefix); `portless list` shows the route
- **`pnpm check`**: Typecheck, verify formatting, and run type-aware linting
- **`pnpm lint`**: Type-aware lint plus format check only; `turbo run check` runs this once at the root as `//#lint`
- **`pnpm fix`**: Apply Oxfmt and safe Oxlint fixes
- **`pnpm test`**: Build and run the Vitest suite once
- **`pnpm build`**: Compile package outputs
- **`pnpm typecheck`**: Strict effect-tsrs checks for workspaces and root scripts
- **`pnpm typecheck:tsc`**: Patched `tsc` for workspaces and root scripts; runs at checker bumps, not in CI
- **`pnpm typecheck:fast`**: Fast feedback in seconds; no Effect diagnostics; `pnpm check` is still the gate
- **`pnpm typecheck:parity`**: Compare effect-tsrs and patched `tsc` errors and exit verdicts, including `TS377xxx`; also compare plain tsrs with Effect-only codes excluded
- **`pnpm bump:checkers`**: Bump both checker pins to npm latest, install without scripts, report bundled revision alignment, and run both parity pairs; never commit or push
- **`pnpm vendor:agent-sources`**: Shallow-clone Effect, effect-solutions, xstate, alchemy, better-auth, and Foldkit mirrors
- **`pnpm infra:plan`**: Preview the Alchemy Stack diff without applying
- **`pnpm infra:deploy` / `pnpm infra:destroy`**: Apply or tear down the Stack (asks for approval)
- **`pnpm exec lefthook install`**: Install git hooks (also via `prepare`)
- **`pnpm turbo run check test build`**: Required validation before claiming a change is ready

Run `pnpm fix` only when you intend to rewrite files. Finish with `pnpm turbo run check test build`.

## Deploy

Follow [ship](/skills/ship) and `skills/ship/references/project.md` for deployment commands, approval, checks, and recovery.

## Release the ratstack package

- `.github/workflows/ratstack-publish.yml` publishes `ratstack` to npm with trusted publishing (OIDC). No npm token exists in the repo or its secrets.
- Bump `apps/cli/npm/ratstack/package.json` and `apps/cli/src/version.ts` together. The e2e test fails when they differ.
- Merge to `main`, then push the tag `ratstack-v<version>` on that merged commit. The workflow refuses a tag that does not match the version or is not on `main`.
- The workflow runs the full gate, then `npm publish` from `apps/cli/dist/npm`. npm adds provenance.
- The npm package settings name this repo, `ratstack-publish.yml`, and the `npm` environment as the trusted publisher. Changing the workflow filename breaks publishing.

## Fence (cheating is uncomfortable)

Why lives in `AGENTS.md` / `VISION.md`. The stack and hooks are the enforceable fence. Fence wins over prose.

- Lefthook pre-commit runs `pnpm check` and `pnpm test`. `check` runs strict effect-tsrs; floating Effects and warning-level Effect diagnostics fail. CI type-checks through `check` only.
- Agents must not use `git … --no-verify` (or equivalent hook bypass)
- Blocked by: Pi `.pi/extensions/git-interceptor`, Cursor `.cursor/hooks.json`, Claude Code `.claude/settings.json`
- Policy source: `scripts/vcs-command-policy.js`

If a hook fails, fix the failure. Do not disable the fence.

## Source-first Effect / XState work

Before writing, reviewing, or refactoring Effect or XState code, read the installed Effect package's `AGENTS.md` first, for example `packages/core/node_modules/effect/AGENTS.md`. It ships with the installed version, so it is never stale. Then inspect vendored source for the pinned versions. Populate mirrors:

```sh
pnpm vendor:agent-sources
# or
./scripts/vendor-agent-sources.sh --refresh
```

Inventory: `.agent_sources/README.md` is generated in the local source mirror and is not part of this repository.

- **Effect Schema, Context.Service, CLI**: `.agent_sources/github.com/Effect-TS/effect/`
- **Idiomatic Effect**: `.agent_sources/github.com/kitlangton/effect-solutions/`
- **XState**: `.agent_sources/github.com/statelyai/xstate/`
- **`@xstate/effect` (v6 Effect bridge)**: `.agent_sources/github.com/statelyai/xstate/packages/xstate-effect/` (`README.md`, `docs/`, `src/*.test.ts`)
- **Alchemy resources, Cloudflare, AWS**: `.agent_sources/github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/` and <https://alchemy.run/llms.txt>

Refs are derived from the workspace pins, so bumping a package and re-running the script keeps them matched. The `pi-effect` tool reads the Effect mirror in place; it needs no link.

Mirrors are reference material, not runtime dependencies. Exclude them from typecheck, test, lint, and format. Do not vendor product-specific corpora in this template.

## Source control

Preserve existing work. Inspect status before editing, stage only files changed for the current task, and do not commit generated output, secrets, or populated `.agent_sources/github.com/` trees. Use the repository's existing source-control tool; do not initialize or migrate one without approval. Never pass `--no-verify` to git.

`.shitrat/public-allow.json` tells the ShitRat public-push guard that `.brain/` is public content here, because the site is built from it. A child project owns that file: narrow or delete it the day its `.brain` holds anything that isn't meant to be public.

## Project law

A child project replaces this section on day one with its own product rules. These rules describe the rat-stack template, not the product in a clone. Keep durable product intent in `VISION.md`.

- One contract, every surface. Define schemas and metadata with `defineContract`; bind a server-side handler with `implement` and add the capability to `capabilities`. CLI, HTTP, MCP, RPC, and code mode are projections in `packages/capability`. Do not add a command, route, or tool handler that bypasses a capability.
- Schemas are the contract. Input, output, and failure are Effect `Schema`; JSON Schema, OpenAPI, and the code-mode declarations are derived from them, never hand-written.
- Lifecycles are machines. Finite modes, retries, and cancellation live in XState machines started with `createEffectActor`; side effects live in declared `createEffectLogic` actors, never inline.
- The sandbox is a surface, not a bypass. Anything reachable from a code-mode program must be a capability and goes through that capability's schemas and handler.
- Gardener rule: add a lint rule before cleaning up a bad pattern; lint baselines only shrink. The routine is `skills/gardener`; before simplifying or replacing a design, run `skills/uncomplect`.
- Refresh peers, versions, and tiers after every bump of Effect, Alchemy, XState, or `@xstate/effect`. On every gardener pass, refresh peers whose checked date is more than 14 days old. Report stale dates; they never block other gardener work. The repo-native `skills/gardener` pass owns the peers refresh through `skills/find-peers`: check default-branch manifests or lockfiles, record exact versions and checked dates in `.brain/data/peers.json`, and explain tiers with evidence. The content build reads our pins from manifests and filters/sorts that dataset into `.brain/resources/peers.svx`; never hand-edit generated entries. Drift is expected. Preserve every peer; show S through B in the main list and C through F in a collapsed Also seen list. Put the rubric and full ranking at the top of the report for feedback after shipping; no separate approval round is required.
- Tautological tests considered harmful.
- Change-detector tests considered harmful.
- Do not create regression tests for bug fixes without a genuine gap in behavior testing.
- Prefer property and model tests over example tests. A domain rule is an `it.prop` over Effect `Arbitrary` inputs; anything with history (sessions, retries, lifecycles) is a model checked over generated command sequences. Keep example tests for seams. Plant a bug before trusting a new property: it must fail. Reference: `packages/events/test/`.
- Errors are part of the interface. Name the failure, keep its source context, say how to fix it, and fail at the boundary. Fence messages (lint rules, content-build violations, startup failures, deploy refusals, the VCS policy) read `<what>. <why>. Fix: <step>`, and the step names a command, file, or replacement in a code span; `packages/core/test/fixtures/fence-message.ts` is the grammar the fence-message tests check. Build-time code references accumulate every independent failure before emitting assets; drift is a warning, never a fallback.
- `packages/code-snippets` owns the build-only excerpt pipeline and ports; `/git` and `/shiki` are adapters. Worker graphs must contain neither code-snippets nor Shiki.
- No comments in code. `no-comments/no-comments` (`scripts/oxlint-plugin-no-comments.ts`) bans them, after Lauren Tan's Dune rule: agents copy comments, and a comment that explains a workaround spreads the workaround. Say it in a name, a type, a test, a commit message, or the Brain. Two kinds survive: tool directives, with the reason inline after `--`, and a one-line `SAFETY:` invariant above a type assertion. TypeScript's `@ts-expect-error`, `@ts-ignore`, and `@ts-nocheck` count as directives here; `typescript/ban-ts-comment` decides which may stay, so write `// @ts-expect-error -- <reason>`. `--fix` deletes prose, so move anything a comment knows into a name, a test, the commit, or the Brain before running it. Plain JS files keep JSDoc blocks made only of type tags (`@param {string} command`), because that is their type syntax; Ultracite's JSDoc description rules are off for the same reason. Credit for borrowed code lives in `PROVENANCE.md`.
- Diagnostic overrides are targeted and explained: `// @effect-diagnostics-next-line <rule>:off -- <reason>`. File-level overrides exist only at projection boundaries (`packages/capability/src/to-toolkit.ts`, `packages/capability/src/to-code-mode.ts`, `packages/capability/src/to-rpc.ts`) and in process-spawning test files.
- Lint overrides follow the same rule: `// oxlint-disable-next-line <rule> -- <reason>`. Every type assertion carries a one-line `SAFETY:` comment naming the invariant it relies on. `unicorn/throw-new-error` is off because `Schema.TaggedError(...)` looks like a throw to it. Anti-slop overrides exist only where a type is erased on purpose (the projections in `packages/capability`, the sandbox RPC boundary, the lint plugin's AST walker); anywhere else, parse the value at its boundary with Effect `Schema`.
- `no-comments/directive-reason` (`scripts/oxlint-plugin-no-comments.ts`) enforces the reason: every `oxlint-disable*` or `eslint-disable*` comment without text after `--` fails lint.
- Hot pink is the only accent. `--accent` (#ff1493) marks borders, rules and focus rings; `--accent-text` (#c8006e, 5.7:1 on white) is the only pink text. Use it for at most one thing per screen, plus focus. News chrome uses no pink. The allowed selectors cover `:focus-visible` and copy controls; links, headings, tables and tier cells never use it. `apps/site/test/accent.test.ts` holds the allowed selectors.
- Pins stay exact. A vendored dependency carries a matching `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entry and a removal rule in `vendor/README.md`.

## Architecture

A child project replaces this section on day one with its own architecture. Record module boundaries, dependency direction, data ownership, and state-machine seams here. Link deeper docs instead of duplicating them.

- `rat-stack-boundaries/no-core-adapters` keeps provider adapters out of core. Core owns job-shaped ports; adapter packages implement them, and apps provide them at composition. `packages/subscriber-delivery` implements subscriber intake and confirmation; `packages/core/test/boundaries-rule.test.ts` checks the boundary.
- `rat-stack-boundaries/no-cross-layer-imports` enforces dependency direction: `apps/cli` → `packages/core` → `packages/capability` → Effect/XState. Packages do not import apps; `packages/capability` does not import domain code; `apps/infra` owns its Stack wiring. `core` owns shared contracts and the `inspectFile` handler; each capability's owner keeps its handler beside its data or infrastructure. Core depends on `capability` for `defineContract` and `implement`.
- `rat-stack-boundaries/no-browser-server-imports` applies to `apps/*/src/features/**` and `apps/*/src/client/**`. Browser modules may import only `@rat-stack/core/contracts` and `@rat-stack/capability/rpc-group` from these packages; they cannot import handler modules. `rat-stack-boundaries/no-feature-transport` applies to `apps/*/src/features/**`.
- `rat-stack-boundaries/no-hand-rolled-surface` keeps `Rpc.make`, `RpcGroup.make`, `HttpApi*`, `Tool.make`, and `Toolkit.make` inside `packages/capability`; everything else projects contracts. `rat-stack-boundaries/no-browser-globals-on-server` keeps `window`, `document`, `navigator`, and web storage in `apps/*/src/client/**` and `apps/*/src/features/**`.
- `rat-stack-patterns` (`scripts/oxlint-plugin-patterns.ts`): `contract-binding-matches-name` (`const searchContract = defineContract("search", …)`), `no-module-level-mutable-state` (module `let`/`var` in `apps/*/src` and `packages/*/src` leaks across Worker requests), and `acquire-release-constructs-in-acquire-body` (build pools inside acquire, not before).
- `packages/core/src/file-inspector.ts` is the reference service shape: a `Context.Service` class whose `make` captures its dependencies so its methods carry no requirements, with `static layer` beside it. `packages/core/src/config-service.ts` derives a service from Effect `Config` (production `layer` reads the ConfigProvider, `configLayer` takes parsed values for tests); `AppConfig` is the instance and mirrors `.env.schema`.
- `packages/core/src/inspect-machine.ts` is the reference shape for a lifecycle: the machine owns states, declared `createEffectLogic` actors own side effects and typed failures, `join` plus `Effect.orDie` hands the outcome back to Effect. `packages/core/src/contracts.ts` owns `inspectFileContract`; `packages/core/src/inspect-file.ts` implements it and registers the capability.
- Effect-backed machines start only under `createEffectActor`, never `createActor`. Only actions and actors declared in `setupEffect` contribute to the actor's requirements; the `xstate-effect/no-inline-effect` lint rule enforces the inline cases.
- `packages/capability/src`: `contract.ts` defines shared contracts; `implement.ts` binds typed handlers and adds approval requirements; `to-command.ts`, `to-http-api.ts`, `to-toolkit.ts`, `to-rpc.ts`, and `to-code-mode.ts` project implemented capabilities. `to-rpc-group.ts` builds the contract-only client group; `to-rpc.ts` derives the server group from those same contracts. `catalog.ts`, `sandbox-service.ts`, and `sandbox-subprocess.ts` support code mode. `to-code-mode.ts` imports from `to-toolkit.ts`, so MCP is a prerequisite for code mode.
- Devtools are capabilities: `devtools(capabilities)` adds the `rat_*` capabilities, and a dev composition provides the recording layer from `devtoolsLayer()` through `CallWatch` (`@rat-stack/capability/call-watch`). `implement` reads that ambient reference once per call and surrounds the approval-gated handler, so denied calls are recorded too; the default is a no-op. `CallWatch` observes calls across projections without changing their capability lists. `aroundHandlers` stays as the explicit wrapper over one capability list: drovr uses it for `writeGate` to serialize and audit approval-gated writes. Both compose because `implement` reads `CallWatch` inside the handler that `aroundHandlers` wraps; the gate runs outside the recorder. `rat_call` dispatches through `invokerFor`, the same path code mode uses. Machines report through `watchActor` (`@rat-stack/capability/actor-watch`), a no-op `ActorWatch` reference that the recorder overrides; `rat-stack-patterns/watch-effect-actors` requires the call. `devtools(capabilities, { runAs })` records each call's identity and lets `rat_call` take `as`; the composition root passes `runAsPerson` from `@rat-stack/auth/devtools`, so devtools never imports auth. `rat-stack-boundaries/no-devtools-in-production` keeps `@rat-stack/devtools` and `@rat-stack/auth/devtools` in `apps/*/src/dev/**`, `apps/cli`, and tests, and keeps everything outside an app's `dev/` folder from importing it, so a deployed entry cannot reach `rat_call` or test people. `--devtools` binds `127.0.0.1` only. Plan and tool list: `.brain/archives/projects/rat-devtools.svx`.
- `apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts` and `apps/cli/src/learn-surfaces.ts` are the only places projections are instantiated; `learn-surfaces.ts` stays devtools-free because the published `ratstack` bin imports it. `apps/cli/src/command.ts` maps them to subcommands; `apps/cli/src/cli.ts` is the composition root that provides `FileInspector` and `NodeServices`, and `apps/cli/src/ratstack.ts` is the composition root for the `ratstack` bin. Both share `learn-layer.ts`.
- The [README's Keep or cut section](/README.md#keep-or-cut) lists what to delete per surface.

## Wiki writing

Follow [write-a-wiki-page](/skills/write-a-wiki-page) for prose, visuals, code excerpts, and content-build diagnostics.

## Web feature blueprint

`apps/web/src/features/<name>/` holds a thin route and view. It reads the Model and sends Messages; components never handle transport, retries, or process startup. `apps/web/src/client/<name>/` owns the Foldkit program: Model, Messages, `update`, and named `Command.define` definitions. Remote state lives in the Model, as Foldkit `AsyncData` or a `foldkit/experimental` `Query`. The capability in `packages/core` is the shared typed edge, imported by both sides. A cartridge owns durable behavior.

One send follows one path: feature → Message → `update` → named Command → `RpcClient` over the contract's `toRpcGroup` → shared capability → server-side Durable Object or database cartridge. The server stays authoritative. The Command returns a result Message, and `update` folds it into the Model.

## Worker autonomy ladder

A worker acts at the lowest rung that applies. Climb only when the rung below does not cover the step.

- **0 — Do it**: Fix your own red CI, failing hook, or stale git snapshot. Arm a wait watch. Read, edit, and test inside your write scope.
- **1 — Do it and report**: Commit on your branch. Tighten a test. Edit docs or the Brain. Report what changed and which checks ran.
- **2 — Ask the desk or owner**: A choice that changes scope, a guarantee, or the design, where the repo does not decide.
- **3 — Owner sign-off**: Everything in "Needs owner sign-off" below.
- **Never — Do not do this**: `--no-verify` or any hook bypass. Merging or deploying as a worker. Force-pushing. Secrets or customer data in a PR.

At rung 2 or 3, ask one question with a recommendation. Keep doing independent work while you wait. Red CI is work, not a question: reproduce it, fix it, and push.

Never end a turn "waiting" without a wake. Procedure: `skills/rat-stack-mode/principles/own-your-wait.md`.

## Boundaries and sign-off

A child project replaces this section on day one with its own boundaries. This section names changes agents may make directly and changes that need owner approval.

- Safe by default: adding a capability in `packages/core` and wiring it into `capabilities`; new or tightened tests; a targeted diagnostic override with a written reason; README, AGENTS.md, and `.brain/` edits; tightening a lint rule; removing a surface by following Keep or cut; any change under `apps/infra`, and `pnpm infra:deploy` once `pnpm infra:plan` shows only the intended diff and the gate passes, followed by `pnpm site:smoke`.
- Needs owner sign-off: adding or changing a dependency version (pins are exact and CI installs cold); any edit to `oxlint.config.ts`, the diagnostics map in `tsconfig.base.json`, `lefthook.yml`, or `scripts/vcs-command-policy.js` that loosens the fence; `pnpm infra:destroy`, and a deploy whose plan replaces or deletes a resource; widening sandbox permissions or adding a runtime that reaches the network; exposing `serve` or `mcp` beyond localhost; vendoring a package as a `file:` tarball; deleting `.agent_sources/` or `vendor/`.

# /VISION.md

Source: VISION.md
SHA-256: 6de758c187e818a9dfe5d861a9e97e3d18cb280ba21631ec1a095fcd9570db50

# Vision

rat-stack is the reference for how we build: an app and its cloud as one typed program. Effect owns the hard parts, Alchemy infers the infrastructure from the code, and the fence raises the floor, so an agent can build it reliably with high-trust.

*An Effect stack so pure (aspirational) Kit Langton will blush.*

The goal is to **build the best Effect + Alchemy application that we can**, as close to a perfect Effect application as we can get. Every change here moves toward that, and projects that grow out of rat-stack move toward it too. In practice:

- New code takes the rat-stack path: a shared contract, a job-shaped service port, a provider adapter outside core, and an outcome you can observe. Ports name the application's jobs; Layers supply the adapters. The fence keeps core free of HTTP-client and vendor implementations.
- Existing code is finished that way when someone touches it, and the old version is deleted.
- Debt only shrinks. Plain async code moves onto Effect, and lint exemptions get retired, never added.
- The fence (lint, types, the Effect language service, CI) makes the easy path the right one.
- Where a platform behaves differently from a test fake, test against the real thing. [Worker init runs twice](https://ratstack.sh/lore/init-runs-twice) is what happens when you don't.

We and our agents use it to understand what we are building. Real projects take it in the way they take a library: vendor it, keep the bins they need, and pull the rest.

It is also the working code behind a YouTube series by [Joel Hooks](https://www.youtube.com/@JoelHooks) on Alchemy and Effect. Every claim made on camera points at something that runs here. The series arc lives with the content research. `ratstack.sh` is the teaching surface.

**Public GitHub is a steal-the-ideas surface, not a supported product**.

Any project that grows out of rat-stack writes its own vision.

Scope: `joelhooks/rat-stack`, the reference repo, and the shape a project inherits when it vendors or clones it.

Audience: The agents that work from this reference, engineers who work through agents and want to trust what an agent built, and people watching the series who want the working code. This is not a support queue, compatibility promise, ghostwriting service, growth automation, thin npm init, or TypeScript tutorial dressed up as a template excited to go out on a Saturday night.

Status: `ratstack.sh` is deployed. Effect 4 is stable. XState, `@xstate/effect`, and Alchemy are pinned to betas, so their APIs can drift.

Some of it's still fuckin' pre-release. It's fine. Keep track 🙏

## Why it exists

Agents will take the shortest path. Lazy mfers.

A skeleton without commandments chiseled in stone produces a ball of mud. A pile of prose without a strong fence is legacy documentation.

This reference gives a project:

1. Why. `VISION.md` and `AGENTS.md` explain the point.
2. Fence. Pins, `pnpm check`, lefthook, and harness hooks block hook bypass.
3. Context. Vendored Effect, effect-solutions, XState, and Alchemy sources support source-first edits.

The stack is the fundamental floor. The foundation. [Sam Goodwin's argument](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MtKHzAH6uXM\&t=1790s) sets the bar: the whole cloud becomes a library, limited by the accounts you have, and the type system should guarantee that the infrastructure is correct.

## Pieces, trust, floor, and range

Four ideas hold this together.

**Pieces.** Alchemy Layers as literally composable SaaS (next section). Each one is a product you can provide, swap, or pull out.

**Trust.** [Lauren Tan ships thousands of agent-written PRs](https://x.com/poteto/status/2102050467505430555) because she trusts the environment her agents work in. She ranks five places a correction can live, hardest first: the codebase, static analysis (lint, compiler, CI), rules, skills, and the style guide. The hard rungs make a bad pattern impossible to write. Her team built Dune, an agent-friendly framework, on one principle: agents love taking shortcuts, so "what if we designed a framework such that the shortcut, the easy path, is the right path for agents?" Dune enforces process boundaries through the import graph and keeps a single paved path for each blessed pattern. Her point is that the framework itself matters less than owning one. rat-stack is ours. Alchemy puts infrastructure on the compiler rung: remove a binding and the code that uses it stops compiling. rat-stack's fence is the rest of the ladder, built in.

**Floor.** [Theo Browne](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iBrAWpjXNxs\&t=349s): "raising the floor is way more beneficial than raising the ceiling." [He gave the same advice about videos](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9GCu3hiNjw\&t=707s) on Joel's channel: "raise the baseline so that you average higher... the floor is the hardest part to get right." A higher floor also makes failure cheaper: "it'll also make it hurt less when the video you put a lot of effort into bombs." The floor is the worst thing that happens on a normal run. His math is about long runs. A step that fails 5% of the time every ten minutes fails about 70% of the time over four hours. Cut that 5% to 3% and the four-hour failure rate drops to about 50%. Small cuts to the failure rate multiply how long the work can run. [At CascadiaJS](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TV6f2weVgCI\&t=135s) he also said failure got cheap: "experimentation is now significantly cheaper... it costs pennies." Theo applies the floor to models. We apply it to the environment. Types, the fence, and cartridges that pull out cleanly raise the floor for every agent working here. That floor is what makes long-running agent loops worth leaving unattended.

**Range.** At [CascadiaJS 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TV6f2weVgCI) Theo closed with "build bigger." A month later [he refined it](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xUnRQ9vLXxo\&t=798s): "bigger is probably the wrong word... It's time to think wider." He means range, how much ground your software covers. A team could never match AWS's range without thousands of engineers. Now "you can build a database platform into your product in a day or two." He also says to architect products so users can build the features you are missing. And in his words, "wider prompting requires higher floors." He names the bottleneck too: "building is now like a thirty minute process... but the deploying hasn't went down at all." Composable Layers that carry their own infrastructure are our answer to that gap. The compiler checks resource requirements; plans and real-infrastructure checks prove the deployed behavior.

Theo's case for ambition is to prompt further. Lauren's method is to build the environment. We take the ambition from him and the method from her.

## Layers are composable SaaS

With Alchemy, an Effect Layer can declare the cloud resources it needs. Providing the Layer provisions them on the next deploy. Sam calls this "SaaS as NPM." We build on it:

- A service tag is the product's API.
- A Layer is one vendor's implementation, and it carries its own infrastructure.
- `Layer.provide` is that vendor's private supply chain. Swapping vendors is a one-line change.
- Typed errors are the SLA, written in the type.

Alchemy spans providers. One stack can run Cloudflare next to PlanetScale, and that range is part of the point.

## The house rule: a clean playground

The house rule is a clean, organized playground where real work gets done. It sets no limit on size. Picture clear, labeled bins on shelves that push in and pull out like game cartridges. Anything good can go in if it passes the cartridge test:

- **Labeled.** One package, one job, named for that job.
- **Push in.** Adding it takes one package plus one `Layer.provide` or Stack line.
- **Pull out.** Removing it takes deleting that package and that line, and `pnpm turbo run check test build` still passes.
- **Self-contained.** It declares its own resources and bindings. Nothing spills into other bins.
- **EZ to trash.** It can be tossed in the garbage without affecting anything else.

Everything built here is real.

## Outcomes

- Agent-facing pages give the agent useful next actions, not only information. Markdown can carry AgentOnly guidance that HTML leaves out. Capability and MCP next-action links are a direction to prove, not something the projections guarantee today.
- A project that vendors or clones rat-stack starts with a pnpm and Turborepo workspace, a real Effect CLI, and a trust fence.
- Agents hit a loud failure when they cheat, including `git … --no-verify` and skipped checks. Consider adding hooks to your harness to stop them cold.
- Prose explains the why. CI, lefthook, and agent hooks enforce the fence.
- Someone can ask an agent for an Effect-shaped, Alchemy-shaped solution and catch it when the agent gets it wrong.
- Product-specific corpora, tokens, and customer data stay out of the shared reference.
- Workers act at the lowest rung of the autonomy ladder in `AGENTS.md` that applies. Fixing red CI, a failing hook, or a stale snapshot is their work, so owners see decisions, not chores. A worker that must wait arms a wake on the event it needs and does not stall silently.

## Current priorities

1. Electrify the trust fence. Fuckin agent cheaters stay uncomfortable and obvious. They will feel shame and we will thwart them.
2. Hold advocacy and judgment together. Teach the judgment and let Alchemy win on merit.
3. Prove the claims in code, cheapest first:
   1. Importing `apps/infra/alchemy.run.ts` deploys nothing, and removing a binding is a type error.
   2. A database service tag with two vendor Layers, Cloudflare D1 and Hyperdrive in front of PlanetScale Postgres, with Drizzle inside each vendor. D1 is the free bin. PlanetScale has no free tier, and its cheapest database is single-node Postgres. The tag sits above Drizzle, so swapping vendors stays one line.
4. Prove behavior against real infrastructure where local fakes differ. The database suite currently uses local SQLite and PGlite; per-PR deployed-resource tests remain a goal, not existing coverage.
5. Keep the teaching surface aligned with the running application. `/systems` records what each shipped system does, the standard it keeps, and how to check it. Request analytics runs with a server-set persistent `rat_vid` cookie; event bodies exclude request bodies and sensitive query keys.
6. Prove the signup lifecycle through an external list provider behind job-shaped ports. Submission starts double opt-in; a person confirms their email before joining. Agents apply through `joinInterest` over MCP, HTTP, or the CLI with a single-use page ticket and the person's approval of the exact card; confirmation is still required.
7. Coming: extract the existing agent front door in `apps/site` (REST, MCP, A2A, code-mode sandbox, rate limits) into a cartridge that a project provides instead of inherits.

## Questions this repo answers in code

- Does the type system protect infrastructure correctness? Removing a binding should make typecheck fail. Not yet proven in this repo.
- Does importing `apps/infra/alchemy.run.ts` stay pure? It should deploy nothing. Not yet proven by a test.
- Can a vendor be swapped by changing one line? `packages/database` has one `DatabaseVendor` with D1 and Hyperdrive Postgres Layers, both tested. No test swaps them yet.
- Where does a correction to an agent live? Lauren Tan's fence ladder puts code first, then lint and CI, then rules and skills, with the style guide last. The `--no-verify` rung is proven today by `packages/core/test/vcs-command-policy.test.ts`.
- Can provider details stay outside core? Subscriber delivery lives in `packages/subscriber-delivery`; `no-core-adapters` and its fixture tests enforce the boundary.
- Can the agent discover its next useful action from a response? Agent-only page guidance is built; next-action links in capability and MCP results still need proof.
- Can agent-only signup stay double opt-in? Yes, so far: agents submit an approved application, and a person confirms their email through an email link in a browser. On 2026-10-01 a live `joinInterest` run sent one confirmation email, refused a reused ticket, and sent no second email for a repeat.

## Open questions

- Does `ratstack.sh` stay in this repo? For now it does: the [lore wiki](https://ratstack.sh/lore/) explains the ideas from `.brain/resources/lore/`; [systems](https://ratstack.sh/systems) documents shipped behavior from `.brain/areas/`. Both cite public sources and code.

## Merge by default

- Tests and checks that encode the existing fence
- Docs that sharpen why and fence without adding a second product promise
- Cartridges that pass the cartridge test and are real
- Pin bumps that stay exact and reviewed as stack changes

## Needs sign-off

- Weakening lefthook, CI, or `--no-verify` blocks
- Replacing pnpm, Turborepo, Effect, or XState as the default floor
- Adding product-specific vendor corpora to the shared reference
- Turning the public repo into a supported starter product
- Resource destruction, replacement, or deletion, and deploys whose plans include them. `AGENTS.md` owns the full approval rules for infrastructure changes and deploys.

## Will not do for now

- Support SLAs or a promise that it works on every agent harness
- Vendoring x-algorithm or other app-specific source
- Generating publishable copy as part of the reference
- Toy examples that exist only to demonstrate a pattern
- Bun or npm as the install story
- A gut-me-on-day-one scaffold with no fence

## Decision boundaries

- Safe by default: changes that keep the why in VISION and AGENTS, the fence enforceable, and every bin removable
- Needs owner sign-off: new promises, toolchain swaps, or making the fence optional
- Evidence expected: `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` green, plus hook policy tests that still block `git commit --no-verify`

## Amendment policy

This document changes when the thesis is wrong, not when a downstream project's product is different. Agents may propose amendments with receipts. Joel approves. A project that grows out of rat-stack writes its own `VISION.md` instead of stretching this one.
