## Patterns

### Browser RPC behind a private Worker binding — adopt

**Source:** [Alchemy example README](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/README.md), [RPC schema](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/src/backend/rpc.ts), [browser client](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/src/rpc-client.ts), [proxy route](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/src/routes/rpc.ts), [Stack](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/alchemy.run.ts).

One `RpcGroup` declares the wire contract; the backend serves it and `AtomRpc.Service` turns it into module-scope query and mutation atoms for React. The browser calls a same-origin TanStack `/rpc` route, which forwards to a private `BACKEND` service binding; the backend has no public Workers URL.

Adopt this for the web bin. Keep capability schemas in `packages/core`, the `toRpc` projection in `packages/capability`, and UI atoms in the web app.
One schema-derived contract carries payloads and typed failures across the wire. The [binding](/lore/bindings) keeps the backend private.
All browser operations go through `toRpc` and the same `/rpc` transport. Keep hand-written domain routes out.

### PlanetScale resources and migrations — adapt

**Source:** [T3Code relay database](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/f5ef0ddb90a8c36584e181b1913e7b8a5df30ffc/infra/relay/src/db.ts) at `f5ef0ddb90a8c36584e181b1913e7b8a5df30ffc` (Effect rc.115, Alchemy beta.79).

T3Code makes `Drizzle.Schema` the migration source, then provisions a PlanetScale database or stage branch, a runtime role, and a Hyperdrive connection from that role's origin. Production retains the shared database; non-production stages use branches. This is the closest inspected resource graph to rat-stack's planned PlanetScale Postgres Layer.

Adapt this for the database cartridge. The vendor Layer should own its schema, migration path, role, and [Hyperdrive binding](/lore/bindings).
Use Alchemy Outputs and typed bindings for connection strings. Keep provider-specific Drizzle details behind the database service tag.
Choose D1 or PlanetScale once with `Layer.provide`. Keep T3Code's stage-mode branch out of domain code.

### Effect-native Drizzle and local Postgres tests — adapt

**Source:** Maple's [`packages/db/src/client.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/packages/db/src/client.ts), [`pglite.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/packages/db/src/pglite.ts), and [`migrate.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/packages/db/src/migrate.ts) at `e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373` (Effect rc.116, Alchemy beta.79).

Maple builds Drizzle over `@effect/sql-pg`, opens the client inside an Effect `Scope`, and uses PGlite plus the same bundled migrations for local and test paths. Its exported `MapleDb` remains Postgres-specific. Use the driver implementation and test technique behind a provider-neutral database contract.

Adapt this for the [database cartridge](/lore/cartridges). Keep the public repository-shaped database service small and let each vendor Layer implement it.
Scope clients to one invocation. Use a real embedded database for migrations and query tests. Keep Drizzle's driver type behind the cross-provider API.
Share migration fixtures and the service contract. D1 and Postgres keep their own schemas and implementations.

### Better Auth's database seam — adopt

**Source:** Alchemy's [`Database.ts`](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/packages/better-auth/src/Database.ts), [`CloudflareD1.ts`](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/packages/better-auth/src/CloudflareD1.ts), [`CloudflareHyperdrive.ts`](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/packages/better-auth/src/CloudflareHyperdrive.ts), [`BetterAuth.ts`](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/packages/better-auth/src/BetterAuth.ts), and [example Worker](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-better-auth/src/worker.ts).

`@alchemy.run/better-auth@2.0.0-beta.79` makes `Database` a service supplied by provider-specific Layers, and `BetterAuth` consumes that service. D1 uses a runtime Worker binding and a separate deploy-time migration connection; Hyperdrive accepts the origin URL for migrations because its runtime connection is minted per invocation, and the integration scopes auth/database work to that execution.

Adopt the official Better Auth integration. It is a separately published Alchemy package with provider subpaths, so rat-stack can use it without forking an adapter.
Its API and migration failures are typed. Database clients are scoped, and the caller supplies one database Layer.
Use one `BetterAuth` service with the database cartridge's selected Layer. Keep runtime D1/Postgres switching out of auth code.

### Runtime database-provider switching — reject

**Source:** OpenSEO's [`auth.ts`](https://github.com/every-app/open-seo/blob/0ffff93101043aad7600a3b6a499a0cd2887ef49/src/lib/auth.ts), [`provider.ts`](https://github.com/every-app/open-seo/blob/0ffff93101043aad7600a3b6a499a0cd2887ef49/src/db/provider.ts), [`pg/client.ts`](https://github.com/every-app/open-seo/blob/0ffff93101043aad7600a3b6a499a0cd2887ef49/src/db/pg/client.ts), and [`alchemy.run.ts`](https://github.com/every-app/open-seo/blob/0ffff93101043aad7600a3b6a499a0cd2887ef49/alchemy.run.ts) at `0ffff93101043aad7600a3b6a499a0cd2887ef49` (Effect beta.93, Alchemy beta.61).

OpenSEO constructs Better Auth directly and selects either a D1 Drizzle adapter or a Postgres adapter by reading `DATABASE_PROVIDER` at runtime. Its Postgres client is created inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` request scope and reaches the database through Hyperdrive, but the auth and schema code still branch on provider.

Reject the selector and retain the request-scope invariant. The branch ties auth to both database implementations; either database Layer should plug into one contract.
An environment string chooses the driver at runtime, outside the `Schema`/Layer boundary.
Keep the per-request Hyperdrive lifetime. Move provider choice to one `Layer.provide` at composition.

### Fast Worker and Durable Object tests — adopt

**Source:** Maple's [`worker-bridge.test.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/apps/api/src/worker-bridge.test.ts), [`ChatSessionObject.test.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/apps/ai/src/chat/ChatSessionObject.test.ts), and [`fake-do-state.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/apps/ai/test/chat/fake-do-state.ts), same Maple commit as above.

The bridge test invokes Alchemy's `Cloudflare.Workers.makeRequestHandler` and checks the request scope, Worker environment, and response. Durable Object tests give the class a narrow fake state backed by real `node:sqlite`, including SQL storage, alarms, and `waitUntil`; they exercise object behavior without pretending to be a full `workerd` runtime.

Adopt this for fast tests alongside real-runtime tests. Keep fixtures beside the Worker or database cartridge that owns them.
Real SQL catches query and storage drift. The narrow fake fails when tests ask for an unsupported state operation.
Use the Alchemy bridge for deterministic Worker tests. Keep a separate integration test for real service bindings and deployed behavior.

### D1 fixture backed by SQLite — adapt

**Source:** Smithers' [`worker/test/d1.ts`](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/blob/38846c64dd322d61e67efafadac1fbd9d34df64f/packages/smithers/build/infra/worker/test/d1.ts) and [`action-cache.test.ts`](https://github.com/smithersai/smithers/blob/38846c64dd322d61e67efafadac1fbd9d34df64f/packages/smithers/build/infra/worker/test/action-cache.test.ts) at `38846c64dd322d61e67efafadac1fbd9d34df64f` (Effect rc.115, Alchemy beta.76).

The test adapter runs shipped SQL migrations against `node:sqlite`, implements only the D1 calls the code uses, and throws on every unsupported method. That makes it a useful D1 unit-test boundary, but it does not prove Cloudflare's D1 binding or runtime behavior.

Adapt this for D1 cartridge tests. Expose a test Layer or helper from the D1 package. Keep it local to D1 rather than creating a repo-wide mock database.
Unsupported calls fail loudly. Use this for local SQL behavior and the Alchemy integration gate for binding behavior.

### Deployed Alchemy integration tests — adopt as a separate gate

**Source:** Alchemy's [`test/integ.test.ts`](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176/examples/cloudflare-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/test/integ.test.ts) at `9802260db8f8b5a083c4b85eb7ea31ae1ff8f176`.

The example's `alchemy/Test/Bun` harness deploys the Stack before tests, retries readiness, sends CRUD calls through the `/rpc` proxy into the database, verifies a tagged failure crosses the wire, and destroys the Stack afterward. This is the closest inspected example of the real-resource integration path called for in `VISION.md`, but its Bun runner is not a fit for rat-stack's pnpm test stack.

Adapt this as a separate credentialed integration gate. Keep fast unit tests uncredentialed.
The integration suite belongs to the Stack and can be removed with it. It proves the full binding, wire, and database path.
Port the deploy/test/destroy lifecycle into a pnpm-compatible harness. Keep `alchemy/Test/Bun` out.

### Boundary tests and agent guidance — adapt

**Source:** Maple's [`vendor-isolation.test.ts`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/packages/chat-platform/src/vendor-isolation.test.ts) and [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/e7bc2d97bea87c99c8b9b33f377956e923d04373/CLAUDE.md), same Maple commit.

The test scans explicitly named generic roots and files to keep chat-vendor names inside connector directories, and checks that guarded roots are non-empty and guarded files still exist. The guidance makes app, product-package, and vendor-neutral-library ownership explicit; it also says services capture implementation dependencies and keep request context invocation-scoped.

Adapt the proof. Maple's lexical vendor-name scanner is product-specific; rat-stack needs checks for its own package ownership and adapter isolation.
Encode the capability-only surface rule in a test or type-aware lint rule. Check that guarded paths exist and contain files.
Extend the current capability fence rather than adding a second generic source-scanning framework.

### Scoped actor inspection and generated model commands — adapt

**Source:** beep-effect at `a7644af785843bb42546109272970f2f7a82b1d7`: [catalog](https://github.com/beep-effect/beep-effect/blob/a7644af785843bb42546109272970f2f7a82b1d7/package.json), [driver manifest](https://github.com/beep-effect/beep-effect/blob/a7644af785843bb42546109272970f2f7a82b1d7/packages/drivers/xstate/package.json), [inspector service](https://github.com/beep-effect/beep-effect/blob/a7644af785843bb42546109272970f2f7a82b1d7/packages/drivers/xstate/src/StatelyInspector.service.ts), [test bridge](https://github.com/beep-effect/beep-effect/blob/a7644af785843bb42546109272970f2f7a82b1d7/packages/drivers/xstate/src/test.ts).

Checked Oct 2. Its catalog selects XState alpha.63 and bridge alpha.5. Effect comes from a pkg.pr.new build at `b5a2d4c1d62c9620a68d72b7f20248c69ef7663b`. That [source manifest](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/b5a2d4c1d62c9620a68d72b7f20248c69ef7663b/packages/effect/package.json) declares 4.0.0; the installed build's semver was not verified. It shares a stack line; an exact release match remains unverified.

The inspector has a disabled production Layer. Its enabled Layer owns the inspector, and `attach` acquires an actor subscription whose finalizer unsubscribes. The test bridge derives event arbitraries from schemas and projects a snapshot's value and context for model comparisons. Its actor SUT opens a scope and closes it on disposal.

Adapt the lifetime checks. Keep `watchActor` and `ActorWatch` in [devtools](/systems/devtools) as our single inspection path. A second Stately service would bypass that fence. The helper runs tests through `ManagedRuntime`, which our test fence forbids. Use `it.effect.prop` and generated command sequences instead of copying its runtime bridge. No production code was adopted.

### Verify Foldkit's exact Effect peers: adopt

**Source:** Hazel at `2504baa1ab85d7966152a615a08dc0d4af4c1f69`: [catalogs](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/hazel/blob/2504baa1ab85d7966152a615a08dc0d4af4c1f69/package.json), [Foldkit client](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/hazel/blob/2504baa1ab85d7966152a615a08dc0d4af4c1f69/apps/web-foldkit/package.json), [lockfile](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/hazel/blob/2504baa1ab85d7966152a615a08dc0d4af4c1f69/bun.lock).

The upstream manifests at `49dc36ef672d1caee23f153f88c09d98c8241670` confirm the boundary: [Foldkit](https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/blob/49dc36ef672d1caee23f153f88c09d98c8241670/packages/foldkit/package.json) and [Vite plugin](https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/blob/49dc36ef672d1caee23f153f88c09d98c8241670/packages/vite-plugin-foldkit/package.json).

Checked Oct 9. Does the shared catalog satisfy Foldkit's exact Effect peers?

- The catalog selects Effect 4.0.1 and Alchemy beta.80.
- The client selects Foldkit 0.167.0 and uses that Effect catalog.
- The lockfile records Foldkit's exact Effect 4.0.0 peer.
- The Vite plugin also requires Effect 4.0.0 and depends on platform-node 4.0.0.

Adopt the manifest and lockfile check. Keep Effect 4.0.0 until Foldkit publishes compatible peers and platform dependencies.
Do not copy the newer Effect catalog. This study changes no runtime adapter or UI code.

### Template lifetime boundaries: adopt

**Source:** [architecture](https://github.com/just-be-dev/effect-cloudflare-foldkit-template/blob/04851db8649501bfaf8d2712429074ba0290a10f/docs/architecture.md) and [manifest](https://github.com/just-be-dev/effect-cloudflare-foldkit-template/blob/04851db8649501bfaf8d2712429074ba0290a10f/package.json) at `04851db8649501bfaf8d2712429074ba0290a10f`.

The source assigns each resource to an application, request, tenant, session, or execution. It acquires request capabilities at the request boundary.
rat-stack already adapts this guidance in [cache completed values](/lore/cache-completed-values), UI tests, and opt-in tracing. `PROVENANCE.md` records the source and license confirmation.

Keep those lifetime boundaries. The template uses Effect 4.0.0 and Alchemy beta.81, with Foldkit 0.165.0. Its package-manager defaults do not replace pnpm here.
This refresh records the existing adoption. It copies no new implementation.

## Weekly peers Oct 27

The refresh checks default-branch commits on October 27. No implementation is adopted.
DeepWiki is unavailable in this session. The three questions below use commit-pinned source directly.

### Session publication: keep the existing boundary

Question: How does `omp-agent-mesh` distinguish local work from publication failure?

Its [session machine](https://github.com/masrurimz/omp-agent-mesh/blob/9729284b8cc62b6d397da349d332ae5f993d3cbe/src/lifecycle/session-machine.ts) declares `announce`, `publishStatus`, and `depart` actors.
The idle and working states each contain publication states. Publication failure enters `unsynced` and retains the typed failure.
Its manifest pins Effect 4.0.6, XState alpha.70, and bridge alpha.9.

Keep this as a current bridge reference. Do not copy a second publication model into rat-stack without a matching domain need.

### Local preparation: keep the existing actor seam

Question: How does `durable-pi` separate local cancellation from durable execution?

Its [preparation reference](https://github.com/cill-i-am/durable-pi/blob/b426e6928b5d7fecf787d8e4eac9a9bfaa85e7f3/tests/lifecycle/preparation.machine.ts) invokes a declared Effect actor.
The machine owns cancellation and deadline transitions. The [architecture decision](https://github.com/cill-i-am/durable-pi/blob/b426e6928b5d7fecf787d8e4eac9a9bfaa85e7f3/docs/decisions/xstate-effect-state-machines.md) separates local scope cleanup from remote cancellation confirmation.
Its manifest pins Effect 4.0.5, XState alpha.68, and bridge alpha.8.

Keep the local lifetime example as a study reference. Do not infer durable execution guarantees from the local actor.
No durable adapter is copied.

### Worker reconciliation: reject direct reuse on the older bridge

Question: Where does `ceirean` handle uncertain worker outcomes?

Its [worker lifecycle](https://github.com/opsydyn/ceirean/blob/9a83e0c498589c10f8577efc07abdb10d0a19f3a/packages/engine/src/worker-lifecycle.ts) separates readiness, execution authorization, and reconciliation states.
Mutation failures can route to reconciliation. Its manifest pins Effect 4.0.5, XState alpha.64, and bridge alpha.6.

Keep the state separation as a reference. Direct reuse requires a bridge migration and behavior checks.
No worker implementation is copied.

## Recommendations from the September study

These recommendations record the original study. The current web bin uses Foldkit; [current pins](/pins.md) come from manifests.

1. TanStack web bin: generate the browser client from capability Schemas as one `RpcGroup`, create module-scope `AtomRpc` atoms, and forward same-origin `/rpc` to a private `RpcWorker` binding.
2. Better Auth: use `@alchemy.run/better-auth@2.0.0-beta.79`; provide the database cartridge's Layer and keep auth API/migration failures typed.
3. Database cartridge: expose one repository-shaped service tag; let D1 and PlanetScale/Hyperdrive Layers own schemas, migrations, and bindings; choose with one `Layer.provide`.
4. Worker tests: add `makeRequestHandler` and SQLite-backed DO/D1 fixtures for fast tests, plus one credentialed Alchemy deploy/test/destroy gate using a pnpm-compatible harness.
5. Capability fence: test or lint that every surface, including `toRpc`, originates from the capability registry; make the test prove its guarded paths exist and contain files.

# /lore/a-browser-send-follows-one-path

Source: .brain/resources/lore/a-browser-send-follows-one-path.svx
SHA-256: 2691b7d1491f1c8122c26d485212e353ef938bb96d6ba3fbeaa2658a41398ad1

# A browser send follows one path to the capability

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

**Goal:** trace one user action from a click to the server and back, and know which file owns each step.

Foldkit is the browser UI framework in rat-stack. A Foldkit program keeps its state in a Model. Events arrive as Messages.

An `update` function takes the Model and a Message, and returns a new Model plus any Commands. A Command is a named task that runs outside `update` and ends by sending another Message.

The docs browser at `/search` is the worked example. Its search box calls the [search capability](/lore/one-capability-every-surface).

## 1. The view sends a Message

The Search button sends `SubmittedSearch`. The view does no fetching.

apps/web/src/features/app.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 224-229; highlighted 226. Title: A click is a Message.

```typescript
          Button.view(
            {
              onClick: Message.SubmittedSearch(),
              toView: ({ button }) => h.button(button, ["Search"]),
              type: "button",
            },
```

Every Message the program accepts is declared in one union:

apps/web/src/client/docs/message.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 7-22; highlighted 17-18,20. Title: SubmittedSearch, SucceededSearch, FailedSearch.

```typescript
export const Message = defineMessageUnion({
  ChangedUrl: { url: Url },
  ClickedLink: { request: UrlRequest },
  CompletedLoadExternal: {},
  CompletedNavigate: {},
  FailedRead: {
    generation: Schema.Finite,
    message: Schema.String,
    notFound: Schema.Boolean,
  },
  FailedSearch: { generation: Schema.Finite },
  SubmittedSearch: {},
  SucceededRead: { document: ReadOutput, generation: Schema.Finite },
  SucceededSearch: { generation: Schema.Finite, result: SearchOutput },
  UpdatedQuery: { value: Schema.String },
});
```

## 2. update returns a Command

`update` sets the search to `Loading`, increases a generation counter, and returns the `SearchDocs` Command:

apps/web/src/features/app.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 35-42; highlighted 39-40. Title: Loading now; the search runs as a Command.

```typescript
const searchFor = (model: AppModel, query: string): DocsReturn => {
  const generation = model.generation + 1;

  return {
    commands: [SearchDocs({ generation, query })],
    model: { ...model, generation, query, search: SearchState.Loading() },
  };
};
```

`update` does no I/O. It describes the next Model and the work to run.

## 3. The Command calls the capability over RPC

apps/web/src/client/docs/command.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 10-18; highlighted 13-15. Title: SearchDocs ends in a result Message.

```typescript
export const SearchDocs = Command.define("SearchDocs", {
  args: { generation: Schema.Finite, query: Schema.String },
  execute: ({ query, generation }) =>
    DocumentQueries.use((queries) => queries.search(query)).pipe(
      Effect.map((result) => Message.SucceededSearch({ generation, result })),
      Effect.orElseSucceed(() => Message.FailedSearch({ generation }))
    ),
  messages: [Message.SucceededSearch, Message.FailedSearch],
});
```

`DocumentQueries` builds its [RPC](/skills/learn-rat-stack) [client](/skills/uncomplect) from the shared contracts. The `rat-stack-boundaries/no-browser-server-imports` lint rule lets browser modules import `@rat-stack/core/contracts` and `@rat-stack/capability/rpc-group`, never a [handler](/systems/capabilities). [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725/AGENTS.md)

apps/web/src/client/docs/queries.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 7-11; highlighted none. Title: The client group comes from the contracts.

```typescript
const { group } = toRpcGroup([searchContract, readContract]);

const protocol = RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp({ url: "/rpc" }).pipe(
  Layer.provide([FetchHttpClient.layer, RpcSerialization.layerJson])
);
```

`DocumentQueries` keeps each search result for 30 seconds. A repeated query in that window is answered from the cache, with no fresh RPC. The RPC call runs on a cache miss:

apps/web/src/client/docs/queries.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 16-20; highlighted 18-19. Title: A 30-second cache in front of the search RPC.

```typescript
  const search = yield* Cache.make({
    capacity: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY,
    lookup: (query: string) => client.search({ limit: 10, query }),
    timeToLive: "30 seconds",
  });
```

On the server, `implement` binds the same `searchContract` to the content store:

apps/site/src/capabilities/search.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 7-11; highlighted none. Title: The server stays authoritative.

```typescript
export const search = implement(searchContract, ({ limit, query }) =>
  ContentStore.use((store) => store.search(query, limit)).pipe(
    Effect.map((matches) => ({ matches, total: matches.length }))
  )
);
```

## 4. update folds the result into the Model

apps/web/src/features/app.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 141-146; highlighted 143. Title: Only the latest search may land.

```typescript
    SucceededSearch: ({ generation, result }) => ({
      model:
        generation === model.generation
          ? { ...model, search: SearchState.Loaded({ result }) }
          : model,
    }),
```

The generation check drops a stale reply. If the user searches twice, the first reply carries an old generation, and `update` keeps the Model unchanged.

## Why one path

Each step has one owner, so each step can be tested alone.

- The Model is data. The view reads it and sends Messages.
- `update` is a function of the Model and a Message. It runs without a network.
- In this program, only Commands call `DocumentQueries`, the RPC client. Each Command ends in a Message.
- The contract is the one [Schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) set that the browser and the server share.

`SearchState` names four states: `Idle`, `Loading`, `Loaded`, and `Failed`. The view matches on all four, so no flag combination can show a spinner and an error at once. [model.ts](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725/apps/web/src/client/docs/model.ts)

# /lore/a-clean-playground

Source: .brain/resources/lore/a-clean-playground.svx
SHA-256: 0ae747b620e7f637ac8d43c0c35ada253adcf3f7df2384dbc2ddaf1d9e238658

# A clean playground

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Every package must do useful work and stay easy to add and remove.
This is the house rule behind the "clean playground" name.
A cartridge is a package for one job, with the resources that job needs.
It must stay self-contained and easy to delete.

Everything built here must do real work. `VISION.md` rejects toy examples that exist only to demonstrate a pattern.

rat-stack is a reference that other projects copy and maintain as source.

Its example CLI inspects real files. Its [database cartridge](/systems/database) owns a `RunLog` service and Layers for two database implementations.

A service is a named interface for a job. A Layer describes how to build services and supply their dependencies.
The website's search and read [capabilities](/systems/capabilities), named actions with shared contracts and handlers, serve the public repo. Each piece does real work.

The clean-playground test asks what remains when one package is removed. Removal must leave other packages' import paths unchanged, keep resource connections contained, and pass all required checks, tests, and builds.

`VISION.md` describes the cartridge test. `AGENTS.md` assigns each package one job and sets the required checks.

[Analytics](/systems/analytics) supplies another working package, with an explicit removal checklist. [Interest signup](/systems/interest) keeps delivery in an [adapter package](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) outside core. One-line infrastructure removal remains unproven for that adapter.

See [cartridges](/lore/cartridges) for the infrastructure example and [the fence](/lore/the-fence), the compiler checks, lint rules, tests, and hooks that enforce these rules.

# /lore/accumulate-independent-errors

Source: .brain/resources/lore/accumulate-independent-errors.svx
SHA-256: ca238a38a6bc9e97456861ba1d12d9ad433d5a04e0bd8d79a5fca495927cba7d

# Accumulate independent errors before writing output

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[Effect](/lore/effect-basics) 4's [`Effect.validate`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts#L594-L651) evaluates every collection element.
It returns all failures as a non-empty array when any element fails.
Successful values are discarded in that case.

The [code-snippets design brief](/lore/code-snippets) uses this operation for checks before writing assets.
Each snippet is an independent job.
A job stops when a dependent stage fails.
Other jobs still run.

The proposed order is:

1. Collect snippet jobs.
2. Check every job.
3. Report each failure with [diagnostic context](/lore/errors-are-part-of-the-interface).
4. Write assets only when all checks succeed.

Error accumulation means reporting every independent failure together. Here it runs across jobs. Each job must pass validation before highlighting.

The planned property inserts exactly `k` independent failures.
It expects exactly `k` diagnostics and zero asset writes.
See [property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) and [the glossary](/glossary).

## Sources

1. [Effect.validate](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts#L594-L651)
   Effect contributors. Collection failure semantics Accessed 2026-10-02.

2. [Effect.validate test](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/effect/test/Effect.test.ts#L1167-L1173)
   Effect contributors. Collected failures Accessed 2026-10-02.

# /lore/admission-controls-new-work

Source: .brain/resources/lore/admission-controls-new-work.svx
SHA-256: 51f30637eeb96b247cccc4c785c47624bda95c5572260b716b4109ba0cf6bfbd

# Admission control protects recovery

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A busy [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) needs a way to reject incoming work. Callers must respect its signal instead of immediately amplifying the same overload.

Book basis: [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B12](/lore/durability-bibliography#b12-site-reliability-engineering).

## Failure it prevents

An overloaded service keeps accepting work and extends its own outage.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Queue` and `Semaphore` offer local capacity controls. They do not choose the ingress response or implement caller cooperation. Model overload modes explicitly when needed.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Queue.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Semaphore.ts`.

## How to check

Exceed capacity. Observe a truthful refusal or durable deferral, bounded backlog, and recovery after demand falls. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Retry load needs a budget](/lore/retry-load-needs-a-budget), [Backpressure reaches the producer](/lore/backpressure-reaches-the-producer).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Nygard, Michael T. Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software. Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007.](https://archive.org/details/releaseitdesignd0000nyga)
   Pragmatic Bookshelf. §4.4 Unbounded Result Sets; Chapter 5 Stability Patterns: §5.1 Timeouts, §5.2 Circuit Breaker, §5.3 Bulkheads, §5.4 Steady State, §5.5 Fail Fast, §5.6 Handshaking, §5.7 Test Harness, §5.8 Decoupling Middleware. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Beyer, Betsy; Jones, Chris; Petoff, Jennifer; Murphy, Niall Richard, editors. Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems. O’Reilly, 2016.](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)
   O’Reilly. Chapter 3 Embracing Risk; Chapter 22 Addressing Cascading Failures (Mike Ulrich); Chapter 26 General Principles of SRE as Applied to Data Integrity; Chapter 27 Reliable Product Launches at Scale. Section-only excerpts limit detailed attribution. Accessed 2026-10-23.

3. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. Queue.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Queue.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# Source-first workflow

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Michael says coding agents learn a fast-moving library more reliably from its source repository. Stale model knowledge and large prompts are less reliable. [08:51](https://youtu.be/Wmp2Tku2PrI?t=531) [12:59](https://youtu.be/Wmp2Tku2PrI?t=779)

He describes compiler diagnostics, tests, lint checks, and saved patterns as feedback for the next move.

Diagnostics report problems found by the compiler. Lint checks reject code patterns that break project rules.
He says patterns should fit the project and model. [30:30](https://youtu.be/Wmp2Tku2PrI?t=1830) [58:08](https://youtu.be/Wmp2Tku2PrI?t=3488)

See [Vibe engineering Effect apps](/lore/ai-engineer-vibe-engineering-effect-apps-michael-arnaldi).

# /lore/agents-explore-tests-remember

Source: .brain/resources/lore/agents-explore-tests-remember.svx
SHA-256: 5c3ba194f64cf073dcae5cea5dbf151d35cf95de9dea18ff2eecbb7fbcb9eb51

# Agents explore, tests remember

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[Joel Hooks, October 1, 2026](https://x.com/joelhooks/status/2105660110068699302):

> "run up to 50 agent users using luna:max and have them click through various scenarios. chaos testing. go nuts, fix all the bad stuff"
>
> real engineering

[André Staltz replied](https://x.com/andrestaltz/status/2105716416444010671):

> @joelhooks And when those agents find good reproduction steps for a bug, convert that into playwright tests.

Agent users click through scenarios and find failures. A good reproduction becomes a repeatable Playwright regression test that repeats the actions and checks their result.

rat-stack has yet to build this fifty-agent exploration and Playwright workflow.

For executable Effect tests, read [tests through supplied services](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

## Rat-stack's reading

We connect the proposal to three practices:

- [Model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing) generates sequences of actions and checks the system against a model. Agent users can propose action sequences for exploration. Model-based testing also needs a model and assertions.
- [Property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) shrinks a failure to a small counterexample. Keep the smallest useful failing case from exploration, rather than every step the agent happened to take.
- [The fence](/lore/the-fence) puts a correction into an enforceable check. A reproduced mistake earns a test when it exposes a genuine behavior gap. Tests that only check the shape of a fix add no such coverage. See [tests that earn their place](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

## A human-driven example

A human-driven signup check found a five-second application-submission timeout and a confirmation email's `/confirm` link returning 404. A person found both failures. The resulting checks use Effect tests.

[Commit 222edd8](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/222edd833ccc19f41da236f6556a5a09dace1582) raised the timeout to twenty seconds and made timeout request an immediate retry.

- The [intake test](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/222edd833ccc19f41da236f6556a5a09dace1582/packages/core/test/interest-intake.test.ts) uses `TestClock` and a hanging fake HTTP client to check the retry outcome.
- The [route test](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/222edd833ccc19f41da236f6556a5a09dace1582/apps/mischief/test/interest.test.ts) checks that GET and POST to `/confirm` return 308. It also checks that the GET redirect preserves the token query.

These checks can run without repeating the live check.

# /lore/alchemy-domain

Source: .brain/resources/lore/alchemy-domain.svx
SHA-256: f250bc6bc3cab48afedb00aed255501a0ecd20d35fb3ec52051fabd7b047b950

# Alchemy Domain models a business as commands, aggregates, and events

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Alchemy Domain is the `@alchemy.run/domain` package, shipped with [Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy) `2.0.0-beta.85`.
The [Domain docs](https://alchemy.run/domain/) call it a domain-driven design framework for [Effect](/lore/effect-basics).
It models a business in its own terms: commands, aggregates, events, views, projections, and policies.

## Commands, aggregates, and events

A command asks for a change.
An aggregate decides whether the change happens, using its current state.
An event records what happened.
Views, projections, and policies then answer reads, feed other stores, and react to events.

## The example: deposit money into an account

The [Domain docs](https://alchemy.run/domain/) build a bank, and its first example deposits money into an account.

The [`DepositMoney` command](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/d0b4a3326718309793459160e94b35abee517b23/website/src/content/docs/domain/index.mdx#L32-L45) names its target, an account id.
It takes an amount as input.

It declares the one event it can record, `MoneyDeposited`, with the amount and the balance after.
It declares the one way it can be refused, `NotOpen`.
It replies with the new balance.

The [account aggregate](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/d0b4a3326718309793459160e94b35abee517b23/website/src/content/docs/domain/index.mdx#L49-L54) decides the command against the account's state.
A closed account refuses it with `NotOpen`.
An open account records `MoneyDeposited` with the balance plus the amount.

A [story](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/d0b4a3326718309793459160e94b35abee517b23/website/src/content/docs/domain/index.mdx#L58-L67) tests it in the business's own words.
Given an account opened for an owner, when 100 is deposited, then `MoneyDeposited` records 100 with a balance of 100.
The reply is a balance of 100.

The links point at the docs page at the commit tagged `v2.0.0-beta.85`, so the example matches the version rat-stack pins.

## One model, two places to run it

The same model runs in memory for tests and on Cloudflare Durable Objects in production, with one ordered partition per key.
[Story](https://alchemy.run/domain/story/) runs the real model in memory, so a story describes what the model does.
On [Cloudflare](https://alchemy.run/domain/cloudflare/), every aggregate instance, view key, and policy gets its own Durable Object, and the app declares none of them.
Swapping `DomainCloudflare.layerDurableObjects()` for `Domain.InMemory` changes nothing else in the program.

## Where it meets rat-stack

rat-stack pins Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.85`, the release that ships this package.
rat-stack's own Workers do not run on Alchemy Domain yet.
An optional `@alchemy.run/domain/Foldkit` [adapter](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) connects a Domain Api to a Foldkit app, as the [Foldkit chapter](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/d0b4a3326718309793459160e94b35abee517b23/website/src/content/docs/domain/foldkit.mdx) describes.

   Alchemy. What the package models, where it runs, and the bank account example. Accessed 2026-11-06.

   Alchemy. Hosting a model on Durable Objects behind a Worker. Accessed 2026-11-06.

# /lore/an-mcp-your-users-want

Source: .brain/resources/lore/an-mcp-your-users-want.svx
SHA-256: ae62490b911c6c34d881d89e611a326b61349c3c0d2673bfc406aa105b27e2b7

# An MCP your users want

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[Rhys Sullivan's practical guide](https://x.com/RhysSullivan/status/2103280866084708510) starts with the jobs people already do in a product. It asks MCP authors to expose dashboard actions, keep code mode as a choice made by the agent's client, and provide documentation search. It also covers links to specific product actions, groups of tools, and OAuth authorization.
OAuth lets a person authorize a client to access a service.

The table compares his advice with rat-stack today. The gaps remain open; this page authorizes no changes.

- **Do what the dashboard can do.**:
  - rat-stack today: Each interface uses the same contract and handler. The public site exposes `search` and `read`; the CLI projects registered capabilities too.
  - Verdict: Agree
- **Keep code mode out of the default MCP tool list.**:
  - rat-stack today: CLI `mcp` uses plain tools; `--code-mode` opts into code mode. The hosted site's MCP includes `execute` because demonstrating the sandbox is the site's job.
  - Verdict: Agree in the template; the hosted site differs
- **Ship search for docs and skills.**:
  - rat-stack today: The site's `search` and `read` capabilities cover public content. Lore pages are included in the searchable documentation.
  - Verdict: Agree
- **Add a deep link into the product.**:
  - rat-stack today: No product-action deep-link tool appears in the hosted capability registry.
  - Verdict: Gap
- **Offer toolsets and permissions tied to the auth token.**:
  - rat-stack today: Contracts can require approval, and `Approval` gates execution. The hosted MCP has no user-token toolsets; `auth.md` says it accepts no credentials.
  - Verdict: Gap
- **Let clients use OAuth; an API spec and Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD) OAuth cover most agents.**:
  - rat-stack today: The auth cartridge supports Better Auth sessions for an app, but ratstack.sh says it has no OAuth or access tokens.
  - Verdict: Gap

The comparison uses `apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts`, `apps/cli/src/command.ts`, `packages/capability/src/approval.ts`, `packages/auth/src/auth.ts`, and the hosted site's `auth.md`. See [one capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) and the [cartridges](/lore/cartridges) page for the contracts and auth boundary.

# /lore/at-protocol

Source: .brain/resources/lore/at-protocol.svx
SHA-256: 9ffd3b076f71fd8f4663c1cba38e02049209e7b9e0a089a955cfcda6dac9eea4

# AT Protocol separates identity, data, and application schemas

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

AT Protocol means Authenticated Transfer Protocol.
It is a decentralized protocol for social web applications.
The [overview](https://atproto.com/guides/overview) separates account identity, data hosting, and application views.

## A DID identifies the account

A decentralized identifier is a persistent account identifier in AT Protocol, abbreviated DID.
It supports the `did:plc` and `did:web` methods.
The [DID specification](https://atproto.com/specs/did) defines their use and the account's DID document.

The [overview](https://atproto.com/guides/overview) distinguishes the DID from the human-readable handle.
The identity includes cryptographic keys and a reference to the current hosting provider.

## A PDS hosts the repository

A PDS is a Personal Data Server.
It hosts account data, manages identity, and routes requests to other services, as the [overview](https://atproto.com/guides/overview) describes.
The [repository specification](https://atproto.com/specs/repository) makes the account's PDS the authoritative repository host.
The DID document declares its location.

A repository holds the account's public records.
Its published versions have cryptographically signed commits.
The [repository specification](https://atproto.com/specs/repository) describes a content-addressed Merkle tree that supports verification of records and the complete repository.

Repository paths have two parts: a collection identifier and a record key.
The [path rules](https://atproto.com/specs/repository#repository-paths) define the collection as a namespaced identifier, or NSID.

## Lexicons describe records and calls

A lexicon is a [schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) definition for records, HTTP endpoints, or event stream messages.
Lexicons are JSON files identified by NSIDs.
The [Lexicon specification](https://atproto.com/specs/lexicon) distinguishes record definitions from queries, procedures, and subscriptions.

A procedure schema describes an operation. It does not make that operation's input a public repository record.

The [overview](https://atproto.com/guides/overview) shows how DIDs, repositories, and lexicons fit together:

```text
DID document ── identifies keys and the current PDS
                                      │
                                      ▼
                            signed public repository
                                      │
                                      ▼
                         records described by lexicons
```

The [repository specification](https://atproto.com/specs/repository) makes repository contents public and verifiable.
A repository signature establishes verifiability. It does not hide the record's contents.

## Read Rat King next

[Rat King](/lore/rat-king) teaches how the agent-mail project uses these building blocks.
It distinguishes public profile records, private runtime bindings, and mailbox procedures.
Its page also separates implemented mail clients from the public-repository roadmap.

## Sources

1. [Protocol overview](https://atproto.com/guides/overview)
   Bluesky Social PBC. Protocol purpose, identity, PDS roles, and application schemas. Accessed 2026-11-05.

2. [AT Protocol DIDs](https://atproto.com/specs/did)
   Bluesky Social PBC. Persistent account identifiers, supported DID methods, and DID documents. Accessed 2026-11-05.

3. [Repository specification](https://atproto.com/specs/repository)
   Bluesky Social PBC. Public records, signed commits, repository paths, and PDS authority. Accessed 2026-11-05.

4. [Lexicon specification](https://atproto.com/specs/lexicon)
   Bluesky Social PBC. Schemas for records, HTTP endpoints, and event streams. Accessed 2026-11-05.

# /lore/backpressure-reaches-the-producer

Source: .brain/resources/lore/backpressure-reaches-the-producer.svx

# Backpressure reaches the producer

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Asynchronous sends can outrun the receiver. Bound fan-out against scarce resources and make the producer participate in the flow-control policy.

Book basis: [B3](/lore/durability-bibliography#b3-designing-elixir-systems-with-otp), [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it).

## Failure it prevents

A bounded consumer hides an ever-growing upstream mailbox or set of waiting producers.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Queue.bounded` suspends offers at capacity. `Queue.dropping` and `Queue.sliding` choose loss policies. Bounded `Effect.forEach` and `Semaphore` cap active work. Upstream backlog needs its own bound.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Queue.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Semaphore.ts`.

## How to check

Run a faster producer against a slower consumer. Check backlog and memory, plus the documented wait, reject, or drop behavior. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Admission control protects recovery](/lore/admission-controls-new-work), [Bulkheads isolate scarce capacity](/lore/bulkheads-isolate-capacity).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/bindings

Source: .brain/resources/lore/bindings.svx
SHA-256: 9c8561c29379c48888a39a823d42243154f6372cc72075e263be1fef3fe93b4f

# Bindings

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

**Goal:** connect a [Worker](/lore/workers-answer-requests-durable-objects-own-named-state) to a resource it declares, and see what it gets back.

A binding is a declared connection. On Cloudflare, it lets a Worker use a platform resource such as a bucket, a queue, or a stream. [Cloudflare bindings](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/)
In [Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy), the binding is declared in the same [Effect](/lore/effect-basics) program as the resource.

## Worked example: the events cartridge writes to a stream

The events [cartridge](/lore/cartridges) sends one row per request to a Pipelines stream.
It binds the stream in two steps:

packages/events/src/basin.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 56-57; highlighted 57. Title: Init: ask for a writer bound to the stream.

```typescript
      const saltValue = yield* salt.text;
      const writer = yield* Cloudflare.Pipelines.WriteStream(stream);
```

packages/events/src/basin.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 75-75; highlighted none. Title: Runtime: provide the binding implementation.

```typescript
  ).pipe(Layer.provide(Cloudflare.Pipelines.WriteStreamBinding));
```

1. `Cloudflare.Pipelines.WriteStream(stream)` names the stream this code writes to. It returns a writer with a `send` method.
2. `Layer.provide(Cloudflare.Pipelines.WriteStreamBinding)` gives the [Layer](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) what it needs: it supplies the implementation that talks to the bound stream at runtime.

Alchemy documents the same two steps for queues: `WriteQueue` in the init phase, and `WriteQueueBinding` in the runtime layer. [Queue.ts](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.85/packages/cloudflare/src/Queues/Queue.ts)

## Why a binding carries permission and configuration

Sam says a binding includes both permissions and environment variables.
A [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies)'s configuration and permissions can be declared together before the application runs. [Happy Path 116, 37:09](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=2229) [37:33](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=2253)

He also describes deriving least-privilege policies: permissions limited to the methods an application uses. [Effect Office Hours 27, 58:16](https://youtu.be/fPSxB7ZgSJw?t=3496) [59:23](https://youtu.be/fPSxB7ZgSJw?t=3563)

## Next

Read [Queues, Pipelines, Workflows and K2 do different jobs](/lore/queues-pipelines-workflows-and-k2-do-different-jobs) to choose what to bind.
Read [Workers answer requests; Durable Objects own named state](/lore/workers-answer-requests-durable-objects-own-named-state) to choose where state lives.
Then read [cartridges](/lore/cartridges) for how a package owns its resources and bindings.

See [Happy Path 116](/lore/happy-path-116-infrastructure-as-effects-sam-goodwin) and [Effect Office Hours 27](/lore/effect-office-hours-27-alchemy-infrastructure-as-effects).

# /lore/build-time-work-stays-out-of-requests

Source: .brain/resources/lore/build-time-work-stays-out-of-requests.svx
SHA-256: 5c290d260f53cf7be8768832c7a59e3c111d1bd5d40f80e3de0c881266e3d8c6

# Build-time work stays out of requests

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

The existing [asset writer](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/scripts/emit-assets.ts) emits output identified by a hash of its content.
The Worker reads that output through [static assets](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/static-assets.ts).

The [code-snippets design brief](/lore/code-snippets) keeps Git reads and highlighting in build-time work.
Request-time work receives static output.
It does not resolve Git objects or start Shiki.

The proposed check verifies that neither the snippet package nor Shiki enters the startup bundle.
The existing [startup budget](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/scripts/startup-budget.ts) limits:

- Entry JavaScript to 3,300,000 bytes.
- Complete JavaScript upload to 5,000,000 bytes.

Check the modules included in the bundle, as well as its size, to verify which packages it includes.

[Checks before writing output](/lore/accumulate-independent-errors) finish before assets are written.
[Pinned sources](/lore/pinned-sources-can-report-drift) require no generation-time network fetch.

See [the glossary](/glossary) for build-time work and request-time work.

# /lore/bulkheads-isolate-capacity

Source: .brain/resources/lore/bulkheads-isolate-capacity.svx

# Bulkheads isolate scarce capacity

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Critical clients need their own capacity. A single shared limit can still let one failed or noisy workload consume every available slot.

> Protect critical clients by giving them their own pool to call.

Source: [Q07](/lore/durability-bibliography#q07); [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B3](/lore/durability-bibliography#b3-designing-elixir-systems-with-otp).

## Failure it prevents

Noncritical load exhausts the pool needed by the primary path.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

Separate `Semaphore` or `Queue` instances isolate local work admission. `Pool` manages actual resources. Independent runtime or infrastructure failure domains require more than fibers.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Semaphore.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Queue.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Pool.ts`.

## How to check

Saturate one workload. Confirm that the separately reserved critical path still acquires its resources. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Backpressure reaches the producer](/lore/backpressure-reaches-the-producer), [Effect is not BEAM](/lore/effect-is-not-beam).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/scopes-own-resources).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

   Pragmatic Bookshelf. §4.4 Unbounded Result Sets; Chapter 5 Stability Patterns: §5.1 Timeouts, §5.2 Circuit Breaker, §5.3 Bulkheads, §5.4 Steady State, §5.5 Fail Fast, §5.6 Handshaking, §5.7 Test Harness, §5.8 Decoupling Middleware. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/cache-completed-values

Source: .brain/resources/lore/cache-completed-values.svx
SHA-256: 42cde4edb388145dd5fc0eb09c1da024a0af311e480cab5d1ef0aecf16d3974f

# Shared caches hold completed values

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A Worker isolate can serve several requests. A request owns its unfinished I/O. Shared caches must contain completed values.

The cold-isolate 1101 failure in [PR #64](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/64) crossed that boundary. `ContentStore` held pending asset reads in a shared cache. Another request could await work owned by the first request.

`Effect.cached`, `Effect.cachedWithTTL`, and `Effect.cachedInvalidateWithTTL` can share pending work. A successful result cache and a pending-work cache have different lifetimes.

## Store the result after the read

`ContentStore` keeps an `Option` in a `Ref`. Each request reads that completed-value cache first.

- A hit returns the completed value.
- A miss reads assets within the current request.
- A successful read stores its completed value.
- A failed read leaves the cache empty.

Concurrent misses can repeat a read. They do not wait for another request's unfinished read.

```text
request A ── cache miss ── asset read ── completed value ── cache
request B ── cache miss ── asset read ── completed value ── cache
request C ── cache hit  ──────────────────────────────── value
```

The cache is a derived copy of generated content assets. The content build writes those assets; requests store only successfully decoded values.

## Check the lifetime at construction

`rat-stack-patterns/no-shared-pending-cache` rejects these cache constructors in module, service, and Worker initialization effects. Keep request-local work inside its request handler.

A targeted exception must explain the cached value and its lifetime with a `--` reason. CryptoKey derivation from a fixed secret needs separate review from request-bound asset reads.

The fixture tests plant the old `ContentStore.make` cache shape. The rule rejects it before it can reach a Worker.

See [Worker init runs twice](/lore/init-runs-twice) for the initialization boundary and [the fence](/lore/the-fence) for validation.

## Sources

   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. ContentStore replaces shared pending asset reads with completed-value caches. Accessed 2026-10-08.

2. [Be explicit about lifetimes](https://github.com/just-be-dev/effect-cloudflare-foldkit-template/blob/04851db8649501bfaf8d2712429074ba0290a10f/docs/architecture.md)
   GitHub just-be-dev. Assign each resource and mutable value to an explicit lifetime. Accessed 2026-10-08.

3. [Request lifetime guardrail](https://github.com/just-be-dev/effect-cloudflare-foldkit-template/blob/04851db8649501bfaf8d2712429074ba0290a10f/docs/guardrails.md)
   GitHub just-be-dev. Keep request identity and instance locks within their owning lifetimes. Accessed 2026-10-08.

# /lore/cafe-stack

Source: .brain/resources/lore/cafe-stack.svx
SHA-256: 9cbed74f00a3786a09df9cb781a1a616a16b7a39f77241aaa44ed58c63309c65

# CAFE names the Cloudflare, Alchemy, Foldkit and Effect stack

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

CAFE is a named stack. Each letter has one job.

Read the [CAFE news](/news) and browse the [project directory](/directory).

[Maxwell Brown](https://github.com/IMax153) coined the name; [Justin Bennett](https://github.com/just-be-dev) spread it with his template on 8 October 2026. That day, [Devin Jameson](https://github.com/devinjameson), Maxwell and [Sam Goodwin](https://github.com/sam-goodwin) streamed a CAFE build, and [Sebastian Lorenz](https://github.com/fubhy) wrote the explainer people share.

- **C**:
  - Part: Cloudflare
  - Job: Runs the app: Workers, Durable Objects, storage, static assets.
- **A**:
  - Part: Alchemy
  - Job: Declares the cloud resources as an Effect program.
- **F**:
  - Part: Foldkit
  - Job: Draws the UI with the Elm Architecture on Effect.
- **E**:
  - Part: Effect
  - Job: Does the typed work between the UI and the cloud.

A request follows one path. The [Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy) Stack declares every box on it.

```text
┌─ Alchemy Stack ──────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                  │
│  Foldkit app (browser)                           │
│      │  HTTP or RPC, typed by a shared schema    │
│      ▼                                           │
│  Worker (Effect)                                 │
│      │                                           │
│      ▼                                           │
│  Durable Object or storage                       │
│                                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The browser and the Worker import the same schemas. Alchemy reads the same program to deploy and to test.

## The canonical example

[Effect-TS/cafe](https://github.com/Effect-TS/cafe) is a chat app from the Effect organization. Its README defines CAFE. [Sam Goodwin](/lore/sam-goodwin), who wrote Alchemy, built it. Maxwell Brown also commits to it.

It shows these patterns:

- `@cafe/api` holds the HTTP and [RPC](/skills/learn-rat-stack) schemas. It may import only `effect`, so the browser can import it safely. A lint rule enforces this.
- The Worker serves an Effect `HttpApi`. [PR #6](https://github.com/Effect-TS/cafe/pull/6) moves chat events to Effect RPC over a `Cloudflare.RpcDurableObject`, one per chat.
- The frontend is a Foldkit single-page app. Side effects are `Command.define` definitions. [PR #2](https://github.com/Effect-TS/cafe/pull/2) streamed socket frames with `Subscription.fromEvent`; PR #6 later replaced the socket with RPC.
- Story tests check update, Messages, and Commands. Scene tests drive the rendered view. Both are pure.
- Live tests deploy the Stack with `Test.make` from `alchemy/Test/Vitest`. The end-to-end test drives Chromium through Playwright.
- CI deploys one stage per pull request and destroys it when the pull request closes.
- `stacks/github.ts` is an Alchemy Stack that writes the CI Cloudflare credentials as repository secrets.
- Configuration comes from `effect/Config`. Its `AGENTS.md` forbids `process.env`.
- The repository carries the Foldkit agent skills.

## Other CAFE apps

- **[just-be-dev/effect-cloudflare-foldkit-template](https://github.com/just-be-dev/effect-cloudflare-foldkit-template)**: A template with tooling and guardrails for Effect 4, Foldkit, and Alchemy 2 on Cloudflare.
- **[NigelThorne/foldkit-demo](https://github.com/NigelThorne/foldkit-demo)**: Live shared sessions on Durable Objects with SQLite and hibernatable WebSockets.
- **[mwarger/corefour](https://github.com/mwarger/corefour)**: A poster app with an Effect `HttpApi` Worker, Foldkit server rendering, and KV and R2 storage.
- **[Manzanita-Research/foldkit-dials](https://github.com/Manzanita-Research/foldkit-dials)**: Live tuning controls for Foldkit apps. See the next section.
- **[Manzanita-Research/pleat](https://github.com/Manzanita-Research/pleat)**: Typed styles for Foldkit and Effect 4. MIT.
- **[Effect-TS/slopcop](https://github.com/Effect-TS/slopcop)**: Several Effect Workers with D1 and Queues, declared in one Alchemy Stack.

Pleat treats a style as a value:

- Styles merge by fixed laws.
- Every rule compiles to atomic CSS when its module loads.
- Recipe variants are typed by Effect [Schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary).
- A model that generates UI can choose styles, but it can never write CSS.

[Jem](https://github.com/jem-computer) at Manzanita Research builds actively in the CAFE space: Pleat, foldkit-dials, and [foldkit-native](https://github.com/Manzanita-Research/foldkit-native).

## foldkit-dials

[Manzanita-Research/foldkit-dials](https://github.com/Manzanita-Research/foldkit-dials) gives a Foldkit app live tuning controls, after DialKit. It is MIT licensed, at version 0.1.0.

- The dials are an Effect Schema.
- Every dial edit is a Message.
- Foldkit DevTools records each edit.
- Time travel replays it.
- Story and Scene tests can drive it.

Its demo deploys with Alchemy. A `stacks/github.ts` Stack bootstraps its CI credentials, as in cafe.

foldkit-dials is a clear example of the Foldkit rule that every change is a Message. A tool that follows the rule gets recording, replay, and tests from the runtime.

## Where rat-stack sits

rat-stack is a CAFE stack with [the fence](/lore/the-fence) around it. The table compares it with cafe at rat-stack commit `3fb103b`.

- **Alchemy Worker shape**:
  - rat-stack: Class form: `Cloudflare.Worker<Mischief>()`, `Cloudflare.Workers.RpcWorker`, `Cloudflare.Website.Foldkit`
  - cafe: `Cloudflare.Worker`, `Cloudflare.RpcDurableObject`, `Cloudflare.Website.Foldkit`
- **Runtime tests**:
  - rat-stack: `alchemy/Test/Vitest` with fixture Workers in `apps/site/test/*-runtime.test.ts`
  - cafe: `Test.make` deploys the whole Stack; Playwright drives Chromium
- **API surface**:
  - rat-stack: One contract projected to RPC, HTTP, MCP, and CLI by `packages/capability`
  - cafe: Hand-written `HttpApi` and `RpcGroup`
- **Foldkit**:
  - rat-stack: `Runtime.makeApplication`, `Command.define`, `@foldkit/oxlint-plugin`, Story and Scene tests
  - cafe: The same, plus the Foldkit agent skills
- **Config**:
  - rat-stack: varlock `.env.schema` into Effect `Config`; no `process.env` in source
  - cafe: `effect/Config`; no `process.env`
- **Pull request stages**:
  - rat-stack: `scripts/deploy-preview.sh` deploys a Website and RpcBackend preview by hand; no live end-to-end test
  - cafe: CI deploys one stage per pull request, runs live tests, and destroys it on close
- **Tracing**:
  - rat-stack: `Cloudflare.Telemetry`, opt-in, off by default
  - cafe: Not enabled

The largest difference is the API [surface](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces). See [one capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) and [infrastructure as effects](/lore/infrastructure-as-effects).

# /lore/capture-first

Source: .brain/resources/lore/capture-first.svx
SHA-256: 8b464935a038067f72a85513f908bfb78f7240be394b0349c6786d39edc20e4d

# Capture first, shape later

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

An event you didn't store can't be analyzed later. Shape decisions change, but a lost event stays lost. Event recording stores everything it is allowed to store. Queries select and interpret the stored fields when they run.

Cloudflare Basin makes this concrete. Events that do not match a structured stream's schema "are accepted during ingestion but will be dropped during processing," the docs say. They also say "schema modifications are not supported after stream creation."

An unstructured stream instead accepts "any valid JSON without validation" into "a single value column." [Manage streams](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/streams/manage-streams/)

Snowplow reached the same rule years earlier. Its pipelines are "non-lossy," it says. When validation or enrichment fails, payloads are "stored into a bad rows storage solution … instead of being discarded." [snowplow-event-recovery](https://github.com/snowplow-incubator/snowplow-event-recovery)

In rat-stack, the `packages/events` cartridge owns event recording and its resources.
It sends one JSON event record per request to an unstructured Basin stream. A pipeline copies it unchanged (`SELECT *`) into an Iceberg table, and queries select and interpret its fields later.

Size and rate limits still apply. The stream also requires the `{ "value": <event> }` row wrapper; omitting it drops rows during processing. [Analytics](/systems/analytics) documents that boundary.

Capture first keeps only permitted request facts. The event record holds method, path, status, and referrer origin and path. Its query string has credential, email, code, and session keys removed.

The request body is never read. The IP is stored only as a salted hash, computed with an additional secret value.

Visitor identity is a setting:

- **`daily`**: Hash of IP, user agent, and day; no cookie.
- **`persistent`**: One first-party id per browser.

The server sets the persistent id. WebKit "deletes all cookies created in JavaScript and all other script-writeable storage after 7 days of no user interaction." [Tracking Prevention in WebKit](https://webkit.org/tracking-prevention/)

Segment's identify guidance joins people later by a stable database id. It advises against using an email address. It gives the reason: "because database IDs never change." [Spec: Identify](https://segment.com/docs/connections/spec/identify/)

Property tests check these rules. See [property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) and [model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing).

## Sources

   Cloudflare docs. Stream validation rules; used for capture-first unstructured ingestion. Accessed 2026-10-01.

2. [GitHub - snowplow-incubator/snowplow-event-recovery · GitHub](https://github.com/snowplow-incubator/snowplow-event-recovery)
   GitHub snowplow-incubator/snowplow-event-recovery. Event recovery design; used for retaining failed payloads rather than discarding them. Accessed 2026-10-01.

3. [Spec: Identify](https://segment.com/docs/connections/spec/identify/)
   Segment docs. Identify guidance; used for joining people with stable database ids. Accessed 2026-10-01.

# /lore/cartridges

Source: .brain/resources/lore/cartridges.svx
SHA-256: e36ad7da1f02f03c253bd74b9c75f193b79ffd367d02c01c68933f7f246db659

# Cartridges

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A cartridge is a package that owns one job and the resources it needs.
A service is the named interface callers use for that job. Its service tag identifies the service.
A Layer describes how to build services and supply their dependencies.

An Alchemy Layer can also declare the cloud resources behind a service.
`Layer.provide` supplies the chosen implementation to the application.
Replacing that Layer changes the implementation and its dependencies without changing callers.

The database cartridge makes this concrete. `DatabaseVendor` represents either D1 or Hyperdrive Postgres.
`packages/database/src/d1.ts` [declares the D1 schema and database](/lore/infrastructure-as-effects#worked-example-a-d1-layer).

`packages/database/src/hyperdrive-postgres.ts` declares the Postgres schema, Hyperdrive connection, and migration registration.
Both provide the same `RunLog` service. The auth cartridge consumes `DatabaseVendor`.

`packages/auth/src/auth.ts` picks Better Auth's D1 or Hyperdrive adapter.

A cartridge must:

- Have a label.
- Add with one package and one Layer or Alchemy Stack line.
- Remove without breaking unrelated packages.
- Declare the bindings that give it access to its resources.
- Be easy to throw away.

Removal must leave no loose resources or broken imports. Delete the package and its provision line, then run `pnpm turbo run check test build`.

[Analytics](/systems/analytics) is a second running example: `packages/events` owns capture and its Basin resources. [README](/README.md) lists the steps needed to remove it. `packages/subscriber-delivery` is a provider adapter behind core's ports. One-line infrastructure removal remains unproven for that package.

## Where the pattern comes from

This project calls the pattern a "cartridge". Sam describes Layers as a way to carry infrastructure and permissions with a service, and calls the idea "SaaS as NPM." [devtools.fm, 21:15](https://youtu.be/MtKHzAH6uXM?t=1275). He also describes swapping implementations by providing different Layers. [Effect Office Hours 27, 34:35](https://youtu.be/fPSxB7ZgSJw?t=2075).

Interchangeability between provider implementations remains unproven. Sam describes test or development Layers for infrastructure and a type error when code still requires a removed binding. [Happy Path 116, 15:25](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=925) [Effect Office Hours 27, 07:05](https://youtu.be/fPSxB7ZgSJw?t=425).

See [one capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) for the shared contract and [a clean playground](/lore/a-clean-playground) for the house rule behind these boundaries.

# /lore/checkpoints-follow-commits

Source: .brain/resources/lore/checkpoints-follow-commits.svx
SHA-256: 2bfdfe15608bc96eaa74adaabf69be2c1b18227a19e6adbe216d744709d7fc71

# Checkpoints follow the promised commit

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A consumer position and its materialized state must agree. Acknowledge processing only after the promised processing completes.

> allowing a single stateful transaction to atomically update both the state and input offsets.

Source: [Q13](/lore/durability-bibliography#q13); [B5](/lore/durability-bibliography#b5-building-event-driven-microservices).

## Failure it prevents

Progress advances without its state, or state commits while replay still reapplies the event.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`SqlClient.withTransaction` covers its database boundary. `Stream.runForEach` expresses handling only. Broker acknowledgement and remote transactions need their own protocol.

Source: `packages/effect/src/sql/SqlClient.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Stream.ts`.

## How to check

Crash before and after state commit and acknowledgement. Redeliver and compare state with the expected checkpoint. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Retry needs idempotent effects](/lore/retry-needs-idempotency), [Dead letters need a return path](/lore/dead-letters-need-a-return-path).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

   O’Reilly. Chapter 3 Communication and Data Contracts; Chapter 6 Deterministic Stream Processing; Chapter 7 Stateful Streaming; Chapter 9 Microservices Using Function-as-a-Service; Chapter 14 Supportive Tooling. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/circuit-breakers-have-state

Source: .brain/resources/lore/circuit-breakers-have-state.svx
SHA-256: 6bcc6e6712a822e0015c5b7603e7c159262b5c4823158565bad3f0085272869d

# Circuit breakers have state

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A circuit breaker is a stateful guard around a dependency. It differs from retry. Its state determines whether a dependency call is attempted. Threshold accounting must match the actual implementation.

> calls to the circuit breaker fail immediately, without any attempt to execute the real operation.

Source: [Q06](/lore/durability-bibliography#q06); [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B11](/lore/durability-bibliography#b11-property-based-testing).

## Failure it prevents

Callers keep spending capacity on a known-unhealthy dependency.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

No dependency circuit-breaker API was found. Compose timeout and typed failure handling with an explicit XState lifecycle. Define whether state is local or shared.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Schema.ts`.

## How to check

Generate success, failure, timeout, cooldown, and probe histories. Verify exact threshold semantics and visible state changes. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Bulkheads isolate scarce capacity](/lore/bulkheads-isolate-capacity), [Supervision chooses what restarts](/lore/supervision-is-a-recovery-policy).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Nygard, Michael T. Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software. Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007.](https://archive.org/details/releaseitdesignd0000nyga)
   Pragmatic Bookshelf. §4.4 Unbounded Result Sets; Chapter 5 Stability Patterns: §5.1 Timeouts, §5.2 Circuit Breaker, §5.3 Bulkheads, §5.4 Steady State, §5.5 Fail Fast, §5.6 Handshaking, §5.7 Test Harness, §5.8 Decoupling Middleware. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Hebert, Fred. Property-Based Testing with PropEr, Erlang, and Elixir. Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2019.](https://pragprog.com/titles/fhproper/property-based-testing-with-proper-erlang-and-elixir/)
   Pragmatic Bookshelf. Chapter 7 Shrinking; Laying Out Stateful Properties; Testing Parallel Executions; Initial State for the State Machine; Adjusting the Model. Use the actual breaker’s threshold semantics. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/cleanup-can-be-an-idempotent-postcondition

Source: .brain/resources/lore/cleanup-can-be-an-idempotent-postcondition.svx

# Cleanup can be an idempotent postcondition

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A useful API can make a routine absent-state condition ordinary. The [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) owns the postcondition instead of requiring every caller to catch and ignore it.

> Rather than throwing an error when unset is asked to delete an unknown variable, it should have simply returned without doing anything.

Source: [Q16](/lore/durability-bibliography#q16); [B10](/lore/durability-bibliography#b10-a-philosophy-of-software-design).

## Failure it prevents

Cleanup accumulates special cases and fails on harmless repeated execution.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

Typed failures do not require exporting avoidable errors. Put the domain meaning in the service [contract](/systems/capabilities); [Effect](/lore/effect-basics) supplies execution. The domain defines the postcondition.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Context.ts`.

## How to check

Run cleanup twice. Require the same intended result, while preserving meaningful permission or storage failures. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Retry needs idempotent effects](/lore/retry-needs-idempotency), [Failures keep their meaning](/lore/failures-keep-their-meaning).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/error-model).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).
