# /lore/every-task-needs-an-owner

Source: .brain/resources/lore/every-task-needs-an-owner.svx
SHA-256: bc6b0393978cc3db4a687cf0110b36141772dab34a813cf762bee46cae652d31

# Every task needs an owner

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Managed worker abstractions make lifecycle policy visible. A task that escapes its owner also escapes that owner’s shutdown and failure handling.

> Elixir can’t manage what it doesn’t know about.

Source: [Q04](/lore/durability-bibliography#q04); [B3](/lore/durability-bibliography#b3-designing-elixir-systems-with-otp).

## Failure it prevents

A request returns but unobserved child work fails or holds resources indefinitely.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Effect.forkScoped` and `FiberSet` attach work to a [Scope](/lore/scopes-own-resources). `Effect.forkDetach` detaches the [fiber](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner) from its parent. The runtime can still stop it. Add recovery policy separately.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Scope.ts`, `packages/effect/src/FiberSet.ts`.

## How to check

Interrupt the owner. Verify child completion or interruption, resource release, and the reported outcome. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Supervision chooses what restarts](/lore/supervision-is-a-recovery-policy), [Durable work needs storage](/lore/durable-work-needs-storage).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# Failures keep their meaning

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Model expected business failures explicitly. Hide recoverable details only where callers do not need them to preserve correctness.

> These different kinds of errors require different implementations.

Source: [Q15](/lore/durability-bibliography#q15); [B7](/lore/durability-bibliography#b7-domain-modeling-made-functional), [B10](/lore/durability-bibliography#b10-a-philosophy-of-software-design).

A broken execution becomes a permanent business refusal, or a permanent refusal triggers endless retry.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Schema.TaggedError` and `Effect.catchTag` carry named expected outcomes. Classification and [defect](/lore/effect-basics) policy remain domain decisions. A [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) seam can own recoverable mechanics.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Schema.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Context.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Layer.ts`.

Exercise each declared failure category. Verify retry, refusal, escalation, and uncertain outcomes remain distinguishable. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

# /lore/flags-climb-on-evidence

Source: .brain/resources/lore/flags-climb-on-evidence.svx
SHA-256: 1ac2a6fd73dbf6e786ffa99b1da4dd3ad3c39e11a93b629312f4be0a1cc03087

# Flags climb on evidence

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A [feature flag](/systems/flags) declares a ladder of values.
Each rung names its authority and the evidence required to leave it.
A climb moves exactly one rung. A downward move uses `off`.

## Measure the exit where the flag is read

Every exit names an event, a measurement location, and a threshold.
Record the observation through `record_flag_evidence`, with its source reference.

A read scope is the partition for a flag value and its evidence.
The child's `readScope` [schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) defines the flag's scope. Its default is the literal `global` scope.
A measurement counts only at its own scope and current rung.

A flip clears current evidence. Returning to a rung needs fresh measurements.

A mismatch returns `FlagScopeMismatch` and a repair instruction.
The same scope check applies to readers, evidence, and flips.

## Authority comes from approval

The roles are `agent`, `arbiter`, and `owner`.
The child supplies the [capability approval service](/systems/capabilities).
That service authorizes the requested climb. Token checks stay in the child's composition.

A climb above agent also needs an `approvalRef` quote.
A role field alone grants nothing.

`off` still passes through the shared capability implementation and attempt audit.
It supplies an always-granted approval implementation, so an approval outage cannot block it.
The flag's declared `kill` policy selects its destination or explains why no stop exists.

## Commit once, then project

A projection is a copy derived from a committed value.

The Durable Object owns the current value and its receipt.
It commits both with a dirty projection marker in one transaction.
An alarm writes that committed value to the KV read replica.

```text
operator → Pending → approval → DO value + receipt + dirty marker
                                                    │
                                                    ▼
                                             alarm → KV → reader
```

The Pending attempt exists before the approval gate.
A separate outcome records success, denial, or failure.
An interrupted call can remain Pending. The authoritative position can still show a committed receipt.

A crash before projection leaves the dirty marker intact.
Redrive uses the committed value. It clears a marker only if that marker still names the projected version.

Cloudflare retries failed alarms six times, starting with two seconds of backoff.
After the final failed retry, the [adapter](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) schedules a fresh alarm at the next exponential backoff step.
An internal redrive method also supports operator recovery.

Readers never call the Durable Object.
They read KV and apply the declaration's `failurePolicy`.
The default policy uses the catalog default when the replica fails.

Under the default policy, an empty KV keeps deployment Config or declared defaults.
The `refuse` policy returns a typed failure on a missing or failed replica read.

The explicit KV ledger fallback retains attempt and outcome keys.
It refuses authoritative writes by default.
A composition must explicitly accept non-atomic writes without cross-isolate serialization.

## Keep urgent stops out of KV

KV changes can take 60 seconds or more to reach another location.
`off` bypasses approval, but it cannot bypass that propagation delay.
Use deployment settings or a stronger control path for kill switches and safety stops.

Each declaration also names its purpose, owner, and removal date.
The removal-date [fence](/lore/the-fence) keeps temporary flags from becoming forgotten behavior.

Use [Add a feature flag](/skills/add-a-feature-flag) to declare the ladder and its checks.
The generated models exercise scoped flips, denied approval, downward moves, attempt accounting, and projection recovery.

1. [Core flag contracts and ledger engine](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/tree/f294f950ebbd3911ac5a8ffea30e1ac87cd26be9/packages/core/src)
   rat-stack. Declared rungs, scoped evidence, approval-gated flips, and attempt receipts. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Flags cartridge adapters](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/tree/f294f950ebbd3911ac5a8ffea30e1ac87cd26be9/packages/flags/src)
   rat-stack. Durable Object authority, durable projection markers, KV readers, and generated history tests. Accessed 2026-10-23.

   Cloudflare. KV is eventually consistent. Changes can take 60 seconds or more to reach another location. Accessed 2026-10-23.

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

# Golden signals expose overload

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[Service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) monitoring needs all four golden signals. Separate symptom detection from internal diagnosis, and distinguish failed-request latency from successful latency.

> The four golden signals of monitoring are latency, traffic, errors, and saturation.

A service reports fast responses while errors rise or scarce capacity is exhausted.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Metric.counter`, gauge, and histogram supply instruments. Connect backlog and parked-work observations through the actual adapters. Define alerts and response outside these constructors.

Create a slow dependency and a parked item. Verify that user-visible failure and resource saturation are observable. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

# /lore/hateoas

Source: .brain/resources/lore/hateoas.svx
SHA-256: 0d224624f19430c4f963fe6468ec67125144256f191e954fb6d8f852826d9942

# HATEOAS

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

HATEOAS means hypermedia as the engine of application state. Roy Fielding names it as one of REST's four uniform-interface constraints in his dissertation, [chapter 5, section 5.1.5](https://ics.uci.edu/~fielding/pubs/dissertation/rest_arch_style.htm#sec_5_1_5). In [section 5.3.3](https://ics.uci.edu/~fielding/pubs/dissertation/rest_arch_style.htm#sec_5_3_3), the application moves between states by choosing among the transitions in the representations it receives. Fielding includes both automated agents and human-operated browsers.

## Rat-stack's application

Joel Hooks puts the agent-facing principle this way:

> My theory about hypertext as the engine of application state is that HATOS style links and pointers should be part of agentic surfaces in that we want to show them what they can do next and give that sort of guidance to agents and bake it in at that layer where humans don't necessarily need to see that you know the information architecture is different and has a different scale

Joel applies the idea to links and pointers on agent-facing pages and responses: `llms.txt`, the markdown variant, MCP responses, and capability responses. They should show the agent what it can do next. Humans need not see all that guidance because information and next actions are organized differently for agents. `AgentOnly` variants are where that extra guidance belongs.

## What exists, and what is direction

[Content negotiation](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/app.ts) serves markdown by default and HTML when requested. It also recognizes browser and crawler user agents; a browser can receive HTML without an explicit Accept header. `/llms.txt` is the starting point for an agent. The [content generator](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/scripts/generate-content.ts) gives that guide links to rules, lore, skills, and the full docs, and builds HTML "Linked from" backlinks from the lore graph.

[Audience variants](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/scripts/content-lib.ts) retain `AgentOnly` blocks in agent markdown and remove them from HTML. `/tokenmaxx` has inline next-action guidance. Its [AgentOnly blocks](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/content/tokenmaxx.md) link to the agent guide and related lore, explain the harness pieces, and guide preparation.

Agents submit a person-approved editable card through `joinInterest` over MCP, HTTP, or CLI. They use a single-use page ticket from the [/tokenmaxx agent view](/tokenmaxx). [Intake verifies the ticket](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/join-intake.ts). Email confirmation is still required; it does not reserve a seat.

Next-action links in capability and MCP responses remain a goal. The projections do not yet supply those links.

[Interest signup](/systems/interest) records the current consent and confirmation boundary. Applications are agent-only. An agent obtains a page ticket and submits the person's approved card with contact permission. The person confirms their email through the email link in a browser.

The [agent guide](/llms.txt) gives the search → read → graph workflow.

[One capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) describes the existing projections. These pieces apply the hypermedia idea; they are not a claim that every rat-stack interface satisfies all of Fielding's REST constraints.

# /lore/hexagonal-architecture

Source: .brain/resources/lore/hexagonal-architecture.svx
SHA-256: 2469b979b3d500f32e52913d5dc729d7d729e0217b92587a81b60268b9bd18bb

# Hexagonal architecture

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Alistair Cockburn's [2005 article](https://alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture/) calls the pattern "Ports and Adapters," with "Hexagonal Architecture" as its alternative name. Users, programs, tests, or batch scripts can drive the application. Tests can run without its eventual devices and databases.

A port is an interface for an application job.
A technology-specific adapter implements that interface for an outside system. The application need not know what is on the other side. The distinction is inside versus outside, not a prescribed number of sides.

## Rat-stack's stance

Joel Hooks:

> I think hexagonal and ports and adapters, generally speaking, is an extremely good fit and matches what we are kind of doing anyway inside of our effect layer. So if we were putting a name on the architecture or a principle from which we derive our own version of the architecture, hexagonal would be it. We are not zealots. However, we do recognize really good ideas when we see them.

Rat-stack's Effect layer follows the inside/outside boundary. We adapt that principle without requiring the whole architecture, its diagram, or particular folder names.

## How rat-stack does it

On the driving side, interfaces call the application.
[One capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) starts with a contract, binds a handler, and projects CLI, HTTP, MCP, RPC, and code mode. The [no-hand-rolled-surface rule](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/scripts/oxlint-plugin-boundaries.ts) keeps interface construction in the projection package.

On the driven side, Effect `Context.Service` definitions provide ports for [subscriber intake (`SubscriberIntake`)](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/interest-intake.ts) and [confirmation (`SubscriberConfirm`)](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/interest-confirm-port.ts).
[Delivery Layers](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/subscriber-delivery/src/delivery.ts) implement those ports outside core.
[Worker wiring](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/worker.ts) supplies the production implementations.

Applications now use the agent-only `joinInterest` capability. The former browser submission routes return 410.
Browser email-link confirmation remains. [Interest signup](/systems/interest) documents the current flow.

Typed preparation for agent-assisted intake uses the same service boundary: [`IntakeTicket`, `AbuseScore`, and `IntakeEvents`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/intake.ts), question and consent schemas, and test layers live in core. [Interest signup](/systems/interest) records the agent-only application path and email confirmation boundary.

## Boundaries fixed

Three leaks have been fixed:

- HTTP adapters lived beside ports in core. Intake and confirmation adapters now live in [`@rat-stack/subscriber-delivery`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/tree/main/packages/subscriber-delivery/src), composed by `src/delivery.ts`.
- Two ports were named for the provider rather than the job. [`SubscriberIntake`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/interest-intake.ts) and [`SubscriberConfirm`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/interest-confirm-port.ts) name the jobs.
- No lint rule kept core free of adapters. [`no-core-adapters`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/scripts/oxlint-plugin-boundaries.ts) rejects HTTP-client and adapter/vendor imports from core, with [failing-case tests](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/test/boundaries-rule.test.ts).

[Cartridges](/lore/cartridges) adds rat-stack's own packaging and removal test, including infrastructure supplied through `Layer.provide`. [A Layer as constructor](/lore/layer-constructor-pattern) explains the construction mechanism.

# /lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect

Source: .brain/resources/lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect.svx
SHA-256: 8b6823c2ef908edbf3b40edc43b865aa33a330e1cc139b796195728104a9d962

# Effect keeps the surfaces on one contract

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

An Effect Schema defines accepted values and provides types and runtime checks.
Our shared contract describes one action's input, output, failures, and metadata.
Effect Schema owns inputs, outputs, and failures in our shared [`contract`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/contract.ts). [`implement.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/implement.ts) binds the handler and its approval requirement.

A projection builds an interface from a capability, a named action with a contract and handler.
The HTTP projection creates an Effect HttpApi. Other projections create CLI commands and an AI toolkit from the same contracts.

[`apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts) and [`apps/site/src/app.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/app.ts) supply implementations with Layers.

## Follow one interface at a time

- [MCP is another surface](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface): discover and call the toolkit over the protocol.
- [OpenAPI describes the refusal too](/lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too): derive the HTTP document and declare the bodyless decode failure.
- [One schema, three surfaces](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces): project the contract instead of maintaining three schemas.
- [Schemas define the boundary](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary): decode unknown values and keep domain refusals typed.
- [One program can replace several tool calls](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls): combine content capabilities without widening their authority.

## Layer supplies the job

[`packages/core/src/join-intake.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/join-intake.ts) builds a `Layer.effect(JoinInterest, ...)`. It captures the ticket, scoring, events, contact store, delivery, and token services. It then returns the submission method.

Source: [`packages/core/src/join-intake.ts` at `b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c`, lines 55–69](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c/packages/core/src/join-intake.ts#L55-L69).

packages/core/src/join-intake.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 55-69; highlighted none.

```typescript
export const joinIntakeLayer = Layer.effect(
  JoinInterest,
  Effect.gen(function* makeJoinIntake() {
    const tickets = yield* IntakeTicket;

    const tokens = yield* InterestTokens;
    const crypto = yield* Crypto.Crypto;

      input: JoinInput

      const statusRef = yield* newStatusRef;
```

Effect's [`Layer.provide`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/effect/src/Layer.ts) supplies a Layer's dependencies. [`HttpApiBuilder.layer`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/effect/src/http-api/HttpApiBuilder.ts) registers HTTP routes and can expose OpenAPI. Neither requires a second domain handler.

[One capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) states the house rule. [Hexagonal architecture](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) names the adapter boundary. [The fence](/lore/the-fence) enforces it.

The [peers](/resources/same-version-repos) page records other Effect and Alchemy projects, whose designs can differ.

Start with [Effect basics](/lore/effect-basics), then [construct a service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) and [compose its Layers](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit).

See also: [Structure an Effect codebase by domain](/lore/structure-effect-by-domain).

# /lore/http-responses-need-validation

Source: .brain/resources/lore/http-responses-need-validation.svx
SHA-256: d5e62b975b2d31ea10830b2fef755e95ee3a5cd858de2b5e82676ca11a057dee

# HTTP success needs a status check and a decoder

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Schema defines accepted values and checks data at runtime.
An adapter implements an application interface for a provider.

A fulfilled HTTP request is not proof of application success.
Check the status and decode the body before passing provider data into the application.
Use the `effect/http` modules.

## Check the protocol response

The deployment checker decodes tool discovery through `ToolsResponse`.
It also requires status 200 and the expected tool names.

packages/deploy/src/checks.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 600-609; highlighted none.

```typescript
          const document =
            yield* HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(ToolsResponse)(response);

          return (
            response.status === 200 &&
            ["search", "read", "execute"].every((name) =>
              document.result.tools.some((tool) => tool.name === name)
            )
          );
        })
```

Use the in-memory fixture below when learning.

## Reject an unacceptable response before trusting its data

`HttpClient.filterStatusOk` accepts 2xx status codes.
An adapter can require a narrower status when its protocol needs one.
The fixture applies the filter before decoding a version response.

packages/deploy/test/fixtures/validated-http-response.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 13-30; highlighted none.

```typescript
    const client = (yield* HttpClient.HttpClient).pipe(
      HttpClient.filterStatusOk
    );

    const response = yield* client
      .get("https://provider.example.test/version")
      .pipe(
        Effect.mapError(
          (cause) => new ResponseFixtureError({ cause, phase: "status" })
        )
      );

    return yield* HttpClientResponse.schemaBodyJson(Reply)(response).pipe(
      Effect.mapError(
        (cause) => new ResponseFixtureError({ cause, phase: "body" })
      )
    );
  }
```

`schemaBodyJson` handles JSON parsing and schema decoding. `ResponseFixtureError` retains the cause and names the failed phase.

The fixture groups request and status failures into its `status` phase.
It groups parsing and schema failures into its `body` phase.
A production adapter should choose failure names that match its job and repair path.

## Supply the transport in tests

The test supplies a client that creates responses in memory.
It does not start an HTTP server or call a provider.

packages/deploy/test/http-response.test.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 15-30; highlighted none.

```typescript
      Effect.sync(() =>
        HttpClientResponse.fromWeb(
          request,
          new Response(scenario.body, {
            headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
            status: scenario.status,
          })
        )
      )
    );

    const result = yield* readValidatedResponse().pipe(
      Effect.provideService(HttpClient.HttpClient, client),
      Effect.result
    );

```

- **200, integer version**: Decoded version
- **503, otherwise valid body**: Named status-phase failure
- **200, malformed JSON**: Named body-phase failure
- **200, string instead of integer**: Named body-phase failure

These tests of the HTTP client interface establish the fixture's status and decoding policy.
Check live endpoint health separately.

## Decide whether replay is safe before adding retries

A transient failure may be temporary. `retryTransient` can retry transient responses and errors.
Its classification does not prove that repeating an operation is safe.
A write can complete remotely even when its response is lost.

Before retrying a write:

1. Identify the operation's replay or idempotency guarantee: whether repeating it can create a second change.
2. Decide which failures allow another attempt.
3. Measure the [retry budget](/lore/retry-load-needs-a-budget), the allowed attempts or time, and select the schedule.
4. Preserve the final named failure when the budget ends.

Do not copy example delays or retry counts into production as measured limits.
The fixture establishes no production retry budget.

## Common mistakes

- Treat fulfilled fetch as success despite a failed status.
- Trust an object because JSON parsing succeeded.
- Replace the whole adapter in a test and stop exercising its decoder.
- Retry a write only because the transport calls its error transient.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Supply `HttpClient`, compose request policies, decode responses, and translate failures at the adapter's interface with the provider.
- In rat-stack, core owns service interfaces named for application jobs. Provider clients remain in adapters under [hexagonal architecture](/lore/hexagonal-architecture).
- In rat-stack, [machines own finite retry lifecycles](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines). Effect also has native schedules and retry operators.

Read [schemas](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) and [failures](/lore/error-model) before defining the adapter's accepted data.
Then read [tracing](/lore/trace-meaningful-operations) to observe the operation without exposing private values.
Return to the [Effect reading order](/lore/effect-basics#read-next).

# /lore/infrastructure-as-effects

Source: .brain/resources/lore/infrastructure-as-effects.svx
SHA-256: b4e9193ebd2727523f3a8351376c2be484e4dd49a472598374aa546c7cc01736

# Infrastructure as effects

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

<picture>
<source media="(max-width: 640px)" srcset="/lore/infrastructure-as-effects/portrait.svg" width="600" height="1290" />
<img src="/lore/infrastructure-as-effects/landscape.svg" width="1200" height="720" alt="One Effect program holds three lanes. A contract projects to command line, HTTP, MCP tools, browser RPC and code mode. Code requires bindings, which declare resources. Plan, review and deploy run in order. The compiler checks these relationships before deployment." />
</picture>

Sam relates runtime clients, business logic, infrastructure policies, and deployed resources in [one typed program](/lore/cafe-stack).
The compiler can check these relationships before deployment.

## Contract → surfaces

A [contract](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) defines shared input, output, failures, and metadata.
Projections turn registered capabilities into command line, HTTP, MCP tools, browser RPC, and code mode surfaces.
Each surface derives its input and failure definitions from the same schemas.

## Code → bindings → resources

A client operation can imply a policy requirement supplied when the function is built.
Sam describes [bindings](/lore/bindings) as permissions and environment variables together at [37:09](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=2229).
An Alchemy Layer can declare the cloud resources behind a service.
The [Stack](/lore/effect-office-hours-27-alchemy-infrastructure-as-effects) declares cloud resources.

## Worked example: a D1 Layer

In the database [cartridge](/lore/cartridges), `makeD1Vendor` declares SQLite migrations and a D1 database.
The database declaration receives those migrations through its `migrations` option.

packages/database/src/d1.ts at c5e4fc13d7740952fcb1646b29a5cdd1b43001a8; lines 17-29; highlighted none. Title: Declare the schema and database.

```typescript
const makeD1Vendor = Effect.fn("makeD1Vendor")(function* makeD1Vendor({
  id,
}: D1Options) {
  const migrations = yield* Drizzle.Schema(`${id}-d1-schema`, {
    dialect: "sqlite",
    out: databaseMigrationDirectory("d1"),
    schema: databaseSchemaFile("d1"),
  });

  const database = yield* Cloudflare.D1.Database(`${id}-d1`, { migrations });

  return { _tag: "D1" as const, database };
});
```

`D1(options)` builds the Layer below.
It combines `RunLogLayer(vendor)` with the `DatabaseVendor` service and provides `QueryDatabaseBinding`.
The package keeps its database declaration and service construction together.

packages/database/src/d1.ts at c5e4fc13d7740952fcb1646b29a5cdd1b43001a8; lines 34-44; highlighted none. Title: Compose services and supply the query binding.

```typescript
export const D1 = (options: D1Options) =>
  Layer.unwrap(
    Effect.gen(function* buildD1Layer() {
      const vendor = yield* makeD1Vendor(options);

      return Layer.mergeAll(
        RunLogLayer(vendor),
        Layer.succeed(DatabaseVendor, vendor)
      );
    })
  ).pipe(Layer.provide(Cloudflare.D1.QueryDatabaseBinding));
```

Trace the declaration first, then the returned Layer.
Read [Database](/systems/database) for its current callers and local verification commands.

## Plan → review → deploy

A [plan model](/lore/plan-model) describes infrastructure changes before they apply.
Sam connects Effect purity with a reviewable plan and a concrete deployment result at [12:22](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=742).
Tests using real infrastructure check behavior after deployment at [16:01](https://youtu.be/fPSxB7ZgSJw?t=961).

## The compiler checks the joins

[Effect](/lore/context-and-requirements) tracks required services in its type.
Effects and Layers let the type system track the resource providers a Stack needs at [07:01](https://youtu.be/fPSxB7ZgSJw?t=421).
Sam describes a type error when code still requires a removed binding at [15:25](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=925).
The compiler can check these relationships before deployment: [Happy Path 116, 28:00](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=1680).

## Cartridges

A [cartridge](/lore/cartridges) is a package that owns one job and the resources it needs.
Replacing its Layer changes the implementation and dependencies without changing callers.

## Lifecycles

Use an [XState machine](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines) for named states, retries, cancellation, or a lifecycle to resume or inspect.
Model the states and the events that move between them.

## The fence

The [fence](/lore/the-fence) is the compiler checks, lint rules, tests, and hooks that enforce project rules.
These rules cannot establish whole-program behavior.

## Cloud as a library

Sam's phrase is that [the whole cloud becomes a library](/lore/cloud-as-a-library), at [29:50](https://youtu.be/MtKHzAH6uXM?t=1790).
He argues that infrastructure tools can retain application-code properties such as debugging and tests at [03:50](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=230).

## The joins at a glance

- **Contract → surfaces**:
  - What the program checks: Shared input and failure schemas
  - Where to read more: [One capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface)
- **Code → bindings → resources**:
  - What the program checks: Required services and resource providers
  - Where to read more: [Bindings](/lore/bindings) · [Infrastructure as Effects, Office Hours 27](/lore/effect-office-hours-27-alchemy-infrastructure-as-effects)
- **Plan → review → deploy**:
  - What the program checks: Changes before application; real-infrastructure behavior after deployment
  - Where to read more: [Plan model](/lore/plan-model)
- **Compiler → joins**:
  - What the program checks: Relationships before deployment; code that requires a removed binding
  - Where to read more: [Happy Path 116](/lore/happy-path-116-infrastructure-as-effects-sam-goodwin)
- **Cartridges**:
  - What the program checks: Removal leaves no loose resources or broken imports
  - Where to read more: [Cartridges](/lore/cartridges)
- **Lifecycles**:
  - What the program checks: Named states and the events between them
  - Where to read more: [Lifecycles are machines](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines)
- **Fence**:
  - What the program checks: Project rules; whole-program behavior remains outside these checks
  - Where to read more: [The fence](/lore/the-fence)
- **Cloud as a library**:
  - What the program checks: Debugging and tests for infrastructure code
  - Where to read more: [Cloud as a library](/lore/cloud-as-a-library)

# /lore/init-runs-twice

Source: .brain/resources/lore/init-runs-twice.svx
SHA-256: 49af0999ee0ca1fb443be954bd63f7c010890670400e3717eacff6098fd3f5a9

# Worker init runs twice

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A Cloudflare Worker's initialization effect runs twice. It runs when Alchemy declares deploy-time resources and when the Worker starts in an isolate, a separate execution environment. Those contexts do not have the same services.

On 2026-09-24, stage-specific rate-limit declarations used `yield* Stage` in the Worker initializer. The runtime did not have that deploy-time service, so production returned error 1101 for about three minutes.

The first change, [commit 95687ec](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/95687ec906a6b4cde99a5b8e5df77115695833a8), added stage-specific rate-limit namespaces but evaluated them during Worker initialization. [A revert](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/9da5f9d) backed it out; [commit 6e85432](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/6e85432034400df8e49a9354a4cab1246d7cece0) fixed it by declaring the resources only when `globalThis.__ALCHEMY_RUNTIME__ !== true`. The check now surrounds the rate-limit declarations and WorkerLoader declaration; the request-serving handler remains available at runtime.

`apps/site/src/worker.ts` shows the boundary. `apps/site/test/worker-runtime-init.test.ts` sets the runtime flag and provides only runtime bindings. It starts the worker and checks that a request returns 404 rather than crashing.

Put 95687ec's unguarded declarations back and the test fails with `Service not found: Stage`, the same failure production hit. Every earlier check exercised only the deploy side. [Merge commit ae312a1](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/ae312a13e91c395a97404a565871d7a96de11388) carries the fix into the merged branch.

See [cartridges](/lore/cartridges) for the rule that each resource belongs to its Layer and [the fence](/lore/the-fence) for the required tests that check this separation.

# Lauren Tan's skills

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Lauren Tan (poteto) ships skills across four repos. Her talk on verification and skills is on [Lauren Tan](/lore/lauren-tan) and [the Dune talk](/lore/poteto-lauren-tan-2500-prs-dune).

**[brainmaxxing](https://github.com/poteto/brainmaxxing/blob/ec4d8e43dee639d6f5d94aed3ca16af7b298ecfc/README.md)** is "stupid simple persistent memory for Claude Code". The agent reads its folder of Markdown memory files at session start and writes to it when it learns something. It ships 16 starter principles and six skills. `brain` supplies the vault workflow; `plan` and `review` support structured work.

Three form a learning loop:

- **`reflect`**: After sessions.
- **`ruminate`**: Over past conversations.
- **`meditate`**: Audit and prune.

The README says `/reflect` alone gets you most of the value. [Skills](https://github.com/poteto/brainmaxxing/tree/ec4d8e43dee639d6f5d94aed3ca16af7b298ecfc/.agents/skills)

**[noodle](https://github.com/poteto/noodle/blob/82d2921c52370f23f29086de81ccfb600939c037/INSTALL.md)** is "skill-based agent orchestration," built in Go. You write skills as markdown files. Noodle's loop schedules and runs them.

It adds one field to skill frontmatter, `schedule`. A skill with it becomes autonomous. The scheduler reads its value as prose. The minimum loop is a schedule skill and an execute skill.

The repo's [own skills](https://github.com/poteto/noodle/tree/82d2921c52370f23f29086de81ccfb600939c037/.agents/skills) include `adversarial-review`, `quality`, `execute`, and `schedule`.

**[how](https://github.com/poteto/how/blob/b1ef42969ea7a2bb50aa26c2480274828a0385e7/README.md)** is a Cursor plugin with one skill, `/how`. It explains how a subsystem or flow works. Critique mode runs critics across different models. For complex questions, it runs parallel explorer subagents and reconciles their findings.

**[verification-skill-example](https://github.com/poteto/verification-skill-example/blob/d5abe70d0d8c671672b6cef4069363f26c488feb/README.md)** is a fictionalized example of a project-local verification skill with a list of features and checks that verify their behavior. About 30 files cover one feature area each. Its README argues that a wiki is for humans. Agents pay for every token they reread.

It argues that a scoped skill plus feature map is cheaper to use and maintained as code. The README calls it a private reference and says the driver scripts are omitted.

Related: [Matt Pocock's skills](/lore/matt-pocock-skills).

# /lore/layer-constructor-pattern

Source: .brain/resources/lore/layer-constructor-pattern.svx
SHA-256: 8fea90d166dd2910f5c5ff6b28b65cb54e25e725b0facefd46508637c3d58c22

# A Layer as constructor

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

**Goal:** write a [Layer](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) the way you would write a class constructor.

A Layer describes how to build a [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) and supply its dependencies.
A service is the named [interface](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces) callers use for a job.

## Worked example: a journal with private state

`FlagJournal` records flag changes.
Its `memory` Layer is a constructor:

packages/core/src/flag-journal.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 34-41; highlighted 38,40. Title: Ref.make is a field; FlagJournal.of is the method table.

```typescript
>()("@rat-stack/core/FlagJournal") {
  static memory = Layer.effect(
    FlagJournal,
    Effect.gen(function* makeFlagJournal() {
      const entries = yield* Ref.make<readonly FlagChange[]>([]);

      return FlagJournal.of({
        list: Effect.fn("FlagJournal.list")(function* list(input) {
```

Read it as a class:

- `Layer.effect(FlagJournal, …)` is the constructor for `FlagJournal`.
- `Ref.make([])` creates a private field. Only the returned methods can reach `entries`.
- `FlagJournal.of({ … })` returns the methods, checked against the service interface.

Each build of the Layer runs the constructor once and creates a fresh `entries` list.

## One service, two constructors

A class can have more than one constructor. A service can have more than one Layer.
`Drift` checks pinned code excerpts against the current source:

packages/code-snippets/src/drift.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 23-31; highlighted 24,28,31. Title: silent needs nothing; layer needs SourceRepository.

```typescript
>()("code-snippets/Drift") {
  static readonly silent = Layer.succeed(
    Drift,
    Drift.of({ check: () => Effect.succeed([]) })
  );
  static readonly layer = Layer.effect(
    Drift,
    Effect.gen(function* makeDrift() {
      const repository = yield* SourceRepository;
```

- `Drift.silent` uses `Layer.succeed`. It needs nothing and reports nothing.
- `Drift.layer` uses `Layer.effect`. Its constructor asks for `SourceRepository`, so the Layer carries that [requirement](/lore/effect-basics).

Callers ask for `Drift` either way. The [composition root](/lore/structure-effect-by-domain) picks the constructor.

## Why it matters

A constructor argument becomes a Layer requirement. The type shows it, and the root must supply it.

Sam compares the constructor pattern to a Layer and uses a React component as an analogy. In the same discussion, he connects the pattern to infrastructure policies. [Watch from 18:45](https://youtu.be/MtKHzAH6uXM?t=1125)

## Next

Read [Layers make dependencies explicit](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) to compose several Layers.
Then read [why dependency injection matters](/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect).

See [Sam Goodwin on Alchemy](/lore/devtools-fm-sam-goodwin-alchemy) and [cartridges](/lore/cartridges).

# /lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit

Source: .brain/resources/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit.svx
SHA-256: b19032544400e871aae9979fc153db80ed1de849adc891170348c80db80a1d8f

# Layer composition makes dependencies explicit

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A service is a named interface. A Layer describes how to build a service from other services.
Choose and supply the services and their dependencies before running the application. Keep dependencies private unless callers need them too.

## Supply dependencies without changing the domain

`FileInspector.layer` needs a filesystem implementation.
`NodeServices.layer` supplies platform services. The CLI combines them before execution.

apps/cli/src/cli.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 22-35; highlighted none.

```typescript
  Effect.provide(
    Layer.mergeAll(
      Layer.provideMerge(FileInspector.layer, NodeServices.layer),
      remoteJoinInterestLayer,
      localPromptLibraryLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(NodeServices.layer)),
      localCafeDirectoryLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(NodeServices.layer)),
      localLearnLayer,
      Flags.defaults(eventFlags),
      Approval.denyAll
    )
  )
);

NodeRuntime.runMain(program);
```

Choose the combinator by the services the resulting Layer should expose:

- **`Layer.provide(dependency)`**: The consuming Layer's services
- **`Layer.provideMerge(dependency)`**: The consuming Layer's services and the dependency's services
- **`Layer.merge` or `mergeAll`**: The combined services; unrelated requirements remain unresolved

Merging services does not, by itself, feed one Layer into another Layer's requirements.

The test suite retains platform services with `provideMerge` because tests also create temporary files.
Production callers that need only the inspector can keep its implementation dependency private with `provide`.

## Reuse Layer identity when sharing construction

Sharing follows Layer identity within a build context that remembers which Layer values it has already constructed. Equivalent construction code does not make two Layer values identical.
Sharing is limited to that construction context.

The fixture gives two consumers a resource. One case shares a Layer value; the other calls the Layer factory again.

packages/core/test/layer-composition.test.ts at 72306d84e9b57f068f8e293c0d2f0c7b934338e1; lines 16-23; highlighted none.

```typescript
      const resource = Resource.layer();

      const graph = Layer.merge(
        ReadAccess.layer.pipe(Layer.provide(resource)),
        WriteAccess.layer.pipe(
          Layer.provide(shared ? resource : Resource.layer())
        )
      );
```

`Resource.layer()` creates a new Layer value. Reusing `resource` lets the two branches share construction.

The fixture counts constructions and compares service ids:

packages/core/test/layer-composition.test.ts at 72306d84e9b57f068f8e293c0d2f0c7b934338e1; lines 25-32; highlighted none.

```typescript
      const ids = yield* Effect.gen(function* readServiceIds() {
        return [yield* ReadAccess, yield* WriteAccess];
      }).pipe(Effect.provide(graph));

      const count = yield* ConstructionCount;

      expect(yield* Ref.get(count)).toBe(constructions);
      expect(ids[0] === ids[1]).toBe(shared);
```

Independent application runtimes do not share instances merely because they import the same Layer value.
Their construction context and memo-map lifetime matter too.

## Common wrong approach

Calling a Layer factory twice can create two pools, caches, or background workers when one shared instance was intended.
Keep the constructed Layer value and provide that same value to both consumers.

Do not use `provideMerge` everywhere to silence missing-service errors.
Read which services callers need. Retaining every dependency exposes implementation details and makes removal harder.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Layers carry output services, construction failures, and input requirements. Composition resolves the requirements.
- In rat-stack, each entrypoint, where the application starts, chooses and supplies implementations in its composition root.
- A cartridge packages one job and its infrastructure. It must be removable without breaking unrelated packages.
- The application chooses its workspace layout and adapter package boundaries.

See also: [service construction](/lore/services-capture-dependencies), [domain structure](/lore/structure-effect-by-domain), [cartridges](/lore/cartridges), and [testing](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

Read [why dependency injection matters](/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect).

# /lore/lifecycles-are-machines

Source: .brain/resources/lore/lifecycles-are-machines.svx
SHA-256: 2b097afb39a77dea1ceec9e194f981a8aa769cd21ac5e82649ec0f5dcaa9dcd3

# Lifecycles are machines

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

**Goal:** move a lifecycle out of boolean flags and into named states, with side effects in declared actors.

A machine is a definition of named states and the events that move between them. Use an XState machine for the application's named states, retries, cancellation, or a lifecycle you need to resume or inspect.
Model the states and the events that move between them instead of accumulating booleans whose combinations have no meaning.

An actor is a running unit that performs declared work.
A side effect is work outside the state description, such as reading a file.
A [Scope](/lore/scopes-own-resources) owns cleanup when that work ends.

## Worked example: inspecting a file

`packages/core/src/inspect-machine.ts` is the working example.
It reads a file and ends in one of two final states.

### 1. Declare the side effect as an actor

packages/core/src/inspect-machine.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 27-31; highlighted none. Title: readStats is the only code that touches the file.

```typescript
const readStats = createEffectLogic({
  effect: ({ input }) =>
    FileInspector.use((inspector) => inspector.inspect(input.path)),
  schemas: { input: Schema.Struct({ path: Schema.String }) },
});
```

`createEffectLogic` defines an Effect-backed side effect with an input [Schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary).

### 2. Let the machine choose transitions

packages/core/src/inspect-machine.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 41-64; highlighted 45-47,52,58. Title: reading invokes readStats, then lands in a final state.

```typescript
  initial: "reading",
  output: ({ context }) => context.outcome,
  states: {
    inspected: { type: "final" },
    reading: {
      invoke: {
        input: ({ context }) => ({ path: context.path }),
        onDone: {
          context: ({ event }) => ({
            outcome: inspectOutcome.Inspected({ stats: event.output }),
          }),
          target: "inspected",
        },
        onError: {
          context: ({ event }) => ({
            outcome: inspectOutcome.Unreadable({ cause: event.error.cause }),
          }),
          target: "unreadable",
        },
        src: "readStats",
      },
    },
    unreadable: { type: "final" },
  },
```

`setupEffect` declares actors. The machine invokes `readStats` by name in the `reading` state.
The machine chooses transitions and records its outcome. The invoked actor performs the file read.

A read failure lands in `unreadable` with its cause. The failure is a state you can test.

### 3. Start it inside Effect and wait for the outcome

packages/core/src/inspect-machine.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 67-70; highlighted 69-70. Title: createEffectActor starts it; watchActor reports it.

```typescript
export const runInspectMachine = Effect.fn("runInspectMachine")(
  function* runInspectMachine(path: string) {
    const actor = yield* createEffectActor(inspectMachine, { input: { path } });
    yield* watchActor("inspectMachine", actor);
```

`createEffectActor` starts the machine inside Effect's scope. `watchActor` makes the run visible to devtools.
`join` waits for the final outcome. `Effect.orDie` treats a machine-level failure as a programming error. The domain read failure remains an explicit machine state.

## Why a machine

Two booleans, `loading` and `failed`, allow four combinations. Only three of them mean anything here.
This machine has exactly three states: `reading`, `inspected`, and `unreadable`.

The [fence](/lore/the-fence) keeps side effects in declared actors. `oxlint.config.ts` loads the lint plugin that `@xstate/effect` ships and sets `xstate-effect/no-inline-effect` to `error`.

That rule matches two cases. It flags an Effect returned from an inline `enq` or `enqueue` callback. It flags inline Effect logic passed to `enq.spawn`. [Rule source](https://unpkg.com/@xstate/effect@1.0.0-beta.0/dist/xstate-effect-oxlint.js)

The stack pins XState `6.0.0-beta.1` and `@xstate/effect` `1.0.0-beta.0` together.
The [migration note](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/.brain/archives/resources/xstate-alpha69-migration.svx#beta1-and-bridge-beta0) records the beta API changes and persistence audit.

## Next

Use [the add-a-lifecycle-machine skill](/skills/add-a-lifecycle-machine) to build one.

See [one capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) for how a capability can own a machine and [the fence](/lore/the-fence) for the rule that protects it.

A machine in memory ends with its process. [Restart must reconstruct known state](/lore/restart-from-known-state) and [supervision chooses what restarts](/lore/supervision-is-a-recovery-policy) cover recovery.

# Matt Pocock's skills

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[mattpocock/skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) describes itself this way:

> "my agent skills that I use every day to do real engineering - not vibe coding."

The README says the skills are "designed to be small, easy to adapt, and composable," and work with any model. It invites you to hack around with them and make them your own. [README](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60/README.md)

The README organizes them around four failure modes. When an agent misses your intent, it prescribes a question-and-answer session to clarify intent: [`grill-me`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60/skills/productivity/grill-me/SKILL.md) for non-code work and [`grill-with-docs`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60/skills/engineering/grill-with-docs/SKILL.md).

`grill-with-docs` also builds a shared language in `GLOSSARY.md` and architecture decision records (ADRs).

For code that doesn't work it points to feedback loops, with [`tdd`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60/skills/engineering/tdd/SKILL.md) and [`diagnosing-bugs`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60/skills/engineering/diagnosing-bugs/SKILL.md). For code with tangled responsibilities it points to [`improve-codebase-architecture`](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/d81f3a183412e71a5b1e84ca21bc1a35eea03a60/skills/engineering/improve-codebase-architecture/SKILL.md).

The reference section splits the skills by whether the user or agent starts them. User-invoked skills run only when you type them. The agent can also select model-invoked skills automatically. It lists engineering and productivity groups, including `to-spec`, `to-tickets`, `implement`, `triage`, `handoff`, and `writing-for-agents`.

There are two ways to install. The Claude Code plugin installs the set as a managed, read-only bundle that updates when Matt ships. The `npx skills@latest add mattpocock/skills` installer copies editable files into your project. The README says to pick one.

Run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` once per repo to set the issue tracker, triage labels, and doc locations.

Related: [Lauren Tan's skills](/lore/lauren-tan-skills).

# /lore/mcp-is-another-surface

Source: .brain/resources/lore/mcp-is-another-surface.svx

# MCP is another surface

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

The Model Context Protocol lets an agent client discover and call tools. The [tools specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools) defines:

- `tools/list` for discovery.
- `tools/call` for calling a tool.
- Input JSON Schema.
- Optional output JSON Schema.

A client that speaks MCP can discover names and arguments without learning a separate call format. In rat-stack, MCP [projects the shared handler](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces).

## The projection

[`packages/capability/src/to-toolkit.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/to-toolkit.ts) turns contracts into Effect tools. It projects input, output, failure, and annotations.

[`apps/site/src/app.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/app.ts):

- Supplies the toolkit to `McpServer.toolkit`.
- Serves it at [/mcp](/mcp).
- Serves public documents as resources.
- Serves skills as prompts.

## The application tool is the same job

[`apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts) includes `joinInterest` in the hosted toolkit. Its [contract](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/src/join-interest-contract.ts) requires contact consent, a page ticket, and the approved card. The same requirements apply over MCP.

The HTTP alternative is `POST /api/joinInterest`. The [first observed application](/lore/two-lines-of-curl-is-a-front-door) uses that route without fetching MCP. The job does not need a protocol-specific handler.

Use [code mode](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls) to combine content calls. It does not expose `joinInterest` inside the sandbox.

See [how we do it with Effect](/lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect) for the whole path.

# /lore/mdsvex-left-unified

Source: .brain/resources/lore/mdsvex-left-unified.svx

# mdsvex left unified

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

mdsvex compiles Markdown with Svelte components. unified processes documents through plugins.
remark processes Markdown, and rehype processes HTML.

CommonMark specifies Markdown syntax. GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) adds features to that syntax.

In [Discussion #259](https://github.com/pngwn/MDsveX/discussions/259), pngwn gives four reasons to leave unified:

- Performance.
- API instability.
- Poor documentation.
- Possible changes to allowed syntax extensions.

The new parser uses its own plugin system instead of remark and rehype plugins.

[Penguin-flavoured markdown](https://github.com/pngwn/MDsveX/discussions/293), or PFM, also changes syntax. On [Reddit, as evilpingwin](https://www.reddit.com/r/sveltejs/comments/15rz6al/thoughts_on_mdsvex_moving_away_from_unified/), pngwn says GFM's features remain supported. The syntax is not always identical. He promises an automated migration path.

## Where we stopped

Our local check of published `mdsvex@1.0.0-next.0` stops on this minimal CommonMark input:

```markdown
- **`x`** x
- y
```

The published migrator converts it to PFM:

```text
- *`x`* x
- y
```

PFM uses one asterisk for strong text; CommonMark uses two.

The next.0 check gives these results:

- The compiler prints `Infinite loop detected`.
- The second list item disappears.
- The parser reports zero errors.
- A supplied rehype plugin is never called.

These results cover the published `1.0.0-next.0` prerelease only. We keep 0.12.8. [The fence](/lore/the-fence) does not permit rewriting valid prose around a parser defect.

## The migrator still uses remark

The [published migrator](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mdsvex/migrate/0.2.0-next.0) depends on `unified`, `remark-parse`, and `remark-gfm`. The new renderer leaves that ecosystem. The migration into it still reads CommonMark with remark.

## Sources

1. [v1 early feedback](https://github.com/pngwn/MDsveX/discussions/259)
   GitHub. v1 early feedback Accessed 2026-10-02.

2. [evilpingwin on syntax and migration](https://www.reddit.com/r/sveltejs/comments/15rz6al/thoughts_on_mdsvex_moving_away_from_unified/)
   Primary source. evilpingwin on syntax and migration Accessed 2026-10-02.

3. [Penguin-flavoured markdown](https://github.com/pngwn/MDsveX/discussions/293)
   GitHub. Penguin-flavoured markdown Accessed 2026-10-02.

4. [Published compiler used in the local reproduction](https://registry.npmjs.org/mdsvex/1.0.0-next.0)
   npm. Published compiler used in the local reproduction Accessed 2026-10-02.

5. [Published migrator dependencies](https://registry.npmjs.org/@mdsvex/migrate/0.2.0-next.0)
   npm. Published migrator dependencies Accessed 2026-10-02.

# Michael Arnaldi

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Dependency injection supplies service implementations to callers.
Resource safety means cleaning up resources after use. Concurrency control manages work that runs at the same time.

Michael traces Effect to a TypeScript team's needs for dependency injection, reliable tests, resource safety, concurrency control, and retries. [Effect Days 2024, 08:40](https://youtu.be/7sJc3Z4mh1w?t=520).

He describes Effect computations through their outputs, predictable failures, and requirements: the services the work needs. [Happy Path 81, 49:15](https://youtu.be/gc5P36t6kD0?t=2955).

# /lore/model-based-testing

Source: .brain/resources/lore/model-based-testing.svx
SHA-256: 4ec69c1a5b3833e0cd523288ba43d6dca220b6299d4722c3d3def9f7e6698ec6

# Model-based testing

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Model-based testing describes expected behavior as a small model. It generates action sequences and compares the real system with the model after each step.
It suits anything with history: sessions, retries, lifecycles.

[David Khourshid](/lore/david-khourshid) described the approach with state machines in [Model-Based Testing in React with State Machines](https://css-tricks.com/model-based-testing-in-react-with-state-machines/). XState builds it into `xstate/graph`: `createTestModel` wraps a machine, and `getShortestPaths` turns it into test paths. "Path generation enables model-based testing - generating test cases directly from your state machine." [Graph & Paths](https://stately.ai/docs/graph)

Effect 4's `Arbitrary.array` generates command sequences. Its documentation uses a state machine as the example, and failed sequences shrink: the generator removes irrelevant commands to reduce the failing sequence. [Arbitrary.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Arbitrary.ts)

In rat-stack, [the visitor identity model](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/events/test/visitor.model.test.ts) generates visits from three devices.
Visits may keep or drop the cookie. Visits also cross day boundaries.

A persistent id survives every visit that keeps its cookie. A daily id stays stable within a day and sets no cookie.
It never repeats on a later day. Making the daily hash ignore the day broke the model at once.

Machines in this repo are [lifecycles](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines), so each one is a ready-made test model. See [property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) for single-input rules.

See also: [Tests through supplied services](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place) and [recovery needs model tests](/lore/recovery-needs-model-tests).

## Sources

1. [Model-Based Testing in React with State Machines](https://css-tricks.com/model-based-testing-in-react-with-state-machines/)
   David Khourshid · CSS-Tricks. Testing article; used for checking action sequences against a model. Accessed 2026-10-01.

2. [Graph & Paths](https://stately.ai/docs/graph)

# /lore/no-comments

Source: .brain/resources/lore/no-comments.svx
SHA-256: 4571682c4578cbe397f42a5410d7362f3b0e24983c75fc22c1d1c2bb548f4690

# No comments

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

The code rule bans prose comments because agents copy them, and a comment that explains a workaround can spread the workaround. Put the reason where the code can enforce or reveal it: in a name, a type, a test, a commit message, or the project's `.brain/` notes.

Three forms remain. Tool directives can suppress a specific diagnostic with a reason after `--`, as in `// oxlint-disable-next-line rule -- reason`. A one-line `SAFETY:` statement above a type assertion names the condition that must remain true to make it safe.

Plain JavaScript can keep JSDoc blocks made only of type tags, because those tags provide type syntax. TypeScript's comment directives also need an inline reason, and the configured lint rule decides which directives may stay.

Before running `pnpm fix`, move each comment's reason into a symbol, type, test, commit, or `.brain/` note. `--fix` can delete prose comments and leave the workaround behind.

See [the fence](/lore/the-fence) for how the rule is enforced and [tests that earn their place](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place) for the test that can replace a comment.

# /lore/old-events-must-still-decode

Source: .brain/resources/lore/old-events-must-still-decode.svx
SHA-256: e4e75b43d8ac09976f091062b45700409da25d58d83be038705c284ea9ee245f

# Old events must still decode

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Historical records remain useful only while consumers can translate their versions. A deployment can break recovery without changing newly produced data.

> Schema evolution ensures that the consumer can translate it to a familiar version.

Source: [Q12](/lore/durability-bibliography#q12); [B5](/lore/durability-bibliography#b5-building-event-driven-microservices), [B14](/lore/durability-bibliography#b14-refactoring-databases).

## Failure it prevents

A new consumer cannot decode already-accepted work.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Schema.decodeUnknownEffect` validates a representation. Define supported versions and transformations; the decoder does not choose the compatibility policy.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Schema.ts`, `packages/effect/src/persistence/PersistedQueue.ts`.

## How to check

Keep old payload fixtures. Decode and restore them with the proposed consumer before removing old representations. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Shared schemas need a transition period](/lore/schema-changes-need-a-transition), [Replay needs stable inputs](/lore/replay-needs-stable-inputs).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Bellemare, Adam. Building Event-Driven Microservices: Leveraging Organizational Data at Scale. O’Reilly, 2020.](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/building-event-driven-microservices/9781492057888/)
   O’Reilly. Chapter 3 Communication and Data Contracts; Chapter 6 Deterministic Stream Processing; Chapter 7 Stateful Streaming; Chapter 9 Microservices Using Function-as-a-Service; Chapter 14 Supportive Tooling. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Ambler, Scott W.; Sadalage, Pramod J. Refactoring Databases: Evolutionary Database Design. Addison-Wesley, 2006.](https://www.amazon.com/Refactoring-Databases-Evolutionary-paperback-Addison-Wesley/dp/0321774515)
   Addison-Wesley. §3.11 What You Have Learned (transition period); Chapter 4 Deploying into Production. Accessed 2026-10-23.

3. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. Schema.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/one-capability-every-surface

Source: .brain/resources/lore/one-capability-every-surface.svx
SHA-256: fa4e675010473ff0a881541e9b1fee0c48e72158d6f0ac0f5f0b2fb89d776f35

# One capability, every surface

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

**Goal:** add one action and get a command, an HTTP route, an [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface) tool, and a code-mode function from it. Browser [RPC](/skills/learn-rat-stack) uses the same contracts; `search` and `read` show that side.

A capability is one named action with a [contract](/systems/capabilities) and a server-side [handler](/systems/capabilities).
A contract defines the shared input, output, failures, and metadata.
[Effect](/lore/effect-basics) [Schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) provides types and runtime checks for these values. `defineContract` owns the name, Effect schemas, annotations, and approval setting. `implement` binds that contract to its handler.

Here, a surface is an [interface](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces) for calling the action.
A projection is code that converts registered capabilities into an interface.
The interfaces are command line, HTTP, MCP tools, browser RPC, and [code mode](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls).
Each interface derives its input and failure definitions from the same schemas.

## Worked example: `inspectFile`

### 1. The contract

packages/core/src/contracts.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 292-300; highlighted none. Title: Name, schemas, failure, and annotations.

```typescript
export const inspectFileContract = defineContract("inspectFile", {
  annotations: { idempotent: true, readOnly: true },
  description: "Count bytes, characters, words, and lines in a file",
  failure: FileStatsError,
  input: Schema.Struct({
    path: Schema.String.annotate({ description: "File to inspect" }),
  }),
  output: FileStatsSchema,
});
```

The contract holds no handler. A browser can import it without server code.

### 2. The handler

packages/core/src/inspect-file.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 14-19; highlighted 14-16,19. Title: implement binds the handler; capabilities registers it.

```typescript
export const inspectFile = implement(inspectFileContract, ({ path }) =>
  runInspectMachine(path)
);

export const capabilities = [
  inspectFile,
```

The handler runs [the inspection machine](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines).

### 3. The projections

apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 40-44; highlighted none. Title: HTTP, MCP tools, and code mode from the same lists.

```typescript
export const http = toHttpApi("RatStack", capabilities);

export const tools = toToolkit(cliCapabilities);

export const codeMode = toCodeMode(cliCapabilities);
```

apps/cli/src/command.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 22-28; highlighted 25-28. Title: The CLI command, with a stats alias.

```typescript
const capabilityCommands = commandCapabilities.map((capability) => {
  const command =
    capability === inspectFile
      ? toCommand(capability, {
          positional: ["path"],
          render: formatFileStats,
        }).pipe(Command.withAlias("stats"))
```

No projection repeats the schema. Each one reads the contract it was given.

## Why one contract

A second hand-written route would need its own schema, and the two could drift.
Here each surface derives its input and failure from one place.

The split replaced `defineCapability`, which bundled contract data and its handler in one definition. The RPC [client](/skills/uncomplect) needed the contract without importing server implementation. `toRpcGroup` now projects contracts alone; `toRpc` connects those same contracts to implemented capabilities. The browser docs client imports only the shared contracts and RPC group. [Commit 9a7bea5](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/9a7bea5) records the split.

Michael Arnaldi demonstrates Schema decoding request input and encoding a frontend-safe result while preserving its output type. [Effect Meetup SF, 27:17](https://youtu.be/BqUnsDnMnMo?t=1637). In another conversation, the speakers discuss generated schemas and migrations as work agents can maintain, and a rule that rejects ad hoc JSON parsing. [Cause & Effect 10, 63:49](https://youtu.be/irmz5X3c7Do?t=3829) [67:53](https://youtu.be/irmz5X3c7Do?t=4073).

## Next

To add a capability, define its contract and implement it beside the data or infrastructure it owns. Register it in `capabilities`, then check each interface you keep. `packages/capability/test/` exercises projections; `apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts` shows the hosted registry.

Use [the add-a-capability skill](/skills/add-a-capability) for the steps.

Read [A browser send follows one path to the capability](/lore/a-browser-send-follows-one-path) to see `search` called over RPC.

[Analytics](/systems/analytics) shows a separate infrastructure [cartridge](/lore/cartridges); [interest signup](/systems/interest) shows core ports with a delivery [adapter](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) outside core. Neither turns static pages or protocol discovery into domain capabilities.

See [lifecycles are machines](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines) for stateful handlers and [cartridges](/lore/cartridges) for the infrastructure boundary. [HATEOAS](/lore/hateoas) covers links that guide an agent's next action; [hexagonal architecture](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) names the ports-and-adapters principle.

# /lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls

Source: .brain/resources/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls.svx

# One program can replace several tool calls

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A capability is a named action with a typed contract and a handler.
Code mode combines calls to those actions in one program.
MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets an agent discover and call tools.

ratstack.sh already offers code mode:

- `POST /api/execute`.
- The MCP `execute` tool.

One request runs an async function body that combines content calls. [Joel's reply](https://x.com/joelhooks/status/2106018556496457773) asks for this alongside CLI, API, and MCP.

## A live program

This program runs against the live HTTP endpoint.

The callable definitions are in [`apps/mischief/src/capabilities/index.ts` at `445b1a20b51a5492f8e586daeb9306e8011b7673`, lines 34–45](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/445b1a20b51a5492f8e586daeb9306e8011b7673/apps/mischief/src/capabilities/index.ts#L34-L45). We wrote this read-only request.

```js
const found = await tools.search({ query: "cartridges", limit: 1 });
const page = await tools.read({ id: found.matches[0].id });
const graph = await tools.backlinks({ slug: page.routePath.split("/").at(-1) });
return { title: page.title, id: page.id, links: graph.backlinks.length };
```

The program passes the search result directly to read and reduces the graph result before returning it.

`POST /api/execute` returned this response on 2026-10-02:

```json
{"logs":[],"result":{"title":"Cartridges","id":"ratstack://lore/cartridges","links":31}}
```

Three typed calls use one outer request. This run measures neither latency nor token savings.

## The sandbox preserves the boundary

[`apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts) builds `toExecuteCapability(contentCapabilities)`. That list contains search, read, backlinks, neighbors, mentions, and path.

`joinInterest` belongs to the outer API/MCP registry. It does not belong to the sandbox's callable list.

[`packages/capability/src/to-code-mode.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/to-code-mode.ts) builds the catalog and TypeScript declarations. Every call from sandbox code returns to application code that validates input and runs the handler.
That code encodes the output or declared failure.

[`sandbox-worker-loader.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/sandbox-worker-loader.ts) runs a fresh Dynamic Worker, a Worker loaded to execute sandbox code, with:

- No outbound network.
- A 100 ms CPU limit.
- Five subrequests.
- A ten-second timeout.

Imports, exports, and fetch are unavailable.

The [HTTP and MCP rate-limit checks](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/app.ts) use [native rate limits](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/rate-limits.ts):

- Six execute calls per IP per minute.
- 300 execute calls total per minute.
- Separate counters in each Cloudflare location.

Combining calls does not waive these limits.

Use the [agent guide](/llms.txt) for the endpoint and call format. See [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface) for the tool transport.

See [how we do it with Effect](/lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect) for the whole path.

# /lore/one-schema-three-surfaces

Source: .brain/resources/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces.svx
SHA-256: c7a00565f72a952f3c6a7c35f02f219fd2f31cf134bd3662ea6c71ce7eded228

# One schema, three surfaces

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[Joel writes in a reply](https://x.com/joelhooks/status/2106018556496457773):

> my approach wrt to the agentic backend is to cover cli/api/mcp with a single openapi schema that is used to generate all three

His example is this repository. A capability is a named action with a contract and handler.
A contract defines the shared input, output, failures, and metadata.
Effect Schema supplies types and runtime checks for these values.

The code makes the direction more precise:

- A capability contract owns Effect schemas.
- HttpApi, OpenAPI, CLI, and MCP derive from that contract.
- CLI and MCP do not consume the generated OpenAPI JSON.

Each interface for calling the action, or surface, shares the same behavior. [`defineContract`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/contract.ts) owns input, output, failure, description, and annotations. `implement` binds one handler.

A projection builds an interface from a capability.

## One contract feeds the projections

```text
Contract (Effect schemas + one handler)
├─ toHttpApi ── HTTP + OpenAPI
├─ toCommand ── CLI
└─ toToolkit ── MCP tools
```

- [to-http-api.ts](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/to-http-api.ts) derives HttpApi endpoints, the handler Layer, and OpenAPI.
- [to-command.ts](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/to-command.ts) derives flags or positional inputs, schema decoding, and the command handler.
- [to-toolkit.ts](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/to-toolkit.ts) derives tool schemas, annotations, and the toolkit handler Layer.

## Where the CLI composes them

[`apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts) composes the projections. [`command.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/cli/src/command.ts) maps registered capabilities to commands. It also prints the generated OpenAPI document.

Source: [`apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts` at `b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c`, lines 25–44](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c/apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts#L25-L44).

apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 25-33,40-44; highlighted none.

```typescript
export const capabilities = [
  ...coreCapabilities,
  ...learnCapabilities,
] as const;

export const cliCapabilities = [
  ...coreCapabilities,
  ...localLearnCapabilities,
] as const;
export const http = toHttpApi("RatStack", capabilities);

export const tools = toToolkit(cliCapabilities);

export const codeMode = toCodeMode(cliCapabilities);
```

HTTP uses stateless learning capabilities. MCP and code mode use local learning capabilities.
Both lists include the same core capabilities, including `inspectFile`.

One HttpApi definition supplies the HTTP implementation and its OpenAPI document. The broader shared definition is the capability contract. This split avoids three independently maintained schemas.

See [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface), [OpenAPI](/lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too), and [code mode](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls) for each interface.

See [how we do it with Effect](/lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect) for the whole path.

# /lore/one-snippet-model-two-renderers

Source: .brain/resources/lore/one-snippet-model-two-renderers.svx
SHA-256: eae8f4a4531b568700fea98915019bb652bb012eea4e4912c9480e4c67728834

# One snippet model feeds both renderers

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

The [component registry](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/scripts/component-registry.ts) defines agent and human renderers.
The [code-snippets design brief](/lore/code-snippets) gives both renderers one snippet model.

The proposed `CodeSnippet` carries:

- Selected source text and original line numbers.
- Highlighted lines and collapsed gaps.
- Repository, commit, path, and source link.
- Diagnostics.

HTML adds colour, a filename, numbered lines, and a source link.
Agent Markdown adds the repository, commit, path, and original line numbers, plus a Markdown code block.
Both renderers use the same source facts.

Both views preserve the same source facts.
The planned property compares each view with the pinned source.

[Whole-file tokenization](/lore/tokenize-before-slicing) supplies the tokens.
[Engine-neutral tokens](/lore/engine-neutral-tokens-keep-adapters-replaceable) keep renderer input independent of Shiki.

See [the glossary](/glossary) for snippet model and renderer parity, the term for views preserving the same source facts.
