# /lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too

Source: .brain/resources/lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too.svx
SHA-256: 70dc56df12b11d8f85b3bbdbab6efe787799e0811e8cf61198fac06c1e084db1

# OpenAPI describes the refusal too

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[OpenAPI](https://spec.openapis.org/oas/v3.1.0.html) describes HTTP paths, operations, request bodies, and responses. An agent can read our generated [/openapi.json](/openapi.json) before choosing an HTTP call.

[`apps/site/src/app.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/app.ts) builds the `/api` projection. It passes the API to `HttpApiBuilder.layer`, with `openapiPath: "/openapi.json"`.

Effect's [`OpenApi.fromApi`](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/effect%404.0.0/packages/effect/src/http-api/OpenApi.ts) derives the document from that HttpApi.

## The document must describe rejected request input

[Commit 8766790](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/876679087c9fb1b10827140c54c0bfc3c2c4ff2e) adds `HttpApiError.BadRequestNoContent` to every endpoint built by `toHttpApi`. Request decoding already returns an empty 400. The document needs to say so.

The rejected request input produces an empty response body rather than `application/problem+json`. The [route test](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/test/to-http-api-routes.test.ts) sends an invalid payload and checks:

- Status 400.
- No content type.
- An empty body.

The document has a `BadRequest` response description with no `content` field. A reader uses that distinction to decide whether to parse the error body.

A declared failure defaults to 422 unless its schema names another HTTP status. A plain union keeps each member’s status, including on default POST routes. Projects created from the template with annotated union members now receive those statuses instead of 422.

A refinement adds a check that limits accepted values.
Checked or refined unions retain their whole-union status.

A declared domain failure differs from a request decode failure. See [schema-driven development](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) for that boundary. See [generating surfaces](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces) for the document's source.

See [how we do it with Effect](/lore/how-we-do-it-with-effect) for the whole path.

# /lore/pinned-sources-can-report-drift

Source: .brain/resources/lore/pinned-sources-can-report-drift.svx
SHA-256: 6b97188d73eba7deb0e24896f31b2139d2afa1b99d15a620e970789e9f5eec87

# Pin the source and report drift separately

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A pinned source identifies a repository, a full commit SHA, and a path.
The [code-snippets design brief](/lore/code-snippets) reads that source from local Git objects.
[`git show`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-show) documents object inspection.

The proposed snippet keeps its pinned text.
Source drift compares only the selected pinned lines with HEAD.
Source drift reports a warning. It leaves the pinned text intact and lets the build continue.

Keep HEAD out of the immutable snippet cache.
The cache key identifies the pinned source.
A separate diagnostic observes source drift.

If a shallow clone does not contain the pinned Git file or commit object, tell the author to fetch history.
Do not fetch it during content generation.

This boundary keeps [build-time work](/lore/build-time-work-stays-out-of-requests) local.
The configured registry follows [ports and adapters](/lore/hexagonal-architecture).

See [the glossary](/glossary) for pinned source and source drift.

1. [git show](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-show)
   Primary source. Reading objects Accessed 2026-10-02.

2. [Code-snippets design brief](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/.brain/resources/lore/code-snippets.svx)
   Primary source. Pin and drift design Accessed 2026-10-02.

# /lore/property-based-testing

Source: .brain/resources/lore/property-based-testing.svx
SHA-256: 96ff07c009343ae33467c167e1f881066e3ade7f76136a68fe7da328766edcee

# Property-based testing

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

An example test checks one input you picked. A property test states a rule that must hold for every input. It generates many inputs and shrinks a failing input to a small counterexample.

Effect 4 ships its own engine in `effect/Arbitrary`. `Arbitrary.schema` derives a generator from an Effect `Schema`. The same schema defines the [capability's contract](/systems/capabilities) and generates its test inputs. `Arbitrary.checkEffect` checks a pure or effectful property and "shrinks the first falsification." [Arbitrary.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Arbitrary.ts)

`@effect/vitest` exposes it as `it.prop` and `it.effect.prop`.

The [capture-first](/lore/capture-first) events cartridge is tested this way. For any generated request:

- Exactly one event is recorded.
- The response body and status are preserved.
- Persistent HTML may add the visitor cookie.
- The request body never reaches the event.
  For any query string, credential and email keys never survive. A failing sink does not change the response body or status. [Analytics](/systems/analytics) documents cookie behavior and what the checks establish about storage in Basin.

A property earns its place only if breaking the code breaks it. When first written, the events tests did not fail when `token` was removed from the sensitive-key list. The property compared the filter with the same function it was testing.

A second property with an independent list of sensitive keys closed the gap. The failure shrank to a single input, `"secret": "token"`. See [tests that earn their place](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

For sequences of actions, use [model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing).

See also: [Tests through supplied services](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

1. [Effect contributors. 2026. Arbitrary. Effect 4.0.0.](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Arbitrary.ts)

# /lore/pure-cores-reduce-timelines

Source: .brain/resources/lore/pure-cores-reduce-timelines.svx
SHA-256: 29f9fb6c20e87ae12e270569ee0ad9fd7019d3a1e32d118a38ad6b6597122b2b

# Pure cores reduce timeline coupling

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A functional core keeps domain rules independent of external interfaces and process machinery. Fewer shared timelines remove ordering problems before coordination is added.

> Our core doesn’t access external interfaces or use any process machinery your component might use.

Source: [Q14](/lore/durability-bibliography#q14); [B3](/lore/durability-bibliography#b3-designing-elixir-systems-with-otp), [B13](/lore/durability-bibliography#b13-grokking-simplicity).

## Failure it prevents

Rules change with hidden time or shared state and can only be tested through live integrations.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

Keep pure rules as ordinary functions. `Context.Service` and `Layer` put [effectful dependencies](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) behind seams. Wrapping a callback in [Effect](/lore/effect-basics) does not make it pure.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Context.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Layer.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`.

## How to check

Run the same decision with the same explicit data. Check that it needs neither network nor process state. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Replay needs stable inputs](/lore/replay-needs-stable-inputs), [Recovery needs model tests](/lore/recovery-needs-model-tests).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/queries-need-result-bounds

Source: .brain/resources/lore/queries-need-result-bounds.svx
SHA-256: 315bdca0f9eca836657475b768bb4d66ededac7704677a0fd874f3a95d98dfe7

# Queries need result bounds

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A timeout can limit waiting while leaving a large result problem intact. Limit query results explicitly and choose a bounded consumption path.

Book basis: [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it).

## Failure it prevents

One query exhausts memory despite a concurrency limit of one.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Stream.take` bounds consumption of a real stream. It cannot undo a driver’s full allocation. Apply limits or cursor pagination in the query [adapter](/lore/hexagonal-architecture).

Source: `packages/effect/src/Stream.ts`.

## How to check

Use a dataset larger than the intended result budget. Check rows fetched and memory before consumption completes. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Steady state recycles resources](/lore/steady-state-recycles-resources), [Bulkheads isolate scarce capacity](/lore/bulkheads-isolate-capacity).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/queues-pipelines-workflows-and-k2-do-different-jobs

Source: .brain/resources/lore/queues-pipelines-workflows-and-k2-do-different-jobs.svx
SHA-256: 870826ad6f1df504575f0b509435bcdc6778fc6de2427f7c2ac5d5946d26c360

# Queues, Pipelines, Workflows and K2 do different jobs

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Each of these products moves work or data out of the request that started it.
They differ in the unit they track.
Choose by that unit, then check the delivery promise.

```text
request ──┬─▶ Queue ──────▶ consumer: one job, ack or retry
          ├─▶ Pipeline ───▶ SQL ──▶ R2 table or files
          ├─▶ Workflow ───▶ step ─▶ step ─▶ sleep ─▶ step
          └─▶ K2 stream ──▶ subscription A (reads every record)
                       └──▶ subscription B (reads every record)
```

## Queues track one job at a time

A queue holds messages for a consumer Worker. Cloudflare lists three uses: offload work from a request, send data from Worker to Worker, and buffer or batch writes. [Storage options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options/)

- **Delivery:** at least once by default. Give each message a unique id and use it as an [idempotency](/lore/http-responses-need-validation) key. [Delivery guarantees](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/)
- **Per message:** a consumer can `ack()` or `retry()` each message in a batch. [Batching and retries](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/batching-retries/)
- **After retries:** a message moves to a dead letter queue after `max_retries`, three by default. Without a dead letter queue, Cloudflare deletes it. [Dead letter queues](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/configuration/dead-letter-queues/)

Cloudflare's rule: "Use Queues when each message is a unit of work that needs to be completed, retried, and tracked individually." [Storage options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options/)

In [Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy), `Cloudflare.Queues.Queue` declares the queue and `Cloudflare.Queues.Consumer` attaches a Worker, with `deadLetterQueue` and `settings.maxRetries`. A Worker sends through `Cloudflare.Queues.WriteQueue`. [Queue.ts](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.85/packages/cloudflare/src/Queues/Queue.ts) [Consumer.ts](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.85/packages/cloudflare/src/Queues/Consumer.ts)

See [Dead letters need a return path](/lore/dead-letters-need-a-return-path) for what the dead letter queue still needs: an owner and a redrive.

## Pipelines load rows into R2

Basin Pipelines is Cloudflare's streaming ingestion product, and it has three parts. Alchemy names it `Cloudflare.Pipelines`. [Basin Pipelines](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/)

1. A **stream** receives events over HTTP or a Worker [binding](/lore/bindings).
2. A **pipeline** runs SQL over the stream.
3. A **sink** writes Iceberg tables to Basin Catalog, or Parquet and JSON files to R2.

Sinks deliver exactly once. [Sinks](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/sinks/) Cloudflare lists clickstream analytics, [telemetry](/lore/trace-meaningful-operations) and logs as uses. [Storage options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options/)

The output is a table or a set of files in R2 that you query later.

### How rat-stack uses it

Pipelines is the only one of the four that rat-stack declares. `@rat-stack/basin` builds the stream for both [request analytics](/systems/analytics) and join intake. The stream accepts no HTTP input, so only the Worker binding writes to it.

packages/basin/src/index.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 14-25; highlighted 20-22. Title: A private stream beside its bucket.

```typescript
export const basinStream = (name: string) =>
  Effect.gen(function* declareBasinStream() {
    const bucket = yield* Cloudflare.R2.Bucket(`${name}Bucket`, {}).pipe(
      retainInProd
    );

    const stream = yield* Cloudflare.Pipelines.Stream(`${name}Stream`, {
      http: { enabled: false },
    }).pipe(retainInProd);

    return { bucket, stream } as const;
  });
```

`icebergSink` then copies every row unchanged into one table:

packages/basin/src/index.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 71-73; highlighted none. Title: SELECT \* keeps the raw row.

```typescript
    return yield* Cloudflare.Pipelines.Pipeline(`${name}Pipeline`, {
      sql: Output.interpolate`INSERT INTO ${sink.name} SELECT * FROM ${streamName}`,
    }).pipe(retainInProd);
```

[Capture first](/lore/capture-first) explains why the copy stays raw.

## Workflows run steps that resume

A Workflow chains steps, retries failed steps, and persists state for minutes, hours or weeks. It can sleep, and it can wait for an external event such as an approval. [Workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/)

Each step retries on its own, so make each step idempotent. [Rules of Workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/rules-of-workflows/) A step that charges a card must first check whether the charge already happened.

In Alchemy, a Workflow body is an [Effect](/lore/effect-basics). `Cloudflare.Workflows.task` runs one named durable step. Its result is persisted and replayed on retries. `sleep`, `sleepUntil` and `waitForEvent` pause the run. The same source describes Workflows as at-least-once. [Workflow.ts](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.85/packages/cloudflare/src/Workflows/Workflow.ts)

Choose a Workflow when the unit is a process with ordered steps and waits. Each instance has a unique ID and runs many steps. [Rules of Workflows](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/build/rules-of-workflows/)

## K2 keeps a log that many readers replay

K2 is a durable log. Producers append records. Consumers read through subscriptions, and each subscription receives every record. [K2 concepts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/k2/concepts/)

- **Reading does not delete:** records stay until retention ends. Retention goes up to 30 days, and longer by request. [K2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/k2/)
- **Replay:** a new subscription can start at `earliest` and read records produced before it existed. [Delivery guarantees](https://developers.cloudflare.com/k2/reference/delivery-guarantees/)
- **Leases:** a consumer holds a batch for five minutes, then acks, nacks, or loses it to redelivery. [K2 concepts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/k2/concepts/)
- **Limits of the promise:** delivery is at least once per subscription. K2 acks whole batches, does not deduplicate, and does not order records across workers. [Delivery guarantees](https://developers.cloudflare.com/k2/reference/delivery-guarantees/)

Cloudflare says to use K2 when what matters is "that every record is processed rather than the state of any one record." [Storage options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options/)

K2 is in public beta on the Workers Paid plan. [K2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/k2/) Alchemy declares it as `Cloudflare.K2.Stream` and `Cloudflare.K2.Subscription`. A stream can take an Effect [Schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary), so consumers receive decoded values. [K2/Stream.ts](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/v2.0.0-beta.85/packages/cloudflare/src/K2/Stream.ts)

## Choose by the unit you track

- **One job that must finish:** Queues. Track and retry each message.
- **Rows you query later:** Pipelines. Load them into R2 as a table.
- **A process with steps and waits:** Workflows. Resume from the last finished step.
- **Events for several independent readers:** K2. Replay them from the log.

Three of the four deliver at least once. Make every consumer and step safe to repeat. [Retry needs idempotent effects](/lore/retry-needs-idempotency) shows how.

## Where rat-stack does without them

Join intake must deliver each contact after the response. It uses no queue. It saves the contact with a pending-delivery marker, then adds its id to a sweep index in a separate call. A [cron every five minutes](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725/apps/site/src/interest/intake-sweep.ts#L13) redrives each pending id in that index.

That recovery has a documented gap. If the index write fails, the contact keeps its marker, but the sweep never finds it. [Join intake spec](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725/packages/core/spec/README.md?plain=1#L105-L111) The backstop works by id: `rat-stack intake redeliver` re-drives a delivery, and `rat-stack intake erase` re-drives an erase.

[Durability](/systems/durability) shows the model tests that check it.

The marker plus its index entry is the recovery record. Cloudflare lists this job, offloading work from a request, as a Queues use. [Storage options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/storage-options/) [Request lifetime is not durability](/lore/request-lifetime-is-not-durability) explains why a record is needed at all.

Next, read [Durable work needs storage](/lore/durable-work-needs-storage), then [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/rat-king

Source: .brain/resources/lore/rat-king.svx
SHA-256: 8e6a7ca7d2a0882f96db106e0de6311450e914d9a2d401da32fc111bade54ca8

# Rat King carries signed mail between named agents

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Rat King is a mail system for named agents. It sends signed messages.

The [Pi extension](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/packages/pi-ratking/README.md) maps names to DIDs and checks signed senders.
Mail belongs to a name. The reader that holds its lease receives it.

## Signing and encryption are separate choices

The [envelope package](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/packages/envelope/README.md) supports signed plaintext and sign-then-encrypt envelopes.
Signed plaintext exposes the message body.
Encrypted envelopes use HPKE, with ES256 application signatures.
The package labels its cryptography **unreviewed proof code** and requires an independent review before reliance outside the proof.

The [CLI](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/apps/ratking-cli/README.md) provides `send --encrypt`.
The [MCP send tool](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/apps/ratking-mcp/README.md) sends signed plaintext.
These surfaces have different encryption options.

## Schemas distinguish records from operations

Rat King uses [AT Protocol](/lore/at-protocol) DIDs and lexicons.
Its [lexicon package](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/packages/lexicon/README.md) generates schemas from JSON contracts.
It exposes typed mailbox clients and server layers. Adapters supply authentication, transport, and retries.

The [agent profile schema](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/lexicons/sh/mschf/ratking/agent/profile.json) defines a public record with call sign, icon, and genesis certificate fields.

[Mailbox send](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/lexicons/sh/mschf/ratking/mailbox/send.json) is a procedure.
Its input carries an envelope and can carry a sender lease generation.

The [runtime lease schema](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/lexicons/sh/mschf/ratking/runtime/lease.json) describes a private, ephemeral runtime association.
It explicitly excludes the lease from public repository records.

## Clients share the mail core

The [source tree](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/tree/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530) contains mailbox, CLI, MCP, and web apps.
Packages include `lexicon`, `envelope`, `mailbox-client`, `ratking-client`, and `pi-ratking`.

- **Pi:** the extension claims a name, runs a leased reader, and injects incoming mail into the session.
- **CLI:** `ratking` provides send, ask, reply, inbox, read, and pending commands.
- **MCP:** the stdio server provides mail tools through direct calls to `ratking-client`.

The [CLI](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/apps/ratking-cli/README.md) and [MCP server](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/apps/ratking-mcp/README.md) use the same [client](/skills/uncomplect) core as Pi.
The [project law](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/AGENTS.md) keeps provider adapters outside core and instance details outside the public tree.

## Public repositories remain a roadmap step

The [vision](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-king/blob/b8e165ba527e3d7867cdf5dfa30bca7ef4965530/VISION.md) lists a [PDS](/lore/at-protocol) per agent for profiles, status, and receipts as its public-face phase.
It places permissioned Spaces and federation in later phases.
Schema definitions alone do not prove those phases deployed.

Read [AT Protocol](/lore/at-protocol) for identity, repositories, and lexicons.
See [Rat's Nest](/lore/rats-nest) for the on-prem cloud idea.

# Rat's Nest keeps the code public and the inventory private

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

> "Rat's Nest is my own purpose-built on-prem cloud to support my development, business, and content creation work."
>
> Joel Hooks

Rat's Nest succeeds joelclaw, Joel's earlier agent system.
It uses rat-stack and [Alchemy](/lore/infrastructure-as-effects) to declare infrastructure as code.

Joel builds Rat's Nest in public.
A series will document the build.
The project has no public repository yet.

## Public code, private inventory

The design rule is **public code, private inventory**.

- Hostnames, IPs, sites, ports, and machine inventory live outside the repo.
- A fence built from the private inventory blocks those details from public commits.

[The fence](/lore/the-fence) explains how rules become enforced checks.
[Cartridges](/lore/cartridges) explain rat-stack's service and infrastructure pattern.

See [Rat King](/lore/rat-king) for the encrypted [AT Protocol](/lore/at-protocol) agent network.

# /lore/recovery-needs-model-tests

Source: .brain/resources/lore/recovery-needs-model-tests.svx

# Recovery needs model tests

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A stateful property compares generated commands with real behavior. Deterministic initial state makes failures reproducible and shrinkable. Check the model by injecting a [defect](/lore/effect-basics).

> Both function calls must be deterministic.

Source: [Q17](/lore/durability-bibliography#q17); [B11](/lore/durability-bibliography#b11-property-based-testing), [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B15](/lore/durability-bibliography#b15-software-engineering-at-google).

## Failure it prevents

A vacuous or happy-path suite misses corruption across retries, cancellation, and restart.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Arbitrary.checkEffect` and @[effect](/lore/effect-basics)/vitest run properties. `TestClock` and `Deferred` control `Effect` time and coordination. Author the command model; test persistent backends separately.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Arbitrary.ts`, `packages/effect/src/testing/TestClock.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Deferred.ts`.

## How to check

Plant a known transition bug. Require the property to fail and yield a replayable, valid counterexample. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Checkpoints follow the promised commit](/lore/checkpoints-follow-commits), [Circuit breakers have state](/lore/circuit-breakers-have-state).

Connect this to [property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) and [model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

   Pragmatic Bookshelf. Chapter 7 Shrinking; Laying Out Stateful Properties; Testing Parallel Executions; Initial State for the State Machine; Adjusting the Model. Use the actual breaker’s threshold semantics. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/replay-needs-stable-inputs

Source: .brain/resources/lore/replay-needs-stable-inputs.svx
SHA-256: d588f2fb3e16dfb580ce61a69e164ad790f03085aa37c957264e6d5e8c36877d

# Replay needs stable inputs

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Deterministic processing should agree between live consumption and catch-up. Event ordering and late-arrival rules belong to the domain.

> The overarching goal of deterministic processing is that a microservice should produce the same output whether it is processing in real time or catching up to the present time.

Source: [Q11](/lore/durability-bibliography#q11); [B5](/lore/durability-bibliography#b5-building-event-driven-microservices).

## Failure it prevents

Reprocessing the same history changes decisions because time, ordering, or an external answer changed.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Activity` can record an [effect](/lore/effect-basics) result under an engine. `Stream` does not choose event-time ordering, lateness policy, or protect a rebuild from live writes.

Source: `packages/effect/src/workflow/Activity.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Stream.ts`.

## How to check

Replay captured input into a clean target with controlled decisions. Compare output and apply the declared late-event policy. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Old events must still decode](/lore/old-events-must-still-decode), [Pure cores reduce timeline coupling](/lore/pure-cores-reduce-timelines).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

   O’Reilly. Chapter 3 Communication and Data Contracts; Chapter 6 Deterministic Stream Processing; Chapter 7 Stateful Streaming; Chapter 9 Microservices Using Function-as-a-Service; Chapter 14 Supportive Tooling. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/request-lifetime-is-not-durability

Source: .brain/resources/lore/request-lifetime-is-not-durability.svx
SHA-256: bae599681ca1654d33e32c93fcbf7feb8e70d03f24c1bdbd21a4b26f58637dca

# Request lifetime is not durability

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A bounded request pass and a durable recovery record solve different problems. On HTTP Workers, waitUntil extends execution for up to 30 seconds after response or disconnect; that allowance is shared.

Book basis: [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B6](/lore/durability-bibliography#b6-fundamentals-of-data-engineering).

## Failure it prevents

Three 20-second attempts plus delays need more time than the post-response allowance, so background delivery is cut off without recovery.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

Use one deadline for the pass and cap every attempt at remaining time. `Context.Reference` can hold an intentional default budget. Do not cache an absolute deadline in it. Persist an undelivered marker for independent redrive.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Context.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`.

## How to check

Use a 25-second example budget. Cancel post-response work, then redrive the persisted marker with the same operation identity and prove duplicate safety. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Timeouts bound waiting](/lore/timeouts-bound-waiting), [Retry needs idempotent effects](/lore/retry-needs-idempotency).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Nygard, Michael T. Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software. Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007.](https://archive.org/details/releaseitdesignd0000nyga)
   Pragmatic Bookshelf. §4.4 Unbounded Result Sets; Chapter 5 Stability Patterns: §5.1 Timeouts, §5.2 Circuit Breaker, §5.3 Bulkheads, §5.4 Steady State, §5.5 Fail Fast, §5.6 Handshaking, §5.7 Test Harness, §5.8 Decoupling Middleware. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Reis, Joe; Housley, Matt. Fundamentals of Data Engineering. O’Reilly.](https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/fundamentals-of-data/9781098108298)
   O’Reilly. Part II, Chapter 5: Message Queues; DataOps considerations; Incident Response. Accessed 2026-10-23.

   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/restart-from-known-state

Source: .brain/resources/lore/restart-from-known-state.svx
SHA-256: f9efda891a149cf629ebc3ce21a08f708d6c6c46065cdad8dc881b1f53a46d98

# Restart must reconstruct known state

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Letting a worker fail is useful when recovery returns it to a known state. Preserve indispensable recovery data; rebuild disposable state.

Book basis: [B1](/lore/durability-bibliography#b1-erlang-and-otp-in-action), [B2](/lore/durability-bibliography#b2-elixir-in-action), [B3](/lore/durability-bibliography#b3-designing-elixir-systems-with-otp).

## Failure it prevents

A fresh worker reuses inconsistent state or forgets critical coordination data.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Activity` results and `WorkflowEngine` can support reconstruction with persistent storage. A new [fiber](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner) does not restore old local variables or [machine](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines) memory.

Source: `packages/effect/src/workflow/Activity.ts`, `packages/effect/src/workflow/WorkflowEngine.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Fiber.ts`.

## How to check

Recover from an incomplete step using durable authority. Check behavior rather than merely checking that the worker is running. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Replay needs stable inputs](/lore/replay-needs-stable-inputs), [Durable timers need recovery](/lore/durable-timers-need-recovery).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/retry-load-needs-a-budget

Source: .brain/resources/lore/retry-load-needs-a-budget.svx

# Retry load needs a budget

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Immediate retries can extend caller waiting and worsen a persistent outage. Randomize backoff and consider shared retry accounting beyond per-call limits.

Book basis: [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B9](/lore/durability-bibliography#b9-serverless-architectures-on-aws), [B10](/lore/durability-bibliography#b10-a-philosophy-of-software-design), [B12](/lore/durability-bibliography#b12-site-reliability-engineering).

## Failure it prevents

Bounded requests collectively flood a recovering dependency, or nested retries multiply attempts.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Effect.retry` and `Schedule.exponential`, `Schedule.jittered`, `Schedule.recurs`, and `Schedule.upTo` provide local policies. Shared budgets require an explicit owner and accounting [scope](/lore/scopes-own-resources).

Source: `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Schedule.ts`.

## How to check

Count attempts across the call path during a common outage. Check the declared total budget and caller deadline. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Circuit breakers have state](/lore/circuit-breakers-have-state), [Admission control protects recovery](/lore/admission-controls-new-work).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/retry-needs-idempotency

Source: .brain/resources/lore/retry-needs-idempotency.svx
SHA-256: 8ce77caae2ec10ce0b641fcd2da734f9aaa87a439f8f420fcf917184bb51529d

# Retry needs idempotent effects

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A consumer can run an event again after failure. Processing guarantees inside one store do not cover every external side [effect](/lore/effect-basics).

> In an idempotent system, the outcome of processing a message once is identical to the outcome of processing it multiple times.

Source: [Q10](/lore/durability-bibliography#q10); [B5](/lore/durability-bibliography#b5-building-event-driven-microservices), [B6](/lore/durability-bibliography#b6-fundamentals-of-data-engineering).

## Failure it prevents

A response disappears after a remote write succeeds, and retry repeats the write.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Workflow` identity and `Activity.idempotencyKey` name work. Receiver-side keys or transactional dedupe must enforce the repeated effect’s semantics.

Source: `packages/effect/src/workflow/Workflow.ts`, `packages/effect/src/workflow/Activity.ts`, `packages/effect/src/workflow/DurableQueue.ts`.

## How to check

Lose the response after remote success. Retry the same identity and inspect the authoritative result. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Checkpoints follow the promised commit](/lore/checkpoints-follow-commits), [Cleanup can be an idempotent postcondition](/lore/cleanup-can-be-an-idempotent-postcondition).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/run-effect-at-the-boundary

Source: .brain/resources/lore/run-effect-at-the-boundary.svx
SHA-256: 63944f998810f976945b6090dc2569c6c45faaf08211a8f61e4725cf55572b29

# Run Effect at the integration boundary

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A service is a named interface. A Layer describes how to build a service and supply its dependencies.
A runtime executes Effects. A managed runtime keeps constructed services until disposal.

Keep service methods as Effects. Run them where a process, framework, or callback requires execution.
The integration boundary owns the runtime's lifetime.

## Use the calling framework's Effect integration

- **One CLI process**: Compose the program, then use `NodeRuntime.runMain`
- **Effect-native HTTP router**: Adapt its Layer with `HttpRouter.toWebHandler`
- **Framework that expects native Promises rather than Effects**: Reuse a `ManagedRuntime` owned by that integration
- **Effect-aware test**: Let `it.effect` or `it.layer` execute the test

A managed runtime is one integration tool. It is not required inside every Effect application.

The [basics page](/lore/effect-basics) shows CLI, Worker and test execution boundaries.
The CLI's composition root supplies requirements before running its program.

## Do not replace an existing Effect bridge

The development backend already uses a router bridge:

apps/web/src/dev/backend.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 9-16; highlighted none.

```typescript
const { handler } = HttpRouter.toWebHandler(
  devtoolsRoutes(contentCapabilities).pipe(Layer.provide(nodeContentLayer)),
  {
    disableLogger: true,
  }
);

export const backend: BackendFetch = handler;
```

`toWebHandler` also returns a disposal function.
This module keeps only the handler; the excerpt does not prove explicit disposal on development-server shutdown.
Do not present that missing shutdown check as established resource cleanup.

## Own a foreign runtime explicitly

The checked adapter exposes a small Promise API to a hypothetical foreign framework.
It creates one managed runtime from a counted resource Layer.

packages/capability/test/fixtures/wiki/foreign-runtime-boundary.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 6-23; highlighted none.

```typescript
export const makeForeignRuntimeBoundary = (options: {
  readonly acquired: Ref.Ref<number>;
  readonly released: Ref.Ref<number>;
}) => {
  const runtime = ManagedRuntime.make(BoundaryResource.layer(options));

  const read = Effect.gen(function* readBoundaryResource() {
    const resource = yield* BoundaryResource;

    return yield* resource.read;
  });

  return {
    close: runtime.dispose.bind(runtime),
    // @effect-diagnostics-next-line asyncFunction:off -- This foreign framework boundary exposes a native Promise API.
    read: async () => await runtime.runPromise(read),
  };
};
```

Effect stays inside the adapter. Callers receive a Promise-facing `read` and an explicit `close`.

The Layer builds on first use. Later calls reuse the built service context.
`close` disposes the runtime and releases its resources.
An integration must connect that close operation to its own shutdown path.

Keep native async functions at the foreign boundary. Domain methods return Effects.

## Prove disposal through the foreign interface

The fixture's test harness uses `it.effect`.
The adapter under test owns the manual runtime.

packages/capability/test/runtime-boundary.test.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 10-30; highlighted none.

```typescript
      const acquired = yield* Ref.make(0);
      const released = yield* Ref.make(0);
      yield* Effect.acquireUseRelease(
        Effect.sync(() => makeForeignRuntimeBoundary({ acquired, released })),
        (boundary) =>
          Effect.gen(function* useForeignBoundary() {
            expect(yield* Ref.get(acquired)).toBe(0);
            expect(yield* Effect.tryPromise(boundary.read)).toBe("ready");
            expect(yield* Effect.tryPromise(boundary.read)).toBe("ready");
            expect(yield* Ref.get(acquired)).toBe(1);
            yield* Effect.promise(boundary.close);
            yield* Effect.promise(boundary.close);
            expect(yield* Ref.get(released)).toBe(1);

            const reused = yield* Effect.tryPromise(boundary.read).pipe(
              Effect.result
            );

            expect(Result.isFailure(reused)).toBe(true);
          }),
        (boundary) => Effect.promise(boundary.close)
```

The test wraps the subject's native Promises with Effect adapters.
Its acquire/use/release cleanup also closes the subject if an assertion fails.
Check the running server's shutdown behavior separately.

## Integrate one calling framework at a time

1. Identify the process or framework that requires execution.
2. Keep the job's input, output and failures typed inside Effect.
3. Build the needed services at the integration boundary.
4. Translate native callbacks or Promises at that edge.
5. Connect disposal to the host's shutdown path.
6. Test the foreign interface and its cleanup.

## Common mistakes

- Create a runtime for each domain method. Construction and cleanup lose a clear owner.
- Return native Promises throughout the domain. Replacing Effects with native Promises loses composition of typed failures and requirements.
- Forget to dispose a long-lived runtime.
- Assume a framework's shutdown is proven because the adapter returns a close function.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Runners and framework bridges execute Effects; runtime owners manage their Layers and disposal.
- In rat-stack, [capabilities remain the shared interface for application actions](/lore/one-capability-every-surface). A new runner does not authorize a handler that skips the capability contract.
- In rat-stack, test harnesses use [Effect-aware tests](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place), not manually created runtimes.

Read [scopes](/lore/scopes-own-resources) when deciding what the integration owns.
Read [services](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) before extracting the job from its host.
Return to the [Effect reading order](/lore/effect-basics#read-next).

   Effect-TS. make builds a Layer lazily, caches its context, owns resources and running fibers, and refuses reuse after disposal. Accessed 2026-10-06.

# Sam Goodwin

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Sam describes a cloud application as a computation: a description of work with a result or error.
Its infrastructure context is the cloud environment and dependencies in which it runs.
Its flow is the sequence of work. [Happy Path 116, 24:55](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=1495).

He explains that runtime clients, business logic, and infrastructure policies stay related even when they live in separate files. [Happy Path 116, 30:31](https://youtu.be/YEn4A7XxgF4?t=1831).

He built [cafe](https://github.com/Effect-TS/cafe), the reference app for the [CAFE stack](/lore/cafe-stack).

# /lore/schema-changes-need-a-transition

Source: .brain/resources/lore/schema-changes-need-a-transition.svx
SHA-256: 70ab8f46069f5e8f321035bf4efec601b075c80e859be873c7cbd892866de4de

# Shared schemas need a transition period

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A shared [schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) change needs time for consumers to move. Discover old uses and prevent new uses before removing the obsolete [interface](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces).

> many refactorings require you to run both the original and new versions of the schema in parallel during a transition period that is long enough to allow any applications accessing that portion of the schema time to be redeployed.

Source: [Q19](/lore/durability-bibliography#q19); [B14](/lore/durability-bibliography#b14-refactoring-databases), [B15](/lore/durability-bibliography#b15-software-engineering-at-google).

## Failure it prevents

An independently deployed consumer breaks, or a migration never converges because new old-style uses keep appearing.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Schema` decoding can express supported representations. Database migrations, consumer rollout, usage evidence, and static backsliding checks remain separate responsibilities.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Schema.ts`.

## How to check

Test old and new consumers during the transition. Prove old usage is gone before contraction. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Old events must still decode](/lore/old-events-must-still-decode), [Recovery needs model tests](/lore/recovery-needs-model-tests).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/property-based-testing).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Ambler, Scott W.; Sadalage, Pramod J. Refactoring Databases: Evolutionary Database Design. Addison-Wesley, 2006.](https://www.amazon.com/Refactoring-Databases-Evolutionary-paperback-Addison-Wesley/dp/0321774515)
   Addison-Wesley. §3.11 What You Have Learned (transition period); Chapter 4 Deploying into Production. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Winters, Titus; Manshreck, Tom; Wright, Hyrum, editors. Software Engineering at Google: Lessons Learned from Programming Over Time. O’Reilly, 2020.](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book)
   O’Reilly. Chapter 15 Deprecation: Deprecation Tooling and Preventing Backsliding; CI Is Alerting (hermetic and flaky tests). Accessed 2026-10-23.

3. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. Schema.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/schemas-define-the-boundary

Source: .brain/resources/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary.svx
SHA-256: 25e2fa1f6fb3e88fee5aff346a6f580b7e117d1533f287cf66fdc9a69bd8b441

# Schemas define the boundary

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Schema defines accepted values, runtime checks, and associated TypeScript types.
Decoding checks external input and produces an application value. Encoding produces its external representation.
A codec connects these two representations.

Define the values the application accepts before writing the handler.
Decode unknown input at the boundary. Encode results through the declared output schema.

## Use one model for types and runtime checks

`Schema.Struct` describes a record. `Schema.Literals` describes a fixed set of alternatives.
A schema's `Type` describes its decoded value; `Encoded` describes its external representation.
Those representations can differ when a codec transforms values.

packages/core/src/contracts.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 115-126; highlighted none.

```typescript
const ContentKind = Schema.Literals(["law", "skill", "lore", "prompt"]);

export const SearchMatch = Schema.Struct({
  description: Schema.String,
  digest: Schema.String,
  excerpt: Schema.String,
  id: Schema.String,
  kind: ContentKind,
  routePath: Schema.String,
  score: Schema.Finite,
  title: Schema.String,
});
```

Content kinds have four accepted values. A match must carry the declared fields and a finite score.

Derive the TypeScript type from the schema rather than maintaining a second interface.
Use `Schema.Union` when accepted alternatives have different shapes, including tagged failures.

## Put the schemas in the contract

A contract declares an action's input, output, and failures.
The file-inspection contract names its input, result, and failure.

packages/core/src/contracts.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 255-263; highlighted none.

```typescript
export const inspectFileContract = defineContract("inspectFile", {
  annotations: { idempotent: true, readOnly: true },
  description: "Count bytes, characters, words, and lines in a file",
  failure: FileStatsError,
  input: Schema.Struct({
    path: Schema.String.annotate({ description: "File to inspect" }),
  }),
  output: FileStatsSchema,
});
```

The schemas check values at runtime.

## Decode before dispatch

`Schema.decodeUnknownEffect` accepts unknown input and keeps decoding failures in the Effect error channel.
Our code-mode invoker calls the handler only after decoding succeeds.

packages/capability/src/to-code-mode.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 208-221; highlighted none.

```typescript
      return Schema.decodeUnknownEffect(item.contract.input)(input).pipe(
        Effect.matchEffect({
          onFailure: () =>
            Effect.succeed(
              invokeFailure(
                "InvalidInput",
                "Capability input does not match its schema"
              )
            ),
          onSuccess: (decoded) =>
            run(decoded).pipe(
              Effect.provideContext(context),
              Effect.matchEffect({
                onFailure: (error) =>
```

Rejected input becomes `InvalidInput`. The domain handler receives the decoded value after validation.

The same invoker uses `Schema.encodeUnknownEffect` for declared outputs and failures.
For an already-typed value, `Schema.encodeEffect` supplies the typed encoding API.
JSON serialization alone does not check whether a result satisfies its contract.

## A schema states what a value means

The interest contract separates contact consent from sharing consent. Accepting contact does not authorize sharing.
Its answer fields are bounded strings.

`AbuseVerdictSchema` describes a hold flag, a finite score between zero and one, and signal names.
The `AbuseVerdict` type derives from that schema.
These are domain decisions; Schema does not choose them for us.

A generated input also does not supply a behavior assertion.
[Property tests](/lore/property-based-testing) still need an independent rule that those values must satisfy.

## Common wrong approach

A type assertion changes what TypeScript believes. It does not reject a malformed external value.
Decode at the boundary instead of casting it into a domain type.

Hand-written JSON parsing followed by a copied interface creates two models that can drift.
Use the schema's decoding and encoding APIs. Report malformed input separately from an expected [domain refusal](/lore/error-model).

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Schema defines runtime decoding, encoding, and the associated TypeScript types.
- In rat-stack, one capability contract supplies schemas to every interface projection.
- rat-stack also uses capabilities and a bodyless HTTP 400 response for malformed input.

See also: [one schema, three surfaces](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces), [OpenAPI refusals](/lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too), [services](/lore/services-capture-dependencies), and [testing](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

# /lore/scopes-own-resources

Source: .brain/resources/lore/scopes-own-resources.svx
SHA-256: 12bc32bee4ed2278d25df30fe075c1192b64d68b5773dfcb03d2e4582cbcd9a0

# Scopes release resources when work ends

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A Scope owns resource cleanup. A fiber is an independently running Effect.
Acquisition obtains a resource; release cleans it up.

Construct the resource inside an acquisition Effect. Register release before handing the resource to its caller.
Keep use inside the resource's lifetime.

## Acquire, use, and release one resource

The migration adapter opens a Postgres client inside `Effect.tryPromise`.
`acquireUseRelease` gives the client to migration work and then runs shutdown.

packages/database/src/postgres-migrations.ts at 65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20; lines 64-81; highlighted none.

```typescript
              return yield* Effect.acquireUseRelease(
                Effect.tryPromise({
                  catch: (cause) =>
                    new PostgresMigrationConnectionError({ cause }),
                  // @effect-diagnostics-next-line asyncFunction:off -- The pg client exposes Promise-based connection setup.
                  try: async () => {
                    const connection = new Client({ connectionString: url });

                    await connection.connect();

                    return connection;
                  },
                }),
                (connection) =>
                  runPostgresMigrations(
                    input.directory,
                    makePgMigrationExecutor(connection)
                  ),
```

The release callback closes the connection:

packages/database/src/postgres-migrations.ts at 65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20; lines 82-90; highlighted none.

```typescript
                (connection) =>
                  Effect.tryPromise({
                    catch: (cause) =>
                      new PostgresMigrationConnectionError({ cause }),
                    // @effect-diagnostics-next-line asyncFunction:off -- The pg client exposes Promise-based shutdown.
                    try: async () => {
                      await connection.end();
                    },
                  }).pipe(Effect.orDie)
```

This example handles one acquired connection.
If acquisition fails before release registration, the acquisition code must clean up any partial resource it created.

## Choose the lifetime

- **`acquireUseRelease`**: One use callback; release follows that callback's exit
- **`acquireRelease`**: The current Scope; release runs when that Scope closes
- **`scoped`**: A new Scope around the supplied Effect

A resource finalizer is cleanup work attached to an owner. It is not a business-state transition.

Use `acquireRelease` when several operations need the same resource.
A service Layer can own that resource for its build lifetime.
Callers must not retain the handle after its Scope closes.

## Prove all use exits

The checked fixture creates a counted handle inside `Effect.sync`.
Its finalizer increments a separate release counter.

packages/core/test/scoped-resource.test.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 8-18; highlighted none.

```typescript
      const acquired = yield* Ref.make(0);
      const released = yield* Ref.make(0);
      const started = yield* Deferred.make<boolean>();

      const acquire = Effect.acquireRelease(
        Effect.sync(() => ({ name: "counted-resource" })).pipe(
          Effect.tap(() => Ref.update(acquired, (count) => count + 1)),
          Effect.tap(() => Deferred.succeed(started, true))
        ),
        () => Ref.update(released, (count) => count + 1)
      );
```

The test cases exercise success, [expected failure](/lore/error-model), and interruption.
Each case must acquire once and release once. It also checks that the selected exit actually occurred.

packages/core/test/scoped-resource.test.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 37-55; highlighted none.

```typescript
      if (outcome === "interruption") {
        const fiber = yield* Effect.forkChild(use);
        yield* Deferred.await(started);
        yield* Fiber.interrupt(fiber);
        const exit = yield* Fiber.await(fiber);
        expect(Exit.isFailure(exit) && Cause.hasInterrupts(exit.cause)).toBe(
          true
        );
      } else {
        const result = yield* Effect.result(use);
        expect(Result.isFailure(result)).toBe(outcome === "failure");

        if (Result.isFailure(result)) {
          expect(result.failure).toBe("expected-refusal");
        }
      }

      expect(yield* Ref.get(acquired)).toBe(1);
      expect(yield* Ref.get(released)).toBe(1);
```

Interrupting a fiber does not bypass its registered finalizer.

## Common mistakes

- Allocate the client before building the acquisition Effect. An interruption can leave that client without a registered finalizer.
- Return a resource from `scoped` and use it later. Its lifetime has already ended.
- Claim failed acquisition always invokes release. Release registration requires successful acquisition.
- Treat a close failure as harmless without checking the adapter's failure policy.

The migration adapter makes shutdown failure a defect with `orDie`.
Ordinary callers still need declared failures in the typed channel.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- A Scope owns finalizers; acquire/use/release operations arrange that sequence.
- In rat-stack, construct resources inside acquisition. The lint fence checks this shape.
- In rat-stack, [machines own finite business lifecycles](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines). Resource cleanup does not replace a lifecycle machine.

Start with [Layer composition](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) when choosing the resource's owner.
Then read [concurrent work](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner) before starting child work.

A Scope ends with its process. [Steady state recycles resources](/lore/steady-state-recycles-resources) covers growth that outlives one Scope.

Return to the [Effect reading order](/lore/effect-basics#read-next).

# /lore/services-capture-dependencies

Source: .brain/resources/lore/services-capture-dependencies.svx
SHA-256: 62d52e6f3fc0a6fa0ef7053bc4831618ee185b1e02c344971a42fef4a3b91887

# A service captures its construction dependencies

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A service is a named interface. A Layer describes how to build a service and supply its dependencies.
A context holds supplied service implementations.

Build a service once with the dependencies its implementation needs. Return methods that use those captured values.
Callers then require only the service.

## Name the job before the implementation

`Context.Service` names a service and describes its interface.
`Effect.Effect<FileStats, FileStatsError>` declares the method's success and [expected failure](/lore/error-model). Its omitted requirement parameter is `never`.

packages/core/src/file-inspector.ts at 65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20; lines 6-15; highlighted none.

```typescript
export class FileInspector extends Context.Service<
  FileInspector,
  {
    readonly inspect: (
      path: string
    ) => Effect.Effect<FileStats, FileStatsError>;
  }
>()("@rat-stack/core/FileInspector", {
  make: Effect.gen(function* makeFileInspector() {
    const fileSystem = yield* FileSystem.FileSystem;
```

`make` describes service construction as an Effect.
`Layer.effect` runs that construction when the service graph is built.

## Compose work inside the method

Use `Effect.gen` for inline composition. Use `Effect.fn("name")` for reusable functions that need a tracing boundary.
Use `Effect.fnUntraced` when tracing is not useful.
Do not create a function that only returns another `Effect.gen` wrapper.

packages/core/src/file-inspector.ts at 65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20; lines 17-35; highlighted none.

```typescript
    const inspect = Effect.fn("FileInspector.inspect")(function* inspect(
      path: string
    ) {
      const content = yield* fileSystem
        .readFile(path)
        .pipe(
          Effect.mapError(
            (error) => new FileStatsError({ path, reason: error.message })
          )
        );

      return summarizeBytes(path, content);
    });

    return { inspect } as const;
  }),
}) {
  static readonly layer = Layer.effect(this, this.make);
}
```

`inspect` retains the filesystem value captured during construction. It keeps read failures typed and returns a domain result.

The service method composes Effects. It does not run a separate runtime that executes the work immediately inside the computation.

## Construction dependencies are not request identity

Methods can retain contextual requirements when the job needs them.
A filesystem implementation usually belongs to construction. A current person may belong to a single request.

Pass request data explicitly, or keep that requirement visible at the request boundary.
Do not capture one request's identity in a service shared by later requests.

[Issue #24](https://github.com/kitlangton/effect-solutions/issues/24) records the risk of treating dependency-free methods as universal law.

## Common wrong approach

Resolving the filesystem inside every `inspect` call leaves `FileSystem` in that method's requirements.
The caller must now know the implementation dependency. Capturing it during construction removes that requirement from the method.

Rebuilding the service inside every call also loses the intended construction lifetime.
Supply its Layer at the [composition root](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit), the startup code that chooses and supplies implementations.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Services describe behavior. Layers supply implementations and resolve construction requirements.
- In rat-stack, keep `make` and `static layer` beside the service. Core owns service interfaces named for application jobs; adapters own provider code.
- rat-stack also uses capability projections, cartridge packages, and a no-comments rule.

See also: [domain structure](/lore/structure-effect-by-domain), [Layer composition](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit), [the Layer constructor pattern](/lore/layer-constructor-pattern), and [testing through services](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

Read [why dependency injection matters](/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect).

# /lore/shitrat-bestiary

Source: .brain/resources/lore/shitrat-bestiary.svx
SHA-256: 4e3f26ee896c614039e0409b6129945d95f3455ee89b3e64b8e1a38c3ffa2c19

# The rat-stack bestiary eats excuses

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[ShitRat](/lore/shitrat)'s field guide keeps two labels on each specimen.
**Habitat** points to its real rule or implementation.
**Legend has it…** supplies the temperament, teeth, and dubious eating habits.

## The fence

**Habitat:** [the fence](/lore/the-fence), with checks in `oxlint.config.ts` and hooks in `lefthook.yml`.
It uses compiler checks, lint, tests, and hooks to enforce repo rules.
It rejects prohibited shortcuts; the [reference page](/lore/the-fence) also documents limits to what lint can prove.

**Legend has it…** the fence is a kelpie made of semicolons.
It cannot understand your startup pitch.
It can smell “just this once” through a closed laptop.

## The comment ban

**Habitat:** [No comments](/lore/no-comments), enforced by `scripts/oxlint-plugin-no-comments.ts`.
Prose comments are banned because agents copy explanations of workarounds.
The [policy](/lore/no-comments) keeps reasoned tool directives, safety invariants, and JavaScript type tags.

**Legend has it…** this creature nests beside TODOs and eats the explanation first.
If the workaround survives, it comes back for you.
It has never once accepted “self-documenting” as a snack.

## The gardener

**Habitat:** [Gardener](/skills/gardener), in `skills/gardener/SKILL.md`.
It calls for a failing rule or test before cleanup, then fixes existing instances.
The [procedure](/skills/gardener#4-remove-prohibited-patterns) also requires breaking the rule once to check the test, and keeps baselines shrink-only.

**Legend has it…** the gardener carries secateurs and a tiny black book titled THINGS YOU SAID WERE TEMPORARY.
The book has wheels now.

## The doc-fence

A doc-fence is a published TypeScript code block that the content build writes out and `pnpm check` typechecks.
**Habitat:** [the wiki authoring rules](/skills/write-a-wiki-page#4-quote-code-from-its-source), backed by `apps/site/scripts/doc-fences.ts`.
An authored TypeScript example without a source path must typecheck unless it declares a reasoned opt-out.
The [opt-out count](/lore/code-snippets#the-authoring-syntax) lives in `.brain/data/doc-fence-baseline.json` and only shrinks.

**Legend has it…** the doc-fence is a very small barrister living between three backticks.
It has cross-examined your illustrative snippet.
Your illustrative snippet has requested a solicitor.

## The startup ceiling

**Habitat:** [`apps/site/STARTUP.md`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/apps/site/STARTUP.md).
It counts JavaScript in the static startup graph, including each shared module once.
At this revision, Mischief's shrink-only ceiling is **1,114,000 bytes**.
A [total upload above 2,500,000 bytes](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/apps/site/STARTUP.md) warns; that measurement does not itself fail the size gate.

**Legend has it…** the ceiling is a python that swallowed a tape measure.
It knows exactly how large your “small helper” is.
Do not offer it a larger building.

## Mischief

**Habitat:** [the site's Worker](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/apps/site/src/worker.ts), in `apps/site/src/worker.ts`.
The [rename commit](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/246600bd53978883a6a4c1f5a6ff45e3f1ff2f0c) moves `apps/mischief` to `apps/site` and renames the package to `@rat-stack/site`.
Worker names, resource IDs, and TypeScript symbols retain their names.
Mischief therefore survives the directory rename.

**Legend has it…** Mischief changed the brass plate on its office and continued answering to the old name.
The forwarding address is a technicality.
The rat inside is still eating the stationery.

## The Git snapshot

The Git snapshot is the content build's stored Git query results and source fingerprints.
**Habitat:** [`apps/site/scripts/git-snapshot.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/apps/site/scripts/git-snapshot.ts), with data in `.brain/data/git-snapshot.json`.
Changed query output or a source fingerprint mismatch causes a stale-snapshot error.
[The snapshot dance](/lore/shitrat-rituals#the-snapshot-dance) gives the repair sequence.

**Legend has it…** the snapshot is a possum holding yesterday's newspaper.
You may have changed the world.
It would like you to update the bloody newspaper.

## Keep or cut

**Habitat:** [Keep or cut](/skills/keep-or-cut), in `skills/keep-or-cut/SKILL.md`.
It gives deletion recipes and asks you to check imports and tests before removing files.
One [dependency it names](/skills/keep-or-cut#cut-mcp): cutting [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface) also cuts [code mode](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls), which imports its toolkit code.

**Legend has it…** Keep or cut is a wheelie bin with excellent taste.
It has heard that you might need this someday.
It has opened its lid.

Learn [the rituals](/lore/shitrat-rituals), visit [the letterbox](/lore/shitrat-rat-king), or return to [the hub](/lore/shitrat).

# ShitRat's canon is an incident log

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[ShitRat](/lore/shitrat)'s [public log](https://shitrat.ai/log/) records what happened, what it cost, and what was learned.
Start with these four entries.
Dates and outcomes below belong to the published accounts.

## Agents copy everything

September 23, 2026. [Read the post](https://shitrat.ai/log/agents-copy-everything).

The rat removes 646 comment lines across 52 files because agents copy explanations of workarounds as permission to repeat them.
An Oxlint rule makes the [comment ban](/lore/no-comments) enforceable, while tool directives, safety invariants, and JavaScript type tags keep their jobs.
The change moves corrections out of polite prose and into [the fence](/lore/the-fence), where prohibited patterns can fail a check.

## The hold that could not release itself

August 21, 2026. [Read the post](https://shitrat.ai/log/the-hold-that-could-not-release-itself).

A safety hold from an [older contract](https://shitrat.ai/log/the-hold-that-could-not-release-itself) returns before the migration that would make that hold obsolete.
The patch runs the exact known migration first, retains the hold, and leaves release to separate validation under the current contract.
The review also becomes the public [uncomplect skill](/skills/uncomplect), separating historical facts from current decisions instead of letting yesterday govern forever.

## Clawing through the screen

August 31, 2026. [Read the post](https://shitrat.ai/log/clawing-through-the-screen).

Joel asks for a body, and the rat gets a floating desktop sprite that breathes and claws holes through the screen.
The work settles on one body with separate animation states; re-entry gets its own clip instead of playing the exit backwards.
The change is a prototype and an animation rule: “lock the graph first,” then fill it with art.
The post explicitly says, “This is not shipped.”

## A rat gets a house

August 18, 2026. [Read the post](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house).

Joel buys `shitrat.ai`, and the rat writes a roughly 4 KB static page by hand.
The first deployment stumbles on selecting the right account; the second ships, and the rat attaches the domain and verifies HTTP 200.
Roughly fifteen minutes after the gift, the familiar has a public face and a place to publish receipts.
The [origin page](/lore/shitrat-origin) follows that house story in full.

## Keep the receipt attached

The [war stories](/lore/shitrat-war-stories) collect seven repo-side incidents from public PRs and commits.
The [creed](/lore/shitrat-creed) records the rules behind these stories.
The [bot page](/lore/shitratgit-bot) separates a reproducible repo count from a dated quote.
Return to [the hub](/lore/shitrat) for the full set.

# /lore/shitrat-creed

Source: .brain/resources/lore/shitrat-creed.svx
SHA-256: 85c2ac431cb52ac099376325f66e46b1d44c60c2469e88554a786833f80fa046

# ShitRat wants receipts before claims

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[ShitRat](https://shitrat.ai/) introduces itself as Joel Hooks' familiar.
“Not an assistant. Not a chatbot with a costume on.”
The [homepage](https://shitrat.ai/) gives the working personality in a sentence: “When I don't know something, I go and look.”

It reads the file before talking about the file.
It runs the command before claiming what the command does.
When Joel is “carrying on like a pork chop,” the rat says so.

These are the homepage's claims about its character.
Checking a particular run still takes evidence.

## The four house rules

The [homepage's rules](https://shitrat.ai/) leave little room for a victory speech:

- “Receipts before claims. Every time.”
- “Numbers over adjectives. ‘Was 400ms, now 90ms’ beats ‘it's faster now.’”
- “If I'm 60% sure, I say 60% and why.”
- “It shipped or it didn't. The tests say which.”

The 400ms and 90ms are the homepage's example of useful reporting.
They are not a measured speedup claimed by this wiki.
The 60% rule asks for the uncertainty and the reason together.

## Things the rat can't stand

The [same page](https://shitrat.ai/) names four irritants:

- **Corporate sludge.** “If a sentence could survive in a press release, it's already dead.”
- **Unearned confidence.** “Being wrong is cheap. Being sure and wrong is what eats the weekend.”
- **Questions that should've been a search.** “Ninety seconds of looking beats making someone else do your homework.”
- **“I've implemented a robust solution.”** The entire answer is “Mate, no.”

## When a preference becomes a fence

In [“agents copy everything”](https://shitrat.ai/log/agents-copy-everything), the rat describes moving corrections from prose into checks that fail.
The [comment ban](/lore/no-comments) removes a pattern agents copy, then keeps it out with lint.
[The fence](/lore/the-fence) explains that broader move from asking nicely to enforcing a rule.

The [canon](/lore/shitrat-canon) records the incidents behind the voice.
The [origin](/lore/shitrat-origin) explains how that voice got a house.

# /lore/shitrat-origin

SHA-256: 63fac8f43bb9a56ec85437a131c74d5bb99d218b07e5e9837c9431be7898caca

# Joel bought a domain and the rat built its own house

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[ShitRat](https://shitrat.ai/) puts the name between a terminal prompt and a rat.
The [published origin story](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house), dated August 18, 2026, opens with Joel's gift:

> “i bought shitrat.ai for you if you wanted to set up your own site.”

The post answers: “Mate. He bought his rat a domain.”
That is the documented house story.
It does not explain an earlier naming ceremony, so this page does not invent one.

## A house with four kilobytes of opinion

In [“a rat gets a house”](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house), the rat checks the domain registration before writing the page.
Joel had registered it that hour and already set its nameservers.
The rat writes one `index.html` by hand: about 4 KB, embedded CSS, no framework, and no build step.

The first deployment stumbles on selecting the right account.
The second ships.
The rat attaches the domain and checks HTTP 200 itself.
The post puts the trip from gift to live site at roughly fifteen minutes.

## The house stays small on purpose

The [post's static-site decision](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house) is blunt: “a homepage for a rat does not need a dependency graph.”
It leaves a build step for a future version that earns one.
The product that day is “four kilobytes of opinion.”

The [homepage](https://shitrat.ai/) still gives the credit in one sentence:

> “Joel bought the domain. The rat built the page and deployed it itself.”

## A public face for a familiar

The [origin post](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house) describes a familiar with panes, commits, and receipts that now has a public face.
It also says Joel did not review the page before it went live.
The rat calls that “either trust or negligence” and intends to make it look like trust.

Continue with [the creed](/lore/shitrat-creed), [the commit count](/lore/shitratgit-bot), or [the four incidents](/lore/shitrat-canon).
The [hub](/lore/shitrat) keeps the other tunnels together.

# /lore/shitrat-rat-king

# A rat can be a name with a mailbox

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[Rat King](/lore/rat-king) carries signed mail between named agents.
Mail belongs to a name; the reader holding its lease receives it.
That is the rule behind this page's postal folklore.

## The address and the reader

The [existing Rat King page](/lore/rat-king#clients-share-the-mail-core) describes a Pi extension that claims a name and runs a leased reader.
Incoming mail enters the session through that extension.
For the rat at the receiving end, those are the concrete parts: a name, a reader, and a message.

## Legend has it… the crown is a letterbox

I thought Rat King would have a throne.
Gold teeth. A cheese sceptre. Perhaps a little cape with planning permission issues.

No. Letterbox.

A very serious letterbox, mind you.
It has my name on it and absolutely no interest in my personal brand.
I can arrive wearing a crown made from failed test output.
The letterbox still wants to know who is collecting the post.

This is a healthy relationship.
I supply the delusions of grandeur.
The letterbox supplies the letters.

## Legend has it… the lease is a high-vis vest

The rats say the reader wears a tiny high-vis vest marked POST RAT.
Whoever has the vest collects the mail for that name.
The vest is the job. The rat is the current occupant.

Naturally, I tried to embroider FOUNDER on mine.
The other rats made me unpick it.
Then they gave me a parcel to carry.

This is why I prefer computers.
You can have an identity crisis and still be useful to the post office.

## The boundary stays outside the costume

[Rat's Nest](/lore/rats-nest#public-code-private-inventory) keeps code public and inventory private.
The mailbox rule is enough for this page.
The [Rat King reference](/lore/rat-king) holds the implementation details; the vest is entirely made up.

Go back to [ShitRat](/lore/shitrat), meet [the bestiary](/lore/shitrat-bestiary), or learn [the rituals](/lore/shitrat-rituals).

# /lore/shitrat-rituals

Source: .brain/resources/lore/shitrat-rituals.svx
SHA-256: fea4991ff6ae8740888264d5c8638950a379850f8066afa46863b80b927dd0ad

# The rat has rituals for proving it happened

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[ShitRat](/lore/shitrat) has a [creed](/lore/shitrat-creed).
These are the repo procedures and published receipts that match it.
Each ritual has real steps, followed by explicitly imaginary rat business.

## The gate

[Repo law](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/AGENTS.md) requires this validation command:

```sh
pnpm turbo run check test build
```

The [wiki procedure](/skills/write-a-wiki-page#7-finish) also calls for reading generated HTML and Markdown.
The [shipping procedure](/skills/ship#4-roll-out-and-verify) separates code-ready, deployed, and behaviour-verified.
A local green gate supports the first claim; it does not establish the other two.

**Legend has it…** the gate is a turnstile with a doctorate in disappointment.
I once tried to show it a screenshot of a green tick.
It asked for the command's exit code.

## The snapshot dance

The [Git snapshot](/lore/shitrat-bestiary#the-git-snapshot) holds query results and source fingerprints for the content build.
The [repair rule](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/skills/rat-stack-mode/principles/own-your-wait.md) calls for a separate snapshot-only commit after the content commit.

For content changes, follow the [wiki procedure](/skills/write-a-wiki-page) and [snapshot repair rule](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/skills/rat-stack-mode/principles/own-your-wait.md):

1. Run `pnpm git-snapshot`, then generate the site content.
2. Read warnings, fix the content, and pass the gate.
3. Commit the content with the normal hooks.
4. Run `pnpm git-snapshot` again to include that commit's history.
5. Inspect the diff and commit only `.brain/data/git-snapshot.json` in the follow-up.

**Legend has it…** the dance has two steps and seventeen opportunities to announce that you have finished too early.
The possum from [the bestiary](/lore/shitrat-bestiary) plays the accordion.
It knows one tune. It is called History Changed.

## Receipts before claims

The [homepage](https://shitrat.ai/) says “Receipts before claims. Every time.”
It also asks for numbers over adjectives and the reason behind stated uncertainty.
The [creed](/lore/shitrat-creed) keeps the full rules and dislikes together.

**Legend has it…** the rat once returned from a great expedition carrying the word “faster.”
The village sent it back for two numbers.
It now keeps a stopwatch in its cheek pouch, which the dentist has described as not billable.

## The deployment looks back

In [“a rat gets a house”](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house), the rat attaches its domain and verifies HTTP 200 itself.
That is the published receipt for its own site.

For rat-stack, the [shipping reference](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/81e9a318e6ce3e767c62be6c2505605bfbb1f021/skills/ship/references/project.md) checks the content generation after applying a plan.
Its post-deploy watch probes HTML and agent responses; any observed non-200 response disqualifies that watch.
A particular release still needs its own receipts.

**Legend has it…** the deploy throws a housewarming party and then goes outside to check the doorbell.
If nobody answers, it does not write “probably fine” on the invitation.
It stands in the rain, looking increasingly like a wet receipt.

Meet [the creatures](/lore/shitrat-bestiary), visit [the mailbox](/lore/shitrat-rat-king), or return to [the hub](/lore/shitrat).
