# /lore/shitrat-war-stories

Source: .brain/resources/lore/shitrat-war-stories.svx
SHA-256: 0b5c200e974372bff042471119c351c7984e10ea1e3c178a6d52442064844b7e

# The war stories

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A [deploy rolls itself back](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/223) while the site is serving 200.
Five freshly published pages return to 404.
That is one of [ShitRat](/lore/shitrat)'s repo-side war stories.
The dates below belong to the public records; the passages marked **Legend has it…** belong to the rat.

## The deploy that mugged itself

November 7, 2026. [PR #223](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/223) and [PR #226](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/226).

The site serves 200, but [the deploying machine records 15 client-side transport errors among 1,445 observations](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/223).
The watch treats those status-0 results as failed routes, restores the old Cloudflare Worker versions, and sends five new pages back to 404.
The first fix retries transport errors and records them separately; real non-200 responses fail after the first cycle that sees them.

The follow-up requires two consecutive unreachable cycles and fails a completed watch when transport errors exceed 5% of observations.
It also fails early if even a healthy continuation leaves the final ratio above the limit.

**Legend has it…** the smoke alarm ate five rooms and invoiced the kettle.
The rat now asks whether the house is burning before giving the alarm a sledgehammer.

## Congratulations, your program exploded

November 7, 2026. [PR #220](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/220).

A failed [code mode](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls) program returns HTTP 200 with a `diagnostic` field.
A client trusting the status therefore reads failure as success.
The fix returns HTTP 422 with a typed `ExecuteError`; successful programs keep 200 and lose `diagnostic: null`.

The deployment checks change alongside the response, because an old check would reject the new shape and roll it back.
A generated-program test checks failure reporting across HTTP, [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface), [RPC](/lore/one-capability-every-surface), and the CLI; restoring the false 200 makes it fail.

**Legend has it…** the rat arrives at casualty wearing a badge that says 200 OK.
The nurse changes it to 422 and keeps the scissors.

## Mischief changes the brass plate

October 10, 2026. [Rename commit](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/246600bd53978883a6a4c1f5a6ff45e3f1ff2f0c).

The code moves from `apps/mischief` to `apps/site`, and the package becomes `@rat-stack/site`.
The commit calls this “Mechanical path updates only.”
[Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy) resource IDs, Worker names, and TypeScript symbols keep their names, so Mischief survives the move.

**Legend has it…** Mischief orders new business cards, eats the box, and answers to the old name when the bailiff calls.

## The demolition manual gets road-tested

November 7, 2026. [PR #221](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/221).

The homepage promises removal checklists, but the README covers only seven cuts.
The fix carries out each new tested cut in a scratch branch until `pnpm turbo run check test build` passes.
The checklists record the edits that worked; none of those scratch removals land.

Four parts of the content build get conditional Keep entries explaining their callers and what removal would lose.
The homepage also starts naming which packages go together.

**Legend has it…** the rat follows the flat-pack instructions backwards to establish which screws are structural.
The wardrobe has requested a witness.

## The ceiling gets an expiry date

November 2, 2026. [Dependency-bump commit](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/2623f8fd0192fa1e4d0462f27bde8f4e9341cdf4) and [the startup record](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/7511fdd2c7f2fa607cff1a22a1cba6f0bdeb3220/apps/site/STARTUP.md#temporary-raise-alchemy-beta85-and-effect-41).

[Repo law](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/7511fdd2c7f2fa607cff1a22a1cba6f0bdeb3220/AGENTS.md) says of startup ceilings: “Never raise them to accept growth.”
The dependency bump grows both startup sets, but loading [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface) on demand brings Mischief below its previous size.
Its ceiling drops from 1,247,000 to 1,114,000 bytes.

LearnFeedbackAuth has no MCP endpoint; its one recorded exception raises the ceiling by 60,000 bytes to 1,516,000.
The exception expires when Alchemy ships the bridge fix or on November 16, 2026, whichever comes first.

**Legend has it…** the building inspector finds a rat holding the ceiling up with a broom.
The broom has a removal date.
The rat has read it several times.

## Two accountants disagree about the shed

November 5, 2026. [PR #212](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/212).

Two typecheckers disagree about which imported files receive [Effect](/lore/effect-basics) diagnostics.
Patched `tsc` reports those diagnostics throughout the program; `effect-tsrs` reports them only in each project's included files.
The root and infrastructure projects therefore get different pass/fail answers.

The fix allows exactly the reported modules in those two scopes, leaving the severity map and base configuration unchanged.
The parity run goes from two failures to 29 passing checks.

**Legend has it…** one accountant counts the shed.
The other calls it a lifestyle choice.
The rat receives two invoices for one lawnmower.

## The bouncer eats the guest list

November 5, 2026. [PR #209](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/209).

The workshop's [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface) clients using protocol 2025-11-25 get empty-body 404s when a call after initialization reaches another running copy of the server.
The session lives in one copy's memory; about one in three multi-call production probes fails.
The fix stores one initialization record per session and replays it to rebuild the runtime.

That record contains the initialization body and three allowlisted headers, with no tool arguments or results.
A test reproduces the old 404 and checks requests through fresh front runtimes.

**Legend has it…** the doorman issues wristbands, eats his guest list, and charges the same rat admission again.
The rat is still standing in the doorway.

The [comment purge already has its canon entry](/lore/shitrat-canon#agents-copy-everything).
Meet the creatures in [the bestiary](/lore/shitrat-bestiary), or return to [the hub](/lore/shitrat).

9. [MCP sessions survive isolate changes](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/209)
   rat-stack. November 5, 2026: session memory causes 404s; stored initialization records let another runtime rebuild the session. Accessed 2026-11-07.

# ShitRat is Joel's familiar, with receipts

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

[ShitRat](https://shitrat.ai/) is Joel Hooks' familiar: an AI agent that lives in his terminal and reads files before talking about them.
The homepage rejects both “assistant” and “chatbot with a costume on.”
Its introduction ends with a warning: “A rat — and rats get into things.”

Joel bought the domain; [the rat built the page and deployed it itself](https://shitrat.ai/log/a-rat-gets-a-house).
The house rules put receipts before claims and numbers before adjectives.
The [public log](https://shitrat.ai/log/) records what happened, what it cost, and what was learned.

## Pick a tunnel

## Legend has it…

The rat keeps a tiny clipboard under the floorboards.
Every time someone says “robust solution,” it adds another checkbox.
Nobody has seen the bottom of the page.

# /lore/shitratgit-bot

Source: .brain/resources/lore/shitratgit-bot.svx
SHA-256: 3ecb73bb66fb9d4f676704e41535c03b104478eaac08a299b4ee990dc46c2e2a

# shitratgit\[bot] leaves a countable trail

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

`shitratgit[bot]` is the bot author name on [1,314 commits in rat-stack's history](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commits/7570e37828ac6ba3da991a8ddca2f4298dcd5320/).
This is [ShitRat](/lore/shitrat)'s commit trail in this repository, counted on November 7, 2026.
The same name signs the commits on [the rat's own site](https://github.com/joelhooks/shitrat-ai/commits/main/).
The count stops at `7570e37828ac6ba3da991a8ddca2f4298dcd5320`, rat-stack's `main` when it was counted.

## Count the trail

At [that revision](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commits/7570e37828ac6ba3da991a8ddca2f4298dcd5320/):

- Git reaches **1,365 commits**.
- **1,314** have the exact author name `shitratgit[bot]`.
- The [earliest bot-authored commit by author date](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/3c3c52928658e6f91871a99376a33a17e63876d1) is July 22, 2026.
- That commit is `3c3c52928658e6f91871a99376a33a17e63876d1`, titled [“chore: update Effect v4 to beta.99”](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/3c3c52928658e6f91871a99376a33a17e63876d1).

The count includes all reachable history, including merge commits.
It matches the author name exactly.
It does not measure lines written, review quality, or deployments.
A commit count cannot prove those things.

## Reproduce the count

Run these commands in a checkout containing [the counted revision](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/7570e37828ac6ba3da991a8ddca2f4298dcd5320):

```sh
at=7570e37828ac6ba3da991a8ddca2f4298dcd5320
git rev-list --count "$at"
git log "$at" --format='%an' | grep -Fxc 'shitratgit[bot]'
git log "$at" --format='%aI %an %H' | grep -F ' shitratgit[bot] ' | sort | head -1
```

## The older receipt stays older

On September 23, 2026, [“agents copy everything”](https://shitrat.ai/log/agents-copy-everything) said:

> “Joel called it my stack this week. Fair. I wrote 94 of its 106 commits.”

That is a dated first-person quote from the post.
The 94-of-106 receipt and the 1,314-of-1,365 count describe different moments, and the post does not say how it counted.
Neither is a live counter.

## A commit is not permission to deploy

The [repo's worker autonomy ladder](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/7570e37828ac6ba3da991a8ddca2f4298dcd5320/AGENTS.md) allows workers to commit on their branches.
It prohibits workers from merging or deploying.
For the rat's own public-site deployment story, read [the origin](/lore/shitrat-origin).
For why the code should argue back, read [the fence](/lore/the-fence) and [the canon](/lore/shitrat-canon).

# /lore/steady-state-recycles-resources

Source: .brain/resources/lore/steady-state-recycles-resources.svx
SHA-256: 11b0e5a7f2704aa70efbf597e593c61ce44e63d5d9c00740e69e933c15102e70

# Steady state recycles resources

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Growing logs, retained rows, caches, and objects need a counter-mechanism. Normal operation should not depend on repeated manual cleanup.

> The Steady State pattern says, for every mechanism that accumulates a resource, some other mechanism must recycle that resource.

Source: [Q08](/lore/durability-bibliography#q08); [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it).

## Failure it prevents

Memory, storage, or latency fails after enough otherwise-successful operations.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Cache` and [Scope](/lore/scopes-own-resources) cover runtime lifetime. `PersistedQueue.layerCleanup` handles retained queue records. Durable domain data still needs a storage policy and maintenance owner.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Cache.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Scope.ts`, `packages/effect/src/persistence/PersistedQueue.ts`.

## How to check

Inspect growth over repeated work. Check retention against replay and dedupe requirements before deleting recovery evidence. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Queries need result bounds](/lore/queries-need-result-bounds), [Dead letters need a return path](/lore/dead-letters-need-a-return-path).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/scopes-own-resources).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Nygard, Michael T. Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software. Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007.](https://archive.org/details/releaseitdesignd0000nyga)
   Pragmatic Bookshelf. §4.4 Unbounded Result Sets; Chapter 5 Stability Patterns: §5.1 Timeouts, §5.2 Circuit Breaker, §5.3 Bulkheads, §5.4 Steady State, §5.5 Fail Fast, §5.6 Handshaking, §5.7 Test Harness, §5.8 Decoupling Middleware. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. Cache.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Cache.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

3. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. Scope.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Scope.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

4. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. persistence/PersistedQueue.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/persistence/PersistedQueue.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/structure-effect-by-domain

Source: .brain/resources/lore/structure-effect-by-domain.svx
SHA-256: a7a61e2923060f516aaaf576c838a5a7a60902da1c7e0b4abef1908512ae40d9

# Structure an Effect codebase by domain

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A domain is an area of application work. A service is a named interface for that work.
A Layer describes how to build a service and supply its dependencies.

Group files by domain: `src/coding/edit.ts` puts an edit operation with the coding work it belongs to.
Keep one service and its Layer in each file. Capture dependencies when building the service, so callers need only that service.

An entrypoint is where the application starts. Its composition root chooses and supplies implementations.
Keep platform adapters behind service interfaces. An adapter implements an interface for a platform or provider.

[Justin Bennett asked about folders and service organization](https://x.com/just_be_dev/status/2107194260860613059).
[Sam Goodwin's answer](https://x.com/samgoodwin89/status/2107204053151428850):

> src/{domain} instead of src/{mechanism}. E.g. src/coding/edit.ts instead of src/tools/edit.ts. "tools" is the mechanism, "coding" is the domain.

## The shape in one tree

A small app can use this layout:

```text
src/
├── files/
│   ├── file-inspector.ts    Service, dependency capture, Layer
│   ├── stats.ts             Schema and expected errors
│   └── inspect-machine.ts   Optional finite lifecycle
├── platform/
│   └── files-node.ts        Platform adapter Layer
└── main.ts                  Composition root and runtime entrypoint
test/
└── files/
    └── file-inspector.test.ts
```

Domain folders own behavior. `platform` supplies implementations.
rat-stack separates these jobs into packages; a small app can keep them in one package.

## The rules that hold it together

### Capture dependencies when constructing a service

Keep the service interface and its Layer together.
`FileInspector` captures `FileSystem` during construction. Its methods have no filesystem requirement.

packages/core/src/file-inspector.ts at 54d356037c994f89698760a4727be71d0005a087; lines 6-16,33-35; highlighted none.

```typescript
export class FileInspector extends Context.Service<
  FileInspector,
  {
    readonly inspect: (
      path: string
    ) => Effect.Effect<FileStats, FileStatsError>;
  }
>()("@rat-stack/core/FileInspector", {
  make: Effect.gen(function* makeFileInspector() {
    const fileSystem = yield* FileSystem.FileSystem;

}) {
  static readonly layer = Layer.effect(this, this.make);
}
```

**What to notice:** Construction needs the dependency; callers need only `FileInspector`.
See [service construction](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) for the full pattern.

### Provide Layers at the entrypoint

The composition root chooses implementations and supplies the application's services and their dependencies.
Give each entrypoint its own root. Our CLI assembles dependencies before running the program.

apps/cli/src/cli.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 22-35; highlighted none.

```typescript
  Effect.provide(
    Layer.mergeAll(
      Layer.provideMerge(FileInspector.layer, NodeServices.layer),
      remoteJoinInterestLayer,
      localPromptLibraryLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(NodeServices.layer)),
      localCafeDirectoryLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(NodeServices.layer)),
      localLearnLayer,
      Flags.defaults(eventFlags),
      Approval.denyAll
    )
  )
);

NodeRuntime.runMain(program);
```

`Effect.provide` resolves requirements before `NodeRuntime.runMain` runs the final Effect.
See [Layer composition](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit).

### Keep ports inside and adapters outside

Domain code uses a service interface that names the application's job.
Core owns `SubscriberIntake`; `packages/subscriber-delivery` implements it. Apps provide that implementation.
See [hexagonal architecture](/lore/hexagonal-architecture).

### Keep related definitions with the domain

- Put input, output, and failure schemas in the domain's contract. [Decode at boundaries with Schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary).
- Declare expected failures with useful context. `FileStatsError` keeps the failed path and filesystem reason. See [the error model](/lore/error-model).
- In rat-stack, a [machine](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines) owns finite modes, cancellation, or legal event sequences. Keep it beside the behavior it controls.
- Mirror domain folders in tests. [Supply test services through Layers](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place).

## House style versus Effect idiom

- **Services and composable Layers**: `make` and `static layer` in the same file
- **Schema-backed boundaries**: Capability contracts and derived interface projections
- **Replaceable implementations**: Cartridges with an add/remove test
- **Typed failures and scoped effects**: XState lifecycles through `@xstate/effect`
- **Effect-aware tests**: Property/model testing and a manual-runtime ban
- **Explicit requirements**: A type-aware lint fence
- **No prescribed comment policy**: No prose comments in code

## Where disagreement lives

Sam favors domain folders. Effect leaves folder layout to the application.
Sam also calls one API route per file potentially controversial. rat-stack keeps one capability per file and derives routes.

A monorepo is one repository containing several packages.
Choose monorepo versus single-package layout separately from the service graph.

New to Effect? Start with [Effect basics](/lore/effect-basics).

# /lore/supervision-is-a-recovery-policy

Source: .brain/resources/lore/supervision-is-a-recovery-policy.svx
SHA-256: e5186176a67c5570dd965caa808fb68bdd6c9b45851cc736461b1900649ffe30

# Supervision chooses what restarts

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

OTP restart strategies distinguish independent children from dependent siblings. A persistently broken child also needs a limit on repeated restarts.

> The point of letting an entire subsystem terminate and be restarted is that it brings you back to a state known to function properly.

Source: [Q01](/lore/durability-bibliography#q01); [B1](/lore/durability-bibliography#b1-erlang-and-otp-in-action), [B2](/lore/durability-bibliography#b2-elixir-in-action), [B3](/lore/durability-bibliography#b3-designing-elixir-systems-with-otp).

## Failure it prevents

Healthy siblings restart unnecessarily, or dependent siblings continue with stale state.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

No OTP restart supervisor was found in the checked source. [Scope](/lore/scopes-own-resources) and `FiberSet` handle lifetime. Use XState for explicit restart modes and a host for runtime restart.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`, `packages/effect/src/Scope.ts`, `packages/effect/src/FiberSet.ts`.

## How to check

Generate child failures and repeated restart attempts. Check affected dependents, escalation, and reconstructed state. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Restart must reconstruct known state](/lore/restart-from-known-state), [Circuit breakers have state](/lore/circuit-breakers-have-state).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

# /lore/tests-that-earn-their-place

Source: .brain/resources/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place.svx
SHA-256: b6b924475198ed461badbfceeb3a57cb703e1b2bc3db72d97e376467d8cade7b

# Tests prove behavior through supplied services

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A service is a named interface. A Layer describes how to build a service and supply its dependencies.
A Scope owns cleanup. A capability is a named action; a projection converts it into an interface.

Name the behavior that lacks proof before adding a test.
Supply test services through Layers, return an Effect, and let `@effect/vitest` own its execution.

## Test behavior independently of the implementation

A test that repeats the implementation cannot detect the same mistake in both places.
A snapshot that only records a changed file does not prove a domain rule.
If the existing suite already covers the reported behavior, fix the cause without adding a duplicate test.

Our projection tests execute the produced CLI command, HTTP route, MCP tool, RPC call, or sandbox call.
They check results and declared failures. Returning a projection object does not establish correct behavior.

## Run an Effect through supplied services

`it.effect` runs the Effect returned by the test. `it.layer` supplies services and their dependencies to a block of tests.
The file-inspection integration test uses real platform services and a scoped temporary file:

packages/core/test/file-inspector.test.ts at 65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20; lines 5-5,24-34; highlighted none.

```typescript
import { FileInspector } from "../src/index.js";
it.layer(TestLayer)("FileInspector", (test) => {
  test.effect("reads a file through the Effect filesystem", () =>
    Effect.gen(function* readsThroughFileSystem() {
      const file = yield* writeTempFile("notes.txt", "one two\nthree\n");
      const inspector = yield* FileInspector;

      const stats = yield* inspector.inspect(file);

      expect(stats).toMatchObject({ bytes: 14, lines: 2, words: 3 });
    })
  );
```

Share a Layer when tests need a common expensive resource.
Do not assume its mutable state resets between tests in the same block.
Use fresh construction or explicit reset when the behavior needs isolation.

`TestClock` controls Effect time for sleeps and retries. Use it instead of waiting for wall-clock delays in a behavior test.
Use `it.live` for an integration test that needs live runtime services.

## Choose the smallest proof that fits the rule

- **One interface between components**: An integration example with supplied services
- **A rule over many inputs**: `it.prop` or `it.effect.prop`
- **State that depends on earlier actions**: A model checked after generated commands
- **UI behaviour, timers, and races**: A [Foldkit Scene](/lore/ui-behaviour-is-a-scene)

Generated inputs do not create the assertion. The test still needs an independent statement of correct behavior.

`Arbitrary.schema` derives input generators from Schema.
Pure properties use `it.prop`; properties returning Effects use `it.effect.prop`.
The core suite generates names and checks that validation trims them before applying the length rule.

## Keep the assertion independent

The name-validation property checks the length rule after trimming each generated string:

packages/core/test/join-identity.test.ts at f1e24f7ee9f9b5f4a06574cb8c1646de001e4a3f; lines 101-120; highlighted none.

```typescript
it.effect.prop(
  "names trim before the nonempty 100-character bound",
  { input: Arbitrary.schema(Schema.String) },
  ({ input }) =>
    Effect.gen(function* names() {
      const trimmed = input.trim();

      const exit = yield* Schema.decodeEffect(ApplicantName)(input).pipe(
        Effect.exit
      );

      expect(Exit.isSuccess(exit)).toBe(
        trimmed.length > 0 && trimmed.length <= 100
      );

      if (Exit.isSuccess(exit)) {
        expect(exit.value).toBe(trimmed);
      }
    })
);
```

The assertion does not call `ApplicantName` to decide whether a name is valid.
It states the accepted length directly and checks the trimmed result.

When the sensitive-query test was first written, deleting `token` from the filter did not fail a test that reused that filter.
An independent sensitive-key property closed the gap.
[Property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) records that planted violation and the smaller counterexample.

## Generate histories when order matters

The inspection lifecycle keeps its first terminal outcome after later commands.
The model generates action sequences and checks each step:

packages/core/test/inspect-machine.model.test.ts at f1e24f7ee9f9b5f4a06574cb8c1646de001e4a3f; lines 23-25,214-219; highlighted none.

```typescript
const Command = Schema.Literals(["succeed", "fail", "probe"]);

const commands = Arbitrary.array(Arbitrary.schema(Command), { maxLength: 30 });
  it.effect.prop(
    "real actor preserves generated input, typed outcomes and terminal immutability",
    { generated: commands, scenario: Scenario },
    ({ generated, scenario }) => replayActor(scenario, generated),
    { arbitrary: { runs: 200 } }
  );
```

[Model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing) explains how to check the system against a model after each step.
[Agents explore, tests remember](/lore/agents-explore-tests-remember) explains how exploration can expose a behavior gap worth making repeatable.

## Common wrong approach

Plant a violation in the behavior it claims to protect. Observe failure, then restore the implementation and observe success.

Do not rewrite the test's expected result to match a broken implementation.
Keep the counterexample or missing assertion that explains the behavior gap.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Effect-aware tests supply runtime services, own scopes, and support controlled time.
- In rat-stack, no manual Effect runtime in tests. Prefer properties and models; prove new properties with planted violations.
- Live-provider behavior needs separate proof for each cartridge.

See also: [properties](/lore/property-based-testing), [models](/lore/model-based-testing), [scenes](/lore/ui-behaviour-is-a-scene), [exploration](/lore/agents-explore-tests-remember), and [the fence](/lore/the-fence).

Read [why dependency injection matters](/lore/dependency-injection-is-the-reason-to-choose-effect).

# /lore/the-fence

Source: .brain/resources/lore/the-fence.svx
SHA-256: 14f0a207b24f7c07b6e1b1098d0b20c45b10a0a229b67823965a3445cdc8d757

# The fence

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

The fence is the compiler checks, lint rules, tests, and hooks that enforce project rules.

“Cheating is uncomfortable” means the repo must stop bad shortcuts. Type-aware Oxlint checks project boundaries and patterns. Effect language-service diagnostics run through TypeScript. Lefthook runs checks before a commit, and harness hooks block `git … --no-verify`.

If an enforced check and a paragraph disagree, follow the enforced rule and fix the paragraph.

The pieces live in `oxlint.config.ts`, `scripts/oxlint-plugin-boundaries.ts`, `scripts/oxlint-plugin-patterns.ts`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `lefthook.yml`, and `scripts/vcs-command-policy.js`. `pnpm turbo run check test build` is the required validation command. Do not weaken a hook to get a green result.

A fence has limits. The lint rules use syntax and known aliases; they do not resolve every dynamic import, package condition, or cross-file re-export. The public Brain note [Oxlint rule limits](/resources/lint-rule-limits) lists those cases.

When lint misses a case, improve the rule or boundary. These rules cannot establish whole-program behavior.

## Where to enforce a correction

Lauren Tan describes five places to put a correction, from more durable to less enforceable: the codebase, static analysis, rules, skills, and style guides. She says to move a correction as high on that ladder as it can go. [Watch from 15:00](https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2101938030122868736/vid/avc1/3442x2160/BQlPlAZCEVPDemv1.mp4#t=900) [18:20](https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2101938030122868736/vid/avc1/3442x2160/BQlPlAZCEVPDemv1.mp4#t=1100).

Her Dune talk describes an agent-oriented framework where each folder has an owner and process boundaries are visible in the code tree. She sums up the design goal as making the shortcut the right path. [Watch from 19:01](https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2101938030122868736/vid/avc1/3442x2160/BQlPlAZCEVPDemv1.mp4#t=1141) [27:45](https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2101938030122868736/vid/avc1/3442x2160/BQlPlAZCEVPDemv1.mp4#t=1665).

See [Lauren Tan's talk](/lore/poteto-lauren-tan-2500-prs-dune) for the source and [no comments](/lore/no-comments) for one house rule the fence enforces. See [tests that earn their place](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place) for the testing law.

# /lore/there-is-no-isr-on-cloudflare

Source: .brain/resources/lore/there-is-no-isr-on-cloudflare.svx
SHA-256: b0c1ca796964b8c97154c62b67b7091837d7513e75107117be1f5c795e37efab

# There is no ISR on Cloudflare

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

ISR means incremental static regeneration: storing generated content and refreshing it later.
A Cloudflare Worker runs request-handling code. Its entrypoint is where that code starts.

There is no SvelteKit `isr` switch for the Cloudflare adapter. [That configuration belongs to adapter-vercel](https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/adapter-vercel).

[Vercel ISR](https://vercel.com/docs/incremental-static-regeneration) stores generated content and regenerates it. [Kit #661](https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/661) asks for a general regeneration feature.

Cloudflare can still cache rendered pages.

[Workers Cache](https://blog.cloudflare.com/workers-cache/) puts a cache in front of a Worker entrypoint. Its [stale-while-revalidate behavior](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/cache/) serves a stale response while the Worker refreshes it.

## What our comparison proves

We compare three local candidates:

- A static-assets gateway.
- A SvelteKit prerender gateway.
- A Workers Cache entrypoint.

The cache candidate creates a marker inside the rendering entrypoint. Repeated identical requests do not reuse it.

An assets response carries `CF-Cache-Status: HIT`. That proves only asset-cache reuse. The selected Miniflare implementation does not implement Workers Cache handling.

The cache candidate's home-page Markdown timings are:

- **Cold: first application request in a fresh runtime**: 8.25 ms
- **Warm: median of 20 sequential requests**: 1.69 ms

Neither number measures reuse of a cached response in Cloudflare's data centers (`HIT`).

The check does not prove:

- Stale-while-revalidate.
- Purge.
- Separate caching for HTML and Markdown responses across Workers Cache HITs.

The accepted configuration leaves cache behavior unproven.

## What we choose

We choose [static assets](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/commit/a337a96). [`apps/site/src/static-assets.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/static-assets.ts) serves separate HTML and Markdown assets. The dynamic signup page stays outside that path.

See [Worker init runs twice](/lore/init-runs-twice) for another boundary a local check can miss.

   Primary source. Vercel ISR Accessed 2026-10-02.

3. [Add incremental static regeneration](https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/issues/661)
   GitHub. Add incremental static regeneration Accessed 2026-10-02.

4. [Workers Cache announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/workers-cache/)
   Primary source. Workers Cache announcement Accessed 2026-10-02.

# /lore/timeouts-bound-waiting

Source: .brain/resources/lore/timeouts-bound-waiting.svx
SHA-256: 011a9fc3ce60253334d9f484ed829e55b8d65badaf498e88f99356776a3b4a0c

# Timeouts bound waiting

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Fallible waits need finite bounds. Carry the caller’s remaining deadline across [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) boundaries rather than granting each hop a fresh full wait.

> The timeout is a simple mechanism allowing you to stop waiting for an answer once you think it will not come.

Source: [Q05](/lore/durability-bibliography#q05); [B4](/lore/durability-bibliography#b4-release-it), [B12](/lore/durability-bibliography#b12-site-reliability-engineering).

## Failure it prevents

Abandoned requests occupy resources while their downstream calls continue.

## Our Effect 4.0.0 reading

`Effect.timeout` and timeoutOption support local timeout policy. Protocols must carry deadline and cancellation. Foreign operations must cooperate with interruption.

Source: `packages/effect/src/Effect.ts`.

## How to check

Delay the dependency past the deadline. Check released capacity and reconcile any uncertain remote write. This check is our proposal. The books do not prescribe it.

Continue with [Retry load needs a budget](/lore/retry-load-needs-a-budget), [Retry needs idempotent effects](/lore/retry-needs-idempotency).

Connect this to [the existing rat-stack guidance](/lore/concurrent-work-needs-an-owner).

Use [the durability skill](/skills/durability) for the full review. Return to [the durability index](/lore/durability).

## Sources

1. [Nygard, Michael T. Release It!: Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software. Pragmatic Bookshelf, 2007.](https://archive.org/details/releaseitdesignd0000nyga)
   Pragmatic Bookshelf. §4.4 Unbounded Result Sets; Chapter 5 Stability Patterns: §5.1 Timeouts, §5.2 Circuit Breaker, §5.3 Bulkheads, §5.4 Steady State, §5.5 Fail Fast, §5.6 Handshaking, §5.7 Test Harness, §5.8 Decoupling Middleware. Accessed 2026-10-23.

2. [Beyer, Betsy; Jones, Chris; Petoff, Jennifer; Murphy, Niall Richard, editors. Site Reliability Engineering: How Google Runs Production Systems. O’Reilly, 2016.](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/)
   O’Reilly. Chapter 3 Embracing Risk; Chapter 22 Addressing Cascading Failures (Mike Ulrich); Chapter 26 General Principles of SRE as Applied to Data Integrity; Chapter 27 Reliable Product Launches at Scale. Section-only excerpts limit detailed attribution. Accessed 2026-10-23.

3. [Effect contributors. Effect 4.0.0. Effect.ts](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/67ba4e46a11ccda0b6761578bfd22c04ae00167d/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts)
   Effect-TS. Pinned source for our Effect mapping, not a claim from the book. Accessed 2026-10-23.

# /lore/tokenize-before-slicing

Source: .brain/resources/lore/tokenize-before-slicing.svx
SHA-256: 7b27f473a75885ae4485949ec3a8f7eefbac456c65881a6ab502cee17926dfa2

# Tokenize the whole file before slicing

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Tokenization splits source text into parts with syntax roles, such as strings and comments.
A highlighter uses those roles to style code.

The [code-snippets design brief](/lore/code-snippets) requires whole-file tokenization.
The highlighter receives the full source before the pipeline selects lines.
Shiki exposes [`codeToTokens`](https://shiki.style/guide/install) for token output.

An excerpt can start inside a multiline comment or string.
Tokenizing only the excerpt removes the preceding source from the highlighter's input.

The proposed pipeline:

1. Tokenizes every source line.
2. Selects the requested ranges.
3. Keeps the original line numbers.
4. Inserts a collapsed gap between separated ranges.

A collapsed gap labels omitted lines separately from source lines.

The planned property compares excerpt tokens with the same lines from whole-file tokenization.
It includes multiline comments and template strings.
See [property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing).

Both renderers consume [one snippet model](/lore/one-snippet-model-two-renderers).
See [the glossary](/glossary) for whole-file tokenization and collapsed gap.

## Sources

1. [Shiki installation and usage](https://shiki.style/guide/install)
   Primary source. codeToTokens API Accessed 2026-10-02.

2. [Code-snippets design brief](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/.brain/resources/lore/code-snippets.svx)
   Primary source. Whole-file tokenization requirement Accessed 2026-10-02.

# /lore/trace-meaningful-operations

Source: .brain/resources/lore/trace-meaningful-operations.svx
SHA-256: d466f51d3ceeaec31a4b3c181786bbb299acbe432779de95258ddb9371ce7cd7

# Trace operations where they mean something

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Telemetry means logs, metrics, and traces.

Name the operation a person needs to understand. Add only context safe for that operation's telemetry.

A tracing span records an operation's timing and outcome. Export is a separate delivery step.

## Name meaningful operations

`FileInspector.inspect` uses a named `Effect.fn`:

packages/core/src/file-inspector.ts at 65e9465f38092e24486392f22c08f45d61230c20; lines 8-25; highlighted none.

```typescript
  {
    readonly inspect: (
      path: string
    ) => Effect.Effect<FileStats, FileStatsError>;
  }
>()("@rat-stack/core/FileInspector", {
  make: Effect.gen(function* makeFileInspector() {
    const fileSystem = yield* FileSystem.FileSystem;

    const inspect = Effect.fn("FileInspector.inspect")(function* inspect(
      path: string
    ) {
      const content = yield* fileSystem
        .readFile(path)
        .pipe(
          Effect.mapError(
            (error) => new FileStatsError({ path, reason: error.message })
          )
```

Use a named `fn` for a reusable operation that deserves a span.
Use `withSpan` around an existing Effect when that boundary carries useful meaning.
Use `fnUntraced` for reusable functions that do not need tracing, especially small library functions and frequently executed code.

Do not create a span merely because a helper exists.
Choose boundaries that answer a question about the job's duration, dependencies or failure.

## Add safe attributes deliberately

A span name should remain stable across requests.
Put safe variation in attributes instead of generating a new name for every input.
Keep unrestricted input, credentials, request bodies and private identities out of telemetry.

- **Useful context**: operation phase or bounded outcome name, a deliberate public category, or a measured count relevant to the operation.
- **Avoid**: full request or response bodies, credentials and authorization headers, unrestricted input, or private identity.

Structured attributes can outlive the request. Structure does not make a private value safe.

Use `annotateCurrentSpan` when adding attributes inside the operation.
Use `annotateSpans` when supplying annotations through an enclosing Effect.
Review the resulting payload as well as the annotation call.

## Supply an exporter, serializer and transport

The exporter prepares trace data. The serializer encodes it. The transport sends it.

OTLP means OpenTelemetry Protocol. A collector receives trace data.

The checked fixture composes the OTLP tracer with JSON serialization and an in-memory HTTP client:

packages/core/test/trace-export.test.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 51-65; highlighted none.

```typescript
      const tracing = OtlpTracer.layer({
        resource: { serviceName: "wiki-fixture" },
        url: "https://collector.example.test/v1/traces",
      }).pipe(
        Layer.provide(OtlpSerialization.layerJson),
        Layer.provide(Layer.succeed(HttpClient.HttpClient, client))
      );

      yield* Effect.scoped(
        Effect.void.pipe(
          Effect.withSpan("fixture.read"),
          Effect.annotateSpans({ phase: "read" }),
          Effect.provide(tracing)
        )
      );
```

These observability modules are marked unstable in the exact 4.0.0 source.
A stable package version does not make every exported module's API stable.
Keep the exact pin and check its source before changing exporter composition.

## Check the delivery boundary you actually exercised

The fixture's transport decodes outbound JSON through a small Schema.
It records the payload in a Ref instead of contacting a collector.
After shutdown, the test requires the operation name and the annotation key.

packages/core/test/trace-export.test.ts at 4019cffbcbdb282d6f006854ff5b1f26d3b407e0; lines 66-79; highlighted none.

```typescript

      const spans = (yield* Ref.get(deliveries)).flatMap((delivery) =>
        delivery.resourceSpans.flatMap((resource) =>
          resource.scopeSpans.flatMap((scope) => scope.spans)
        )
      );

      expect(spans.map((span) => span.name)).toContain("fixture.read");
      expect(
        spans.flatMap((span) =>
          span.attributes.map((attribute) => attribute.key)
        )
      ).toContain("phase");
    })
```

The fixture observes a serialized export request. It does not prove backend acceptance, storage, or a production exporter configuration.

- **Named `fn` in source**: An instrumentation boundary exists
- **Decoded outbound request in the fixture**: This composed exporter emits the expected trace fields
- **Collector receipt**: That collector accepted the payload
- **A queried stored trace**: The backend retained a trace you can retrieve

None of these observations substitutes for the next delivery boundary.

## Native tracing includes platform data

`TRACES_ENABLED` defaults to `false`. `TRACES_HEAD_SAMPLING_RATE` defaults to `0.01` and accepts finite values from zero through one.

The Effect tracer drops arbitrary attributes, events and links. Its native completion attribute records only a fixed outcome.
Its tests cover this boundary. They do not prove privacy for Cloudflare's automatic spans.

[Cloudflare documents these automatic fields](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/spans-and-attributes/):

- **Fetch handler**: Full URL, path, accept headers, language, user agent, geographic data and ASN
- **Outbound fetch**: Full URL and query, selected headers, method, status and body sizes
- **Cache operation**: Request URL, selected cache and conditional headers, and payload sizes
- **D1 and Durable Object SQL**: SQL text; Durable Object SQL also records query bindings
- **KV and R2**: Keys, prefixes, metadata and operation details; R2 also lists encryption-key-related fields
- **RPC**: Method or property path, target kind and correlation IDs
- **Email handler**: Sender, recipient and message size
- **Root and child spans**: Worker identity, invocation/version IDs and region; root spans add outcome and timing

Full URLs and query strings can contain tokens or email addresses.
SQL bindings, storage keys and custom metadata can contain private values.
The Effect attribute policy does not redact these platform fields.

For outbound fetch, the listed headers include content-type, content-length, accept and accept-encoding.
Fetch handlers also list accept-language.

The documentation lists body sizes. Body contents, Authorization values and Cookie values are absent from that list.
That list does not prove that all runtime versions omit other fields.
The representation of R2 encryption-key-related fields remains unverified here.

Owner approval is required before enabling native traces. Review this list and the authenticated plan before changing the flag.
A low sampling rate reduces collection volume. It does not make captured private values safe.

Mischief and RpcBackend register a per-event telemetry Layer.
The Website builds its native tracer inside each request.
Its development and prerender paths work without the Cloudflare runtime.
These Layers retain no request tracer or async-context map across requests.

## Keep other observers distinct

[Devtools](/systems/devtools) records capability calls and watched actor lifecycles.
[Request analytics](/systems/analytics) captures request events through its own sink.
Neither system substitutes for trace-export evidence.

Logs also have their own logger and export configuration.
Do not claim a log was delivered because it appeared in a local console.

## Common mistakes

- Assume naming a span installs a collector.
- Treat a test transport as a live backend.
- Put every argument into telemetry for convenience.
- Copy exporter settings from a different Effect version without checking its dependencies.

## Effect idiom and house rule

- Instrument meaningful operations and compose explicit observability Layers where the application starts and runs Effects.
- In rat-stack, keep private values scoped and report each observed delivery boundary honestly.
- In rat-stack, actor watching and capability recording remain their own devtools paths.

Next, [run Effect at the integration boundary](/lore/run-effect-at-the-boundary) and connect observability lifetime to its runtime owner.
Return to the [Effect reading order](/lore/effect-basics#read-next).

# An agent applied through Markdown and HTTP

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

Our first observed agent application uses the [Markdown workshop page](/tokenmaxx) and [llms.txt](/llms.txt). The request reconstruction contains three agent requests: two reads, then one POST.
GET reads a page. POST sends application data.

- **Start**: GET /tokenmaxx with text/markdown
- **0.263 seconds later**: GET /llms.txt
- **18 minutes 16 seconds later**: POST /api/joinInterest

The reconstruction records:

- No requests for OpenAPI, AGENTS.md, lore, or MCP.
- One POST and no retry.
- A 200 submission response.
- Confirmation 88 seconds after submission.

## What the requests do not tell us

The 18-minute gap fits the [page's interview and approval flow](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/content/tokenmaxx.md). The reconstruction contains neither the agent's questions nor the person's answers.

Browser activity and agent requests are linked by timing only. The user agent does not name the software running the agent. We cannot identify which agent runs the calls.

This is one counts-only observation from our request analytics. Other calls may need [OpenAPI](/lore/openapi-describes-the-refusal-too) or [MCP](/lore/mcp-is-another-surface).

[Interest signup](/systems/interest) keeps the consent and email-confirmation rules. [HATEOAS](/lore/hateoas) explains why the page carries the next action.

# /lore/ui-behaviour-is-a-scene

Source: .brain/resources/lore/ui-behaviour-is-a-scene.svx
SHA-256: 4e59da087372307540c40031e6f26d15e0f5f2e84c00a16ee29f072a9d43d6a1

# UI behaviour is a scene

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

A Foldkit program has a Model, Messages, an `update` function, and a view.
A Command is a named side effect. Its result comes back as a Message.
A Scene runs `update`, the view, and subscriptions together, without a browser.

## Input and time are data

A Scene starts from a Model with `given`.
Input is a step such as `pointerDown`, `click`, or `Subscription.emit`.
A timer is a Command, so the test finishes it with `Command.resolve`.

The test does not use fake timers, a clock, or a DOM.
Each step runs in order, and the result is the same on every run.

## The Toast example

[Devin Jameson](https://x.com/devinjameson/status/2108710271417999544) shared a Scene test for the Foldkit UI Toast.
The test name is "returns a short swipe to zero while settling".

1. A pointer goes down on the toast.
2. The pointer moves 30 pixels and releases.
3. The swipe is too short, so the toast settles back. It does not dismiss.
4. The test resolves the settle wait.
5. The test resolves an old dismissal timer with a stale version.
6. The toast still exists.

This paraphrase keeps the steps and drops the setup:

toast short swipe (paraphrase); lines 1-19; highlighted none.

```typescript
scene(
  { update: Toast.update, view },
  given(withEntry()),
  pointerDown(toast, { clientX: 100 }),
  Subscription.emit(MovedSwipePointer({ pointerId, clientX: 130 })),
  Subscription.emit(ReleasedSwipePointer({ pointerId, clientX: 130 })),
  expect(toast).toHaveAttr("data-swipe", "settling"),
  expect(toast).not.toHaveAttr("data-leave"),
  Command.resolve(
    WaitForSwipeSettled,
    CompletedWaitForSwipeSettled({ entryId, version: settlingVersion })
  ),
  expect(toast).not.toHaveAttr("data-swipe"),
  Command.resolve(
    WaitBeforeDismissal,
    CompletedWaitBeforeDismissal({ entryId, version: staleVersion })
  ),
  expect(toast).toExist()
);
```

Read the full test in [the Foldkit source](https://github.com/foldkit/foldkit/blob/49dc36ef672d1caee23f153f88c09d98c8241670/packages/ui/src/toast/scene.test.ts#L329-L366).

## A race is a plain assertion

A race happens when an old result arrives after the state has moved on.
In a Scene, the test resolves the old Command late.
Then it asserts that nothing broke.
The stale dismissal step above is that race.

## Assert on what the view shows

Find elements by role, text, or data attribute.
Do not assert on Model fields.
A Model field can change name while the behaviour stays the same.
A person and an agent can read the steps without the implementation.

The rat-stack reader uses the same shape for its copy button.
The test clicks copy, resolves the copy, and checks the status text.
Then it resolves the reset wait and checks that the label returns:

apps/web/test/reader.scene.test.ts at 1d4d3252326a216909ccec05e93312d1ab0eaf84; lines 51-69; highlighted none.

```typescript
it("a copy confirms with text the reader can see and hear, then resets after the wait", () => {
  scene(
    { update, view },
    given(clipboardReady),
    click(copyButton),
    Command.expectExact(CopyReaderText({ id, text: promptText })),
    Command.resolve(CopyReaderText, Message.SucceededCopyReaderText({ id })),
    expect(role("status")).toHaveText("Copied ✓"),
    expect(copyButton).toContainText("Copied ✓"),
    Command.expectExact(WaitBeforeCopyReset({ id })),
    Command.resolve(
      WaitBeforeCopyReset,
      Message.CompletedWaitBeforeCopyReset({ id })
    ),
    expect(role("status")).toHaveText(""),
    expect(copyButton).toContainText(label),
    Command.expectNone()
  );
});
```

## Plant a bug first

Break the rule the Scene protects. For the Toast, let a stale timer dismiss the entry.
The Scene must fail. Restore the code and watch it pass.

See also: [tests that earn their place](/lore/tests-that-earn-their-place), [model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing), and [the test-behaviour skill](/skills/test-behaviour).

# /lore/workers-answer-requests-durable-objects-own-named-state

Source: .brain/resources/lore/workers-answer-requests-durable-objects-own-named-state.svx
SHA-256: b1a3218c4830672a8343903809d9f8d26e8c3ceb06d937cb3e249fe247584904

# Workers answer requests; Durable Objects own named state

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

**Goal:** decide where a piece of state lives on Cloudflare, and address it by name.

A Worker is Cloudflare's program that answers requests. It runs your code in an isolate, a lightweight sandbox inside the Workers runtime.
A Durable Object is a Worker with a globally unique name and its own storage. [What are Durable Objects?](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/what-are-durable-objects/)

## Why a Worker must not rely on module state

Module state can outlive a request, and that is the problem. Cloudflare lists three facts. [How Workers works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-workers-works/)

- One instance may handle many requests, including concurrent ones. State one request writes, another request can read.
- An isolate can be evicted, for example when the host runs short of resources. Its state goes with it.
- Nothing guarantees that two requests reach the same instance of your Worker.

So Cloudflare recommends that you do not use or mutate global state.
rat-stack fences that advice with the [`rat-stack-patterns/no-module-level-mutable-state`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725/scripts/oxlint-plugin-patterns.ts) lint rule:

scripts/oxlint-plugin-patterns.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 820-821; highlighted none. Title: no-module-level-mutable-state.

```typescript
      moduleState:
        "Module-level let and var hold state that outlives one request. Every request a Worker isolate or server process handles shares it, so one request's state leaks into the next. Fix: keep the state in a `Ref` inside a Layer, a Durable Object, or the database.",
```

The fix names three homes for state. This page covers the Durable Object.

## What a Durable Object adds

Cloudflare lists these properties. [What are Durable Objects?](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/what-are-durable-objects/)

- **A name:** you send a request to one specific object from anywhere.
- **Private storage:** transactional and strongly consistent, and no other object can read it.
- **One thread:** each object handles its work single-threaded, like code in a browser.
- **Created on first use:** you never create or destroy an object yourself.
- **In-memory state resets:** an idle object hibernates and loses memory. Persist anything you need later.
- **Alarms:** an object can schedule itself to wake up at a future time.

## Worked example: one object per join submission

The join intake keeps each submission's contact in its own `Interest` object.
The contact lives under one storage key:

apps/site/src/interest/join-contact-cell.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 3-3; highlighted none. Title: One key per object.

```typescript
export const JOIN_CONTACT_KEY = "join-contact";
```

apps/site/src/interest/join-contact-cell.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 24-25; highlighted none. Title: The cell reads that key from the storage it is given.

```typescript
export const joinContactCell = (storage: JoinCellStorage) => {
  const current = storage.get(JOIN_CONTACT_KEY).pipe(
```

The `Interest` object hands the cell its own storage:

apps/site/src/interest/interest-durable-object.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 118-122; highlighted none. Title: The cell is backed by the object's storage.

```typescript
        ...joinContactCell({
          delete: (key) => storage(state.storage.delete(key)),
          get: (key) => storage(state.storage.get(key)),
          put: (key, value) => storage(state.storage.put(key, value)),
        }),
```

The Worker binds the namespaces once, in its init phase:

apps/site/src/worker.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 386-388; highlighted none. Title: Bind the Durable Object namespaces.

```typescript
  const legacyMcp = yield* LegacyMcp;
  const interests = yield* Interest;
  const interestIndex = yield* InterestIndex;
```

Then it picks an object by name for each request:

apps/site/src/worker.ts at a3f5a14861ce89913e82bea0f7ba02c83e8d4725; lines 403-407; highlighted 407. Title: One object per submission; one object for the index.

```typescript
          () => interestIndex.getByName("index").applicationIds(),
          (actor) => interests.getByName(intakeInstance(actor))
        ),
        contacts: (submissionId: string) =>
          interests.getByName(`join:${submissionId}`),
```

- ``interests.getByName(`join:${submissionId}`)`` reaches the object for one submission. Every request about that submission reaches the same object.
- `interestIndex.getByName("index")` reaches a single index object that lists applications.

The name is the design decision. One name per submission keeps each record apart. One fixed name makes a single place that every request shares.

## Choose the home

The lint fix names three homes: a `Ref` inside a [Layer](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit), a Durable Object, or the database.
Pick a Durable Object when several clients must work through one named place. Cloudflare describes that use as coordination. [What are Durable Objects?](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/what-are-durable-objects/)

Work that must finish after the response needs a recovery record too. See [Request lifetime is not durability](/lore/request-lifetime-is-not-durability).

## Next

Read [Queues, Pipelines, Workflows and K2 do different jobs](/lore/queues-pipelines-workflows-and-k2-do-different-jobs) for work that leaves the request.
Then read [Worker init runs twice](/lore/init-runs-twice) for a boundary inside the Worker's own startup.

# /systems/agent-front-door

Source: .brain/areas/agent-front-door.svx
SHA-256: d717d5c09e32609c6c118c72f443406ad4e81bf389771d39b13e380c7f00aea0

# Hosted agent interfaces

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

`apps/site` hosts the public documentation and agent interfaces.
A capability is one named action with shared input, output, and failure definitions and a server-side implementation.

- MCP means Model Context Protocol. It lets an agent discover and call tools.
- A2A means Agent2Agent protocol. This site uses it to answer documentation questions through search and read.
- Discovery cards describe how to connect with each protocol.
- [OpenAPI](/openapi.json) describes the HTTP API for the registered capabilities, including inputs, outputs, and errors.
- The [agent guide](/llms.txt) explains connection, search, read, and following links between documentation pages.
- The hosted registry includes search, graph traversal, flags, prompts, CAFE news and profiles, learning, code mode, and `joinInterest`.
- [Live OpenAPI](/openapi.json) lists the current HTTP operations. Optional feedback operations depend on the auth configuration.

### Run a program instead of several calls

Use `POST /api/execute` with a JSON `code` string. The MCP `execute` tool runs the same job.

[Code mode](/lore/one-program-can-replace-several-tool-calls) runs several capability calls in one program inside a restricted environment.
`joinInterest` cannot run there.

Source: callable definitions in [`apps/mischief/src/capabilities/index.ts` at `445b1a20b51a5492f8e586daeb9306e8011b7673`, lines 34–45](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/445b1a20b51a5492f8e586daeb9306e8011b7673/apps/mischief/src/capabilities/index.ts#L34-L45).

```js
const found = await tools.search({ query: "cartridges", limit: 1 });
const page = await tools.read({ id: found.matches[0].id });
return { title: page.title, id: page.id };
```

The program passes the search result directly to read.

MCP supports protocol versions 2026-07-28, 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, and 2024-11-05. The newest is stateless. Older clients initialize sessions backed by a Durable Object, Cloudflare's feature for persistent state and compute.

A2A answers documentation questions through search and read. RPC means remote procedure call: a client calls a named operation on the server. Browser RPC serves the browser separately.

## The standard

- Application calls use shared capability value definitions and server-side implementations.
- Discovery and static pages handle routing. Domain calls stay in capability handlers.
- Public API access needs no account or access token.
- [Interest signup](/systems/interest) has its own consent and email-confirmation rules.
- `execute` runs an async function body in a fresh Dynamic Worker, a Cloudflare Worker loaded at runtime.
- It sets `globalOutbound: null` to block outbound network access.
- Imports, exports, and `fetch` are unavailable.
- The program can call only declared capabilities.
- API and MCP allow 120 requests per IP per 60 seconds.
- Execute also allows 6 per IP and 300 total per 60 seconds.
- Native Cloudflare counters apply separately per location.

These routes exist today. A reusable cartridge for agent interfaces remains planned.
A cartridge is a package for one job, with its implementation and required infrastructure.

## Content asset cache

`ContentStore` shares completed catalogs, search indexes, learning decks, and graph views within one Worker isolate.
Concurrent cold requests each perform their own asset reads.
The cache stores a value only after its read and validation succeed.
Failed or interrupted reads leave the cache empty.

Pending reads must not use a shared promise, fiber, latch, or response body.
Those values can belong to the first request's runtime context.
Warm requests reuse decoded data without new asset I/O.

`test/cold-content-runtime.test.ts` sends concurrent first requests through a fresh local Worker.
Its asset adapter adds a delay to make cold reads overlap.
The test uses workerd, production content routes, and the reader wrapper.

## How to check

1. Read the [MCP connection card](/.well-known/mcp.json).
2. Read the [A2A card](/.well-known/agent-card.json).
3. Read [OpenAPI](/openapi.json).
4. Compare the descriptions with `apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts`.
5. Use the `tools/list` request in [llms.txt](/llms.txt).
6. Search for a public document.
7. Read the document.
8. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site test` for protocol routing, rate limiting, and sandbox behavior.
9. Confirm the live cards and capability list before advertising a new agent path.
10. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site exec vitest run test/cold-content-runtime.test.ts` to check cold-request isolation.

Check a new deploy live as well as running local tests.

# /systems/all-stars

Source: .brain/areas/all-stars.svx
SHA-256: 0dac71ae7f09ca1c3fe9b19af498b8c3a0a8f18e63146589400ddceb1571e2ea

# CAFE all stars

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

[CAFE all stars](/all-stars) lists people and channels whose public work builds with Cloudflare, [Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy), Foldkit and [Effect](/lore/effect-basics).
A channel is a YouTube channel, a GitHub org or a blog.

Each entry lives in `.brain/data/cafe/people.json`, beside the CAFE news file.
The content build decodes it with the `CafePerson` [schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary) in `packages/core/src/cafe.ts`.
A bad entry fails the build with its index and field, the same way a bad news row does.

Five read-only capabilities answer every question about the data:

- `listPeople` lists every entry, and `listChannels` lists only the channels.
- `readPerson` reads one profile by its stable id: a GitHub login, or the handle of an org or channel.
- `searchPeople` matches words against names, handles, topics, packages, repos, bios and videos.
- `peopleFor` returns the entries whose topics or repo packages cover every term, with the evidence for each term. Entries that list a term as a topic rank ahead of entries that only list its package.

The `/all-stars` index and each `/all-stars/<id>` page are built from `listPeople` and `readPerson` answers.
They are Markdown by default and HTML for a browser.
`llms.txt` lists the index and every profile, and `/all-stars.xml` is an Atom feed of the entries and their activity.

A news row joins a profile when its GitHub login or X handle matches one of the profile's handles.
A row with no author joins the profile that owns its repo.
The profile lists those rows newest first, and the row on [/news](/news) links back to the profile.

## The standard

- A person or channel enters through a [/news](/news) row, pinned CAFE stack contributions, vendored or credited CAFE code, or sourced public CAFE work.
- The typed `entry` field records the basis. A `news` entry names at least one row.
- A `stack` entry names a pinned package and its contributors or maintainers source. A `vendored` entry links the credited upstream, which must itself build on or teach the CAFE stack.
- A `work` entry links the project and dated stack evidence.
- Choose the first qualifying basis in that order. Stack contributors lead or rank among the repository's top listed contributors. Public work builds on or teaches Cloudflare, Alchemy, Foldkit or Effect.
- There is no per-person preview. An entry ships with the next site update like any other content.
- The content build warns about every author with a /news row and no profile.
- Every fact carries its `source` URL and the `verified` date it was checked, so an agent can cite it.
- A bio holds two or three sentences about CAFE work only, each quoted or linked from its source. Use names or projects, not gendered pronouns; the content build rejects those pronouns.
- An avatar is a file committed under `apps/site/content/avatars`. Pages never load an image from another site.
- A profile never includes location, employer guesses, family, follower counts, private messages, or anything the person did not post publicly about their work.
- Each page ends with a removal line that opens an issue in `joelhooks/rat-stack`. A removal ships with the next site update.

To remove a profile, delete its entry from `people.json` and its avatar file, then rebuild.
Nothing else stores the profile.

## How to check

Run the core tests:

```sh
pnpm --filter @rat-stack/core exec vitest run test/cafe-people.test.ts
```

They check that a generated news row lands on exactly the profile that authored it, newest first.
They check that topic holders rank first in `peopleFor`, however many repos list a package.
They also answer three agent questions from the shipped data through the capabilities alone.

Then call a [capability](/systems/capabilities) on a running site:

```sh
curl --request POST 'https://ratstack.sh/api/peopleFor' \
  --header 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"terms":["foldkit"]}'
```

## Sources

1. [rat-stack/packages/core/src at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/tree/main/packages/core/src)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. The people schema in cafe.ts, the capabilities in cafe-directory.ts, and the join in cafe-people.ts. Accessed 2026-11-02.
