# /systems/analytics

Source: .brain/areas/analytics.svx
SHA-256: 7f050b3186080e2e5c6ff1bfa34a04cc4c3d9489efc6c8c8ba8bbdbff23c6660

# Analytics

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

The `packages/events` [cartridge](/lore/cartridges) is a package for one job, with its implementation and required infrastructure.
It records one JSON event for each HTTP request when capture is enabled.

It follows [capture first, shape later](/lore/capture-first). Each event is stored unchanged. Queries select and interpret its fields later.

A stream receives events. A pipeline copies them to a sink, the destination that writes the stored files.

1. `withEventCapture` wraps the Worker's fetch handler.
2. It sends the event in the background after building the response.
3. A Worker binding, a declared connection to a resource, sends the event to an unstructured Cloudflare Pipelines stream.
4. The pipeline runs `INSERT INTO <sink> SELECT * FROM <stream>`.
5. A Basin Catalog sink writes Parquet files to the Iceberg table `default.events_raw` in R2.

R2 is Cloudflare's object storage. Parquet stores data by column in files. Iceberg organizes those files as a table.
Basin Catalog makes the table queryable with SQL.

Sending events through the public HTTP endpoint is disabled. The sink writes files every 300 seconds by default.
See [Basin Catalog sink](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/sinks/available-sinks/r2-data-catalog/).

Each event holds:

- A visitor id and UUIDv7 message id. UUIDv7 is a time-ordered identifier format.
- A server block: host, received time, salted IP hash, and user agent. The hash combines the IP with a secret salt to produce a one-way value.
- Coarse geography from Cloudflare's [`request.cf`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/request/#incomingrequestcfproperties): continent, country, EU membership, region and region code, city, and time zone.
  It also includes the Cloudflare data center, the network's autonomous system number, and its organization.
  The autonomous system number identifies the network.
- A request block: method, path, status, duration, accept type, and content type.
- Whether the request carries a signed agent header.
- The referrer's origin and path.
- The query string, with credential, email, code, and session keys removed.

## The standard

- Each HTTP response gets exactly one event when capture is enabled.
- Capture preserves the response body and status. Persistent HTML responses may add a visitor cookie.
- The HTTP request body never reaches an event.
- Credential, email, code, and session query keys are removed.
- Basin stores an IP address only as a salted hash.
- Geography comes from `request.cf`, which Cloudflare derives in its data centers. The capture code never derives it from the IP.
- Latitude, longitude, postal code, and metro code are never stored. The Mischief Worker sets `captureCity` to store city.
- A missing or malformed `request.cf` field is left out; it never fails the request.
- In `persistent` mode, the server sets a first-party HttpOnly cookie, which browser scripts cannot read. A browser keeps one id across visits.
- In `daily` mode, no cookie is set. An id never repeats on a later day.
- Each row is `{ "value": <event> }`. The unstructured stream requires the `value` column.
- Ingest accepts events without `value`, but the pipeline drops them as `missing_field`.
- The sink token is read only during deployment. It is never bound into the Worker.

## Worker logs

These HTTP Worker declarations use `privateObservability` from `apps/site/src/observability.ts`:

- Mischief.
- RpcBackend.
- Website.

The policy disables per-request invocation logs and traces. Application `console` and Effect error logs remain enabled. Effect is the library that describes work with typed failures and required services.
A service is a named interface for one job.

500s log their cause with an incident id.

Cloudflare invocation logs contain request, response, and related metadata. They are separate from custom application messages.
Alchemy cannot set `redactQueryString`, so invocation logs would store confirm tokens and device codes from query strings.
Mischief therefore keeps invocation logs off and writes one `HTTP request` log per request with method, path without query, status, and milliseconds.
`joinInterest` logs one outcome label (`accepted`, `busy`, `saved_mail_delayed`, `not_open`, or `failed`) and nothing else.
See [Workers Logs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/workers-logs/).

Client IPs reach Basin only as salted hashes. The Worker policy prevents automatic request-header dumps in stored invocation logs.
Application logs must not print raw IPs or request headers.

These settings apply after deployment. They do not erase stored logs from earlier deployments.

## Crash archive

Mischief declares `MischiefCrashTail` as an Alchemy `tailConsumers` entry.
`registerCrashTail` registers a native tail listener through the host Worker's `listen` method.
Returning a `tail` method from the Effect Worker shape does not register this listener.

The tail Worker receives execution traces after Mischief finishes an invocation.
It records failed outcomes and traces with exceptions, including exceptions after a successful response.

Successful traces without exceptions produce no object.
Initialization exceptions keep their event time and script version even when the trace has no fetch event.

The `packages/crash` cartridge owns the `CrashArchive` port and its R2 adapter.
A private `MischiefCrashBucket` holds one immutable JSON object per failed trace.
Keys use `crashes/<UTC-day>/<random-id>.json`.
Separate objects prevent concurrent deliveries from overwriting a daily file.

There is no daily aggregate or second store.

Each record contains only:

- The outcome.
- Exception names, sanitized messages, and stack locations.
- Console levels and sanitized text from traces with exceptions or an exception outcome.
- The script version id, when Cloudflare supplies it.
- The event time, or `null` when absent.
- The URL path without its query string, or `null` without a fetch event.

Exception messages keep ordinary diagnostic text, including quoted property names.
Redaction removes credential-shaped values, emails, IP addresses, and URL query strings.
Credential rules cover bearer tokens, key assignments, known token prefixes, JWTs, private keys, and long opaque values.
Custom exception names become `[redacted name]`.

Credential rules apply even when Cloudflare removes sensitive header values before delivery.
They cannot identify every secret written as ordinary prose.

Stack locations retain a source filename, line, and column.
They exclude function names, directory paths, URLs, and the first error line.

Known credential-header, cookie, and query values are removed from exception and console text at token boundaries.
Ordinary header values do not participate in redaction.
Paths use credential-shape rules instead of substitutions from unrelated headers or query values.

Console records keep the level and redacted string arguments for exception outcomes or traces with exceptions.
Structured arguments and serialized request payloads are omitted.
Missing levels stay `null`; older records can have no console field.

The archive excludes request headers, bodies, and diagnostic-channel payloads.
Redaction removes recognized private values from diagnostic text.

The tail Worker has no public HTTP route and disables its own observability.
Mischief keeps invocation logs and traces disabled.
Crash capture operates independently of `EVENTS_ENABLED`.

R2 permits direct object reads without a catalog, pipeline, or sink token.
The archive supplies best-effort evidence.
Missing records do not prove health.
Cloudflare delivery limits, missing stack data, and archive failures can leave gaps.

Null fields stay unknown; they do not acquire guessed values.
Replayed deliveries can create duplicate records with different object keys.
The bucket retains its objects when removed from the Stack.

### Read crashes without a dashboard

Use an R2 read-only S3 profile for the archive.
Get the physical bucket name from the production plan for `MischiefCrashBucket`.
Use a UTC-day prefix to bound the listing.
The following commands need AWS CLI and an authenticated R2 S3 profile.

```sh
aws --profile <r2-read-profile> \
  --endpoint-url https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com \
  s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket <crash-bucket> \
  --prefix crashes/2026-10-08/ --max-keys 20 --no-paginate
```

Read `Contents[].Key` from the result.
If `IsTruncated` is true, pass `NextContinuationToken` with `--continuation-token` for the next page.
Fetch one exact key; do not sync the entire archive.

```sh
aws --profile <r2-read-profile> \
  --endpoint-url https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com \
  s3api get-object --bucket <crash-bucket> \
  --key <listed-key> crash.json
```

Compare `eventTime`, `path`, and `scriptVersion` with the failed deployment probe.
Read stack locations against that script version's source.
A Cloudflare ray id is not stored, so this comparison is a correlation rather than an exact join.
Fix the observed cause in a separate change.

Before deployment, run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/crash exec vitest run test/crash.test.ts`.
Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site exec vitest run test/crash-tail.test.ts` to exercise Alchemy's exported tail dispatcher.
After deployment, verify the tail consumer attachment and read an actual failed trace from R2.
Local tests prove projection and archive writes; they do not prove Cloudflare delivery.

## Deleting stored events

A delete from `events_raw` writes a new Iceberg snapshot. Older snapshots keep their Parquet files, and those files still hold the deleted rows.

Snapshot expiry and compaction remove the old files. Cloudflare runs this maintenance on its own schedule. In one test run, no snapshot expired within 38 minutes.

The cartridge does not prove that a delete physically erases a row by a known time. Consider this before you enable capture for visitors who can request erasure, for example under GDPR in the EU or UK:

- `persistent` mode sets a cookie that lasts 400 days. Some jurisdictions require consent for it.
- `daily` mode sets no cookie, and its visitor ids do not repeat on a later day.
- The IP hash salt does not rotate. In persistent mode the same IP gives the same hash. In daily mode the hash includes the request day, so the IP hash rotates daily.
- `EVENTS_ENABLED=false` records nothing.

## Switches

- **`EVENTS_ENABLED`**:
  - Default: `false`
  - What it does: Off retains the bucket, stream, and salt, and records nothing. On adds the catalog, sink, and pipeline.
- **`EVENTS_SINK_TOKEN`**:
  - Default: unset
  - What it does: Requires R2 Admin Read & Write when capture is on. Export it in the deploy shell.
- **`EVENTS_IDENTITY_MODE`**:
  - Default: `persistent` in the site schema
  - What it does: `persistent` or `daily` visitor ids. The Worker falls back to `daily` when absent.

The sink token is read from the process environment. A value in `.env` or an `--env-file` is not seen.
The deploy credential cannot create API tokens, so the sink token is supplied separately.
See [Basin Catalog sink](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/sinks/available-sinks/r2-data-catalog/).

## How to check

1. Check an HTML response in `persistent` mode without a `rat_vid` cookie. The response must set one.
2. Check `pipelinesUserErrorsAdaptiveGroups` for zero pipeline errors.
3. Check `pipelinesSinkAdaptiveGroups` for records and files written. See [Metrics and analytics](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/observability/metrics/).
4. Find the queryable catalog with `wrangler basin catalog get <bucket>`.
5. Query it with `wrangler basin sql query <warehouse> "<sql>"`. The command calls the catalog a warehouse. Wrangler reads `WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN`. See [Query data](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-sql/query-data/).
6. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site exec vitest run test/worker-observability.test.ts`.
7. Review the deployed Worker settings before claiming the invocation-log policy is active.

A cookie proves that the persistent capture wrapper is enabled. It does not prove that an event is stored in the table.

```sql
SELECT json_get_str(value, 'body', 'path') AS path, count(*) AS requests
FROM default.events_raw
GROUP BY path
ORDER BY requests DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

The query reads each path from JSON in the `value` column.

Queries use JSON functions such as `json_get_str`.
See [Scalar functions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-sql/sql-reference/scalar-functions/).

## Tests

The cartridge uses [property-based testing](/lore/property-based-testing) and [model-based testing](/lore/model-based-testing).

Properties cover:

- One event per request.
- Preserved response body and status.
- Persistent cookies.
- No HTTP request body in events.
- No sensitive query keys.

The visitor model follows ids across devices, cookies, and days.
The observability test checks every application Worker declaration against a named privacy policy.
HTTP Workers use `privateObservability`; the tail Worker uses the stricter `silentObservability`.

## Removing it

The README's Keep or cut section lists the removal steps under "No analytics."

# /systems/auth

Source: .brain/areas/auth.svx
SHA-256: f97ba8dc4fbcfa070ac4aabc0e6985096195f71208b81f6c5ce144dad373bf74

# Auth

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

The auth cartridge, `packages/auth`, is a package for one job with its implementation and required infrastructure.
It runs Better Auth, a library for sign-in and sessions, through `@alchemy.run/better-auth`.
It uses the implementation chosen by the [database](/systems/database) cartridge.
People sign in with email and password under `/auth`.

RPC means remote procedure call: a client calls a named operation on the server.
`CurrentPersonMiddleware` checks each call's session before it runs and provides `CurrentPerson`, the signed-in person's id.
This check is middleware: code that runs around a call.

A capability is one named action with shared value definitions and a server-side implementation.
`@rat-stack/auth/devtools` adds `runAsPerson`, the dev-only `rat_test_person` capability, and in-memory test people.

The public sign-in surface is gated by `AUTH_ENABLED`, which defaults to false.
When enabled, [learn feedback](/systems/learn#feedback-sign-in) uses phone approval and a separate feedback-only credential.

The phone page signs in through Better Auth. The agent never receives a sign-in session.
The stock device-token exchange is disabled.

Mischief serves the phone page and the public feedback projections.
It calls the private `LearnFeedbackAuth` Worker through a [Worker binding](/lore/bindings).
That Worker owns Better Auth, the D1 database, and the signing secret.
It has no public route and sets `workersDev` to false.

The web app's dev server also uses auth, where devtools calls can run as test people.

## The standard

- An RPC call without a valid session fails as `Unauthenticated`. That is the only auth failure sent to the client.
- Feedback credentials permit `learnFeedback` only. They cannot provide `CurrentPerson` to another capability.
- Off keeps only the database and signing-secret foundation. It exposes no auth route, feedback tool, or private Worker.
- Mischief contains no Better Auth implementation. `apps/site/scripts/startup-budget.ts` enforces a separate static-startup ceiling for each Worker. Total JavaScript above 2,500,000 bytes warns; it does not fail the build.
- A session whose user id fails the person-id schema check also fails as `Unauthenticated`.
- Test people and `rat_test_person` never reach production. Lint keeps `@rat-stack/auth/devtools` inside dev folders, the CLI, and tests (`rat-stack-boundaries/no-devtools-in-production`).
- A production build of the web app contains no dev module, no devtools code, and no test person.

## How to check

- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/auth test` signs up, signs in, reads a session, protects an RPC call, and runs devtools calls as a test person.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site exec vitest run test/feedback-auth.test.ts` checks phone approval and feedback storage through a separate private server.
- The same tests check flag-off routes and tool discovery.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site startup:check` measures both uploads and rejects auth implementation modules in Mischief.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/web exec vitest run test/production-bundle.test.ts` builds the web app for production and checks the bundle.

# /systems/capabilities

Source: .brain/areas/capabilities.svx
SHA-256: 8762beb665e61c9a7a308defce901441a183f46c7e7f289bf3960713634ce7e4

# Capabilities

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

A capability is one named action with a contract and a server-side handler.
The contract declares the name, input, output, failure, and metadata. The handler implements the action on the server.

Effect is a library for describing work with typed failures and required services.
A service is a named interface for one job.
Schema describes accepted values, their TypeScript types, and the rules for checking and converting them at runtime.

`defineContract` declares input, output, and failure with Effect Schema.
It sets metadata describing the action, such as whether it is read-only, and any approval requirements.
`implement` connects the contract to one handler.

A projection builds a callable interface from a capability.
The projections in `packages/capability` provide:

- A command line.
- An HTTP API with OpenAPI, which describes its routes, inputs, outputs, and errors.
- MCP tools. Model Context Protocol lets an agent discover and call tools.
- RPC calls. Remote procedure call lets a client call a named server operation.
- Code mode, which combines capability calls in one program inside a restricted environment.
  See [one capability, every surface](/lore/one-capability-every-surface) for why.

The hosted registry includes content search and graph traversal, flags, prompts, CAFE news and profiles, learning, code mode, and `joinInterest`.
[`apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/site/src/capabilities/index.ts) composes that registry.
[Live OpenAPI](/openapi.json) lists its HTTP operations. Optional feedback operations depend on the auth configuration.

The local command line projects the core registry in `apps/cli/src/surfaces.ts`.

## The standard

- Application actions exposed through generated routes, tools, and commands come from capabilities. Static pages, discovery documents, result pages, and protocol routing are composed separately. `Rpc.make`, `RpcGroup.make`, `HttpApi*`, `Tool.make`, and `Toolkit.make` outside `packages/capability` fail lint (`rat-stack-boundaries/no-hand-rolled-surface`).
- Input, output, and failure are Effect schemas. JSON Schema, OpenAPI, and the code-mode declarations are derived from them, never written by hand.
- Invalid input is rejected before the handler runs.
- A declared failure returns the declared error type. MCP returns it as a tool error.
- A capability that needs approval adds an `Approval` requirement and an `ApprovalDenied` failure on every interface. Approval is denied by default. HTTP answers a denial with 403.
- Browser code imports contracts only, never handlers (`rat-stack-boundaries/no-browser-server-imports`).
- Code mode reaches only capabilities, through their schemas.

## Code-mode discovery and execution

Code mode derives tool declarations from capability schemas.
The default discovery budget is 2,000 estimated tokens.
The estimate uses four characters per token.

Discovery selects the shortest declarations and gives each namespace a turn.
Namespace summaries mark the selected tools as `COMPLETE` or `PARTIAL`.

`catalogBudget` sets the budget.
`declarations: "inline"` includes all declarations; `"search"` includes none.
An explicit `catalogBudget` takes precedence over either setting.
The declarations resource always contains the full catalog.

Programs can call `tools.$codemode.search` to find declarations.
An exact tool path returns only that tool.
Other queries rank path segments, path substrings, descriptions, then input fields.

`limit` and `offset` bound each page.
`next` holds the next offset; `remaining` counts matching tools after this page.
`total` keeps its meaning as the full catalog size.

Successful execution returns `result`, `logs`, `toolCalls`, and `truncated`.
Failed execution raises the typed `ExecuteError` with `kind`, `message`, optional `tag`, `logs`, `toolCalls`, and `truncated`.
A declared tool failure retains its tag and a safe message.
Parse errors, invalid data, timeouts, and program failures all use this failure channel.

Host cancellation still interrupts execution.

The HTTP execute response uses status 200 for success and 422 for `ExecuteError`.
Failure bodies carry `_tag: "ExecuteError"` and have no `result`.
MCP reports `isError: true`, CLI exits non-zero, and RPC returns the typed failure.

Consumers of the old success-envelope `diagnostic` field must read the failure response instead.
Health checks require HTTP 422 and decode the complete failure schema.

`toolCalls` lists admitted calls in dispatch order, including failed calls.
`maxToolCalls` rejects extra calls before their handlers run.
Both sandbox adapters run at most eight tool calls at once.
`maxOutputBytes` bounds returned JSON and log content by UTF-8 bytes.

Output cuts set `truncated` and keep the diagnostic and call history.
The budget excludes diagnostic, call-history, and transport-envelope bytes.
Both limits are optional; zero is a valid limit.

Handlers keep the services captured when the program starts.
Devtools records each handler's duration and outcome through the existing `CallWatch`.
A downstream storage adapter owns its statement and row limits.

## How to check

- `curl -sS https://ratstack.sh/openapi.json | jq -r '.paths | keys[]'` lists the current HTTP operations. Compare them with MCP `tools/list` using the request in the [agent guide](/llms.txt). Do not assume a fixed capability count.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/capability test` covers input rejection before the handler and typed failures as tool errors. It checks approval denial as a 403 and a typed tool error, denial by default, and code-mode calls through capability schemas.
- `pnpm lint` fails on any callable interface built outside `packages/capability`.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/capability exec vitest run test/catalog.test.ts test/sandbox-limits.test.ts test/sandbox-conformance.test.ts test/code-mode-context.test.ts` checks discovery, search pages, limits, and captured services.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site exec vitest run test/code-mode-runtime.test.ts` checks the same diagnostics, limits, and concurrency in local workerd.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/devtools test` checks handler duration and failure recording during code-mode execution.

## Removing an interface

The README's Keep or cut table lists the files for "No HTTP", "No MCP", and "No code mode." Cutting MCP cuts code mode, because code mode is built on the MCP toolkit.

# /systems/database

Source: .brain/areas/database.svx
SHA-256: 4d2cc9a9b6b95eac6ade7db99623e815fa9b1eabdfad2495490802d47235acc6

# Database

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

The database [cartridge](/lore/cartridges), `packages/database`, is a package for one job, with its implementation and required infrastructure.
It gives callers one service, `RunLog`. A service is a named interface for one job.

`RunLog` records a capability run with its outcome and lists a person's recent runs.
A capability is one named action with shared value definitions and a server-side implementation.

`DatabaseVendor` chooses where rows are stored: Cloudflare D1, or Postgres through Hyperdrive.

D1 is Cloudflare's SQL database. Hyperdrive connects Workers to a Postgres database through pooled connections.

The chosen implementation includes its resources, Drizzle table definitions, and database migrations.
Drizzle defines and queries tables in TypeScript. Migrations change the database structure.

Effect describes work with typed failures and required services. Schema describes accepted values and their runtime checks.

[Auth](/systems/auth) uses the selected database vendor in the web development backend and the optional private `LearnFeedbackAuth` Worker.
`AUTH_ENABLED` controls the public feedback sign-in surface. The database foundation stays declared when that surface is off.
See `apps/site/src/auth/foundation.ts` and `apps/site/src/auth/private-worker.ts` for the composition.

## The standard

- Callers use `RunLog` and never see SQL, Drizzle, or the chosen implementation.
- Choosing an implementation is one `DatabaseVendor` value.
- Every input passes its Schema check before it reaches storage. Bad input fails as `InvalidDatabaseInput`, and a storage failure fails as `DatabaseError`.
- Run ids use UUIDv7, a time-ordered identifier format. Times come from the Effect clock, so tests control both.
- The same tests pass on both implementations.
- Migrations load when the process starts outside the package.
- A Hyperdrive Postgres query leases its pool for the query and releases it after 250 ms idle. A request never holds the pool across a provider wait. See [Durability](/systems/durability).

## How to check

`pnpm --filter @rat-stack/database test` runs the `RunLog` tests twice, against D1 on local SQLite and against Postgres on PGlite. They cover both outcome variants, filtering by person, limits, ordering by time then id, and rejected limits. A second test loads the migrations from outside the package.

## Sources

1. [rat-stack/packages/database/src/run-log.ts at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/database/src/run-log.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. RunLog service; used for the storage boundary and typed failures. Accessed 2026-10-01.

2. [rat-stack/packages/database/src/vendor.ts at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/database/src/vendor.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Vendor choice; used for D1 and Hyperdrive Postgres selection. Accessed 2026-10-01.

3. [rat-stack/packages/database/test/run-log.test.ts at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/database/test/run-log.test.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Shared storage tests; used for the behavior checked on both vendors. Accessed 2026-10-01.

4. [rat-stack/packages/database/test/migration-paths.test.ts at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/database/test/migration-paths.test.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Migration tests; used to verify loading outside the package. Accessed 2026-10-01.

# /systems/devtools

# Devtools

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

`packages/devtools` adds `rat_*` capabilities to a development application.
A capability is one named action with shared value definitions and a server-side handler, the code that implements it.
The tools list and read calls, call an action, run a recorded call again, and compare results.
`CallWatch` surrounds the handler's approval check and records denied calls too.

A state machine defines named states and the events that permit movement between them.
An actor is a running unit that processes events or performs work for a machine.
`watchActor` lets lifecycle machines report states and events through `ActorWatch`.
Both watchers do nothing unless the application supplies recording.

Effect describes work with typed failures and required services. A service is a named interface for one job.

A Layer describes how to build services and supply their construction dependencies. The recording Layer supplies the watchers.

The local web development backend records calls and serves the overlay, RPC, and MCP tools under `/__rat`.
RPC lets a client call a named server operation. MCP means Model Context Protocol, which lets an agent discover and call tools.

The command-line interface (CLI) enables its devtools interfaces with `--devtools`. They are available only from the same computer.
These capabilities are available only in development.

## The standard

- Tools call existing capabilities through their schemas and handlers. A schema defines the accepted values.
- Recorder code and test people stay in development applications and tests.
- Every Effect-backed lifecycle actor is handed to `watchActor`.
- Production bundles contain no web development modules, devtools code, or test people.

## How to check

- Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/devtools test` for recording and tool behavior.
- Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/web test` for the local backend and production-bundle exclusion test.
- Run `pnpm lint` for `no-devtools-in-production` and `watch-effect-actors`.
- Inspect `rat_list_actors`, `rat_list_transitions`, and `rat_get_actor` in a development application after running a lifecycle capability. Without a recording Layer, these tools cannot show whether a lifecycle ran.

## Sources

1. [Devtools package](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/tree/main/packages/devtools)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Call recording, replay, diff, and inspection capabilities. Accessed 2026-10-01.

2. [Call watcher](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/call-watch.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Ambient call observation without production recording. Accessed 2026-10-01.

3. [Actor watcher](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/capability/src/actor-watch.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Ambient lifecycle observation. Accessed 2026-10-01.

4. [Production bundle test](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/apps/web/test/production-bundle.test.ts)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Exclusion of development code and test people. Accessed 2026-10-01.

# /systems/durability

Source: .brain/areas/durability.svx
SHA-256: 4510d3018c69b8bd66dc329a84d4a4ebfe42212833d75b9de9b4375beda11594

# Durability

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

Durability here means four things:

- A slow provider never holds a database connection.
- A request never waits on a provider after its data commits.
- A tunable changes without a code edit.
- A gate stops only real harm.

rat-stack uses [Effect](/lore/effect-basics)'s own primitives for each one, in real seams. Agents load the [durability skill](/skills/durability) before they change one of these seams.

Each card below has five fields:

- **Problem:** what goes wrong.
- **Primitive:** the Effect answer.
- **Seam:** where rat-stack uses it.
- **Fence:** the test or lint rule that fails on the bug.
- **Incident:** where the lesson came from.

The incidents come from drovr on 2026-10-23.

### 1. Lease a connection for the query

- **Problem:** a connection held across a provider call starves the pool.
- **Primitive:** `RcRef` with `idleTimeToLive`, borrowed inside `Effect.scoped`.
- **Seam:** `packages/database/src/connection-lease.ts`, used by the Hyperdrive Postgres run log. Each request gets its own `RcRef`, because workerd pins sockets to a request.
- **Fence:** `packages/database/test/connection-lease.test.ts`, a model over queries, bursts, and provider waits.
- **Incident:** drovr car #2350. `mysql.acquire` p95 rose from 0.06 s to 2.3 s while PostShiba was slow.
- **Principle:** [lease-connections-per-query](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/lease-connections-per-query.md).

### 2. Answer at commit; dispatch off the request

- **Problem:** a request kept open across a provider call times out its caller.
- **Primitive:** `waitUntil` at the edge, with a backstop that replays the same [idempotency](/lore/http-responses-need-validation) key.
- **Seam:** `joinIntakeLayer` saves a ready contact with a pending-delivery marker. `JoinRequest.afterResponse` runs delivery through `waitUntil`. A five-minute sweep redrives indexed pending contacts with their submission ids.
- **Erase:** the contact is removed after its event tombstone lands. The sweep retries indexed pending erases.
- **Limit:** record and sweep-index writes are separate. A failed index write can strand delivery or erasure. An early erase can also prevent the request's ready commit. [`packages/core/spec/README.md`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/spec/README.md#weaker-environments) records both gaps and the operator backstops.
- **Fence:** `packages/core/test/join-answer-at-commit.model.test.ts` and `packages/core/test/intake-sweep.model.test.ts`.
- **Incident:** drovr's ingress forward. Five `POST /events` answered 503 after their events committed.
- **Principle:** [answer-at-commit](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/answer-at-commit.md).

### 3. Set a provider timeout once

- **Problem:** timeout literals in several layers drift apart.
- **Primitive:** a `Context.Reference` with a default, read at [layer](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) build, then `Effect.timeoutOption`.
- **Seam:** `DrovrIntakeTimeout`. Browser and agent intake both read it. The Worker sets it from `DROVR_INTAKE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. `JoinDeliveryDeadline` gives every delivery one 25-second budget across its retries, under the 30-second `waitUntil` allowance.
- **Fence:** `packages/subscriber-delivery/test/intake-timeout.test.ts`.
- **Incident:** drovr #2339 changed a PostShiba timeout by deploy.
- **Principle:** [one-timeout-at-the-boundary](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/one-timeout-at-the-boundary.md).

### 4. Bound work in flight

- **Problem:** a serial loop lets provider latency set throughput. An unbounded fan-out floods the provider.
- **Primitive:** `Effect.forEach` with `concurrency`, or a `Semaphore`.
- **Seam:** the application listing in `apps/site/src/interest/applications.ts` reads 8 at a time, in id order. `intakeRedeliver` stops at the first outcome other than accepted and returns the rest.
- **Fence:** `apps/site/test/intake-applications-concurrency.test.ts`.
- **Principle:** [bound-in-flight-work-with-keys](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/bound-in-flight-work-with-keys.md).

### 5. Scope waiters to the request

- **Problem:** a module-level `Deferred` or `Semaphore` in a Worker isolate makes one caller wait on another caller's work.
- **Primitive:** a `Deferred`, `Cache`, `Ref`, `Semaphore`, `Queue`, `Latch`, `PubSub`, `PartitionedSemaphore`, or `TxSemaphore` created inside one request or runtime [scope](/lore/scopes-own-resources).
- **Fence:** `rat-stack-patterns/shared-waiters`, with a rejecting and an allowed fixture per constructor in `packages/core/test/patterns-rule.test.ts`.
- **Incident:** drovr cars #2344 and #2348.
- **Principle:** [scope-waiters-to-the-request](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/scope-waiters-to-the-request.md).

### 6. Climb a flag with a ledger

- **Problem:** changing one value by deploy costs a plan, a readback, and another deploy to undo it.
- **Primitive:** a `Context.Service` flags [port](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) with `Layer` adapters and a declared lifecycle [machine](/lore/lifecycles-are-machines).
- **Seam:** the [flags](/systems/flags) [cartridge](/lore/cartridges) separates the `declared → rollingOut → on → removed` lifecycle from scoped evidence rungs. `flip_feature_flag` changes a rung. The default operator adapter commits position, receipt and projection marker in one Durable Object transaction.
- **Fence:** `packages/flags/test/writes.model.test.ts` and `packages/flags/test/lifecycle.model.test.ts`.
- **Incident:** drovr shipped `postshiba-send-hold` dark behind three rungs.
- **Principle:** [climb-flags-with-a-ledger](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/climb-flags-with-a-ledger.md).

### 7. Fail open on liveness, closed on harm

- **Problem:** a gate that refuses on delay stops good work. A fallback in front of real harm lets the harm through.
- **Primitive:** `Schema.TaggedError` refusals, `Effect.catchTag`, and bounded retries.
- **Seam:** the deploy driver refuses an unapproved replacement or deletion with `PlanRejected`. It retries content-version mismatches until a deadline. Failed flag replica reads follow the declaration's `failurePolicy`: catalog default or typed refusal.
- **Fence:** `packages/deploy/test/plan.test.ts` and `packages/deploy/test/content-propagation.model.test.ts`.
- **Incident:** PostShiba's p50 rose from 0.3 s to 8 s. 46 of 47 timed-out first asks still arrived, and drovr did not resend.
- **Principle:** [fail-open-on-liveness](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/skills/durability/principles/fail-open-on-liveness.md).

## The standard

- Every pattern has a seam in shipped code. Toy examples do not count.
- Every pattern has a fence. The fence fails on a planted copy of its incident's bug.
- A provider call never runs inside a held database lease.
- The join answer does not wait on delivery. Its uniform response is not proof that every storage write succeeded.
- Each provider has one timeout value. Config sets it at the [composition root](/lore/structure-effect-by-domain).
- Every fan-out names its bound.
- Effect stays at the pinned version. These patterns add no dependency.

The idle lease of 250 ms is a guess. drovr lists the same value with an expiry. Measure it before you depend on it.

## How to check

1. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/database exec vitest run test/connection-lease.test.ts`.
2. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/core exec vitest run test/join-answer-at-commit.model.test.ts`.
3. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/subscriber-delivery exec vitest run test/intake-timeout.test.ts`.
4. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site exec vitest run test/intake-applications-concurrency.test.ts`.
5. Plant a bug and watch its fence fail:
   - Hold the lease for the whole request.
   - Run delivery before the answer.
   - Put `"20 seconds"` back in the agent intake.
   - Make the application read unbounded.
6. Run `pnpm turbo run check test build --concurrency=1` for the full gate.

# /systems/fence

Source: .brain/areas/fence.svx
SHA-256: 506441063c535703b136160e9a50ce5c836d7f7afbb659ac1bf065edc876907b

# Fence

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

The fence is the compiler checks, lint rules, and hooks that reject prohibited code and shortcuts. [The fence](/lore/the-fence) explains the idea.
Effect describes work with typed failures and required services. A service is a named interface for one job.

XState `6.0.0-beta.1` defines state machines: named states and the events that permit movement between them.
`@xstate/effect` `1.0.0-beta.0` runs them as scoped Effects and supplies the compiled inline-Effect lint rule.
These checks enforce it today:

- Type-aware Oxlint runs Ultracite's core rules and the repo's plugins in `scripts/oxlint-plugin-*.ts`. The plugins cover boundaries, patterns, no comments, Effect tests, and XState with Effect. Vendored anti-slop rules also run. All use `error` severity in `oxlint.config.ts`.
- `rat-stack-boundaries/no-core-adapters` keeps provider adapters out of core. An adapter implements an application-owned interface for a specific provider.
- Ports, interfaces named for application jobs, stay in core. [Fixture tests](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/test/boundaries-rule.test.ts) prove the import boundary.
- Effect language-service diagnostics, compiler messages about Effect code, are set to `error` in `tsconfig.base.json`. `effect-tsgo patch` runs in `prepare`, so both `tsc` and the editor report failures.
- `@yielded/effect-tsrs` `0.2.3` runs TypeScript and Effect diagnostics in `typecheck` and `check`. Every invocation uses `--strict --type-check`. `--type-check` includes ordinary TypeScript diagnostics; `--strict` makes Effect warnings fail.
- effect-tsrs bundles tsrs `8f135f106a63`, contained in plain tsrs `0.20.0`.
- Plain [tsrs](https://blog.cloudflare.com/typescript-rust-port/) `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta` stays in `typecheck:fast`, targeting TypeScript `7.1.0-beta`. It still has no Effect diagnostics; use `typecheck` or `check` for those.
- Patched TypeScript `7.0.2` with `@effect/tsgo` `0.67.5` runs through `pnpm typecheck:tsc` at the switch and on checker bumps. CI does not run it. `ignoreEffectWarningsInTscExitCode` stays false.
- Report any checker disagreement.
- Lefthook runs `pnpm check` and `pnpm test` before every commit.
- `scripts/vcs-command-policy.js` blocks `git … --no-verify`. The Pi extension, the Claude Code hook, and the Cursor hook all call that one file.
- Continuous integration (CI) runs `pnpm turbo run check test build` after a fresh dependency install.
- The install uses the exact versions in the lockfile; it cannot update that file.

## The standard

- A commit runs check and test, and a failure stops it.
- No agent harness configured in the repo can bypass the hooks with `--no-verify`.
- Effect diagnostics fail the typecheck.
- `pnpm bump:checkers` compares effect-tsrs and patched `tsc` errors, including Effect `TS377xxx`, for every package and root scripts. It normalizes paths, ignores suggestions and messages, and compares exit verdicts.
- The same command compares plain tsrs with patched `tsc`, excluding Effect-only codes. Plain tsrs cannot emit those diagnostics.
- Code carries no prose comments. Tool directives need a reason after `--`; type assertions need a one-line `SAFETY:` statement of the condition that makes the assertion safe. Plain JS may keep type-only JSDoc. [No comments](/lore/no-comments) and [repo law](/AGENTS.md) give the full exception policy.
- Every lint or diagnostic override names its rule and gives a reason.
- The number of overrides only shrinks. The [debt ledger](/debt.md), a report counting lint and diagnostic exceptions, publishes the count by kind.
- A new lint rule ships with a test that runs real Oxlint against fixtures.
- Loosening any of this needs the owner's sign-off.

## How to check

- `pnpm turbo run check test build` runs the main gate.
- `pnpm typecheck` runs strict effect-tsrs diagnostics.
- `pnpm typecheck:tsc` runs the patched compiler.
- `pnpm typecheck:parity` compares checker errors and exit verdicts. `pnpm bump:checkers` runs it on every bump.
- `pnpm typecheck:fast` runs plain tsrs for fast feedback without Effect diagnostics.
- `echo '{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git commit --no-verify"}}' | node scripts/hooks/block-git-no-verify.mjs` prints a `deny` decision with the reason.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/core test` runs the fixture tests for the boundary, pattern, no-comment, and unknown-parameter rules, and the command policy test.
- The boundary fixtures in `packages/core/test/boundaries-rule.test.ts` reject adapter imports from core and accept composition outside it.
- `curl -sS https://ratstack.sh/debt.md` shows the current override count.

2. [rat-stack/tsconfig.base.json at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/tsconfig.base.json)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Compiler configuration; used for Effect diagnostics at error severity. Accessed 2026-10-01.

   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Commit hooks; used for the pre-commit check and test gate. Accessed 2026-10-01.

4. [rat-stack/scripts/vcs-command-policy.js at main · joelhooks/rat-stack · GitHub](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/scripts/vcs-command-policy.js)

# /systems/flags

Source: .brain/areas/flags.svx
SHA-256: 12c8f80b8fc41ddbe7e958f1b5e2208822209b8efc334be0a70bc733299c1eb7

# Feature flags

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

The `packages/flags` [cartridge](/lore/cartridges) evaluates typed flags.
A flag declares its name, [schema](/lore/schemas-define-the-boundary), default, owner, purpose, removal date, and [evidence ladder](/lore/flags-climb-on-evidence).

Each rung names its authority and exit measurements. A read scope is the partition for a flag value and its evidence.
A child schema defines it; the default is `global`.

Handlers request the `Flags` [service](/lore/services-capture-dependencies) from core.
The Config [adapter](/lore/hexagonal-architecture) reads deployment configuration.
The memory adapter supplies rules and writable values for tests.

The KV adapter owns its namespace through [Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy).
Under the default policy, missing KV values use Config values or declared defaults.
The `refuse` policy returns a typed failure on a missing or failed replica read.

- `listFlags` lists names, owners, and removal dates.
- `getFlag` evaluates one flag for an optional subject.
- Allow-lists select a value for named subjects.
- Percentage rules use a stable hash of the flag name and subject.
- The first matching rule wins. Missing subjects use the default.

`EVENTS_ENABLED` defaults to `false` and stays deploy-time Config.
Live KV writes cannot change this flag.

`EVENTS_IDENTITY_MODE` defaults to `daily`.
The Worker reads its live value for each captured request.
Config keeps the existing environment keys and boolean spellings.
An empty KV namespace preserves Config behavior.

Invalid Config stops initialization.
A failed KV read follows the catalog's `failurePolicy`.
The default policy returns the declared default. The `refuse` policy preserves the typed failure.

Previews use Config and declare no flags namespace.
The production Worker and content backend read KV.

[Alchemy](/skills/learn-alchemy) still selects analytics resources during deployment.
See [Analytics](/systems/analytics) for capture and identity behavior.

## The standard

- Flag values pass their declared schemas.
- Every declaration names an owner and a `removeBy` date.
- Lint rejects declarations without a literal removal date.
- The flags build rejects expired registered events flags with a typed repair message.
- Each subject keeps its rollout bucket when the rollout percentage changes.
- The lifecycle permits `declared` → `rollingOut` → `on` → `removed`.
- Declared [Effect](/lore/effect-basics) actors record lifecycle transitions. Removed flags stay removed.
- Each [capability](/systems/capabilities) shares its [contract](/systems/capabilities) across surfaces. JSON encoding is required for `getFlag`.

Three operator capabilities replace the raw setter:

- `flip_feature_flag` climbs one rung or flips `off`.
- `record_flag_evidence` records a measurement at the current rung and exact scope.
- `read_flag_ledger` reads a bounded attempt page and the authoritative position.

Climbs use the capability approval service. Above agent, they also need an `approvalRef` quote.
The roles are `agent`, `arbiter`, and `owner`. Token checks belong in the child's composition.

`off` bypasses approval and still records its caller in the attempt ledger.

The CLI accepts `--yes` or asks for interactive approval on a climb.
Its default composition has no live ledger and returns a named error.

The CLI records `local-cli` as a channel label.
Its caller has no authenticated person identity.

The public Worker, [RPC](/skills/learn-rat-stack) readers, and read-only sandbox expose no flag writes.
A child mounts its operator [surface](/lore/one-schema-three-surfaces) and supplies its approval policy and ledger adapter.

Each available-store attempt records its caller, flag, observed old value, requested value, time, and outcome.
The journal stores an immutable Pending key before the approval gate.
A separate completion key records success, denial, failure, or interruption.
Both keys share an attempt id.

Missing completion means Pending with an unknown result.
A failed completion write returns a typed error; the flag may have changed.
Audit storage failures block only writes.
Config and default journals use composition-local memory.

A projection is a copy derived from a committed value.

The default operator adapter uses one Durable Object per flag and scope.
It serializes transitions and commits the value, receipt, and dirty projection marker together.
An alarm projects that committed value to KV. Failed projection keeps the marker for redrive.

Readers use KV and never call the Durable Object.

KV changes may take 60 seconds or more to reach another location.
The observed old value in an attempt may be stale. Climb validation uses the DO's authoritative position.
Use deployment settings or a stronger control path for kill switches and safety stops.

The explicit KV ledger fallback keeps immutable attempt and outcome keys.
It refuses authoritative flips and evidence writes with `FlagAtomicityRequired` by default.
A composition can opt in with `authoritativeWrites: "accept-non-atomic-unserialized"`.

That option accepts the absence of atomic commit and cross-isolate serialization.
Writes to the same KV key can hit its one-write-per-second limit.

The crash-recovery proof uses a persisted service double.
Native workerd transaction and alarm behavior still needs provider qualification.
The operator ledger is not wired into the deployed Stack.

The lifecycle journal is scoped memory, with no durable state between processes.

## How to check

1. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/flags test` for rollout properties, generated write histories, audit failures, and lifecycle histories.
2. Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/core exec vitest run test/patterns-rule.test.ts` for the removal-date [fence](/lore/the-fence).
3. Run `pnpm turbo run check test build --concurrency=1` for the full gate.
4. Inspect the deployment plan. Readers declare one KV namespace. The operator [layer](/lore/layers-make-dependencies-explicit) adds the ledger DO and its KV write [binding](/lore/bindings).
5. Follow [Add a feature flag](/skills/add-a-feature-flag) for scoped evidence, authority, and crash-redrive checks.

To remove the cartridge:

1. Replace `apps/site/src/flags.ts` with core imports.
2. Export `flagsLayer = Flags.defaults(eventFlags)` and `liveFlagsLayer = flagsLayer`.
3. Remove the package dependency and its directory.

Callers keep their typed defaults.
The CLI retains its named read-only failure.

## Sources

1. [Flags cartridge](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/tree/main/packages/flags)
   rat-stack. Evaluation, adapters, audit journal, lifecycle, and behavior tests. Accessed 2026-10-11.

2. [How KV works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/concepts/how-kv-works/)
   Cloudflare. Eventual consistency, cached missing keys, and no atomic transactions. Accessed 2026-10-11.

3. [Workers KV limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/platform/limits/)
   Cloudflare. One write per second to each key. Accessed 2026-10-11.

# /systems/interest

Source: .brain/areas/interest.svx
SHA-256: 4525946b9a86a6f9ab1e2951d57355df3bb76f2b8425e122ddf256bd02a9c7f5

# Interest signup

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

Applications are [agent-only](/tokenmaxx#interested). Submission starts email confirmation. A person must follow the email link in a browser to confirm signup. Confirmation does not reserve a seat.

An agent applies for a person through the `joinInterest` capability.
A capability is one named action with shared value definitions and a server-side implementation.
Call it through MCP, `POST /api/joinInterest`, or the command-line interface (CLI).
MCP means Model Context Protocol, which lets an agent discover and call tools.

The agent view of [/tokenmaxx](/tokenmaxx) carries a fresh page ticket and the application steps. Ask the questions, show an editable card, and submit only what the person approves. Refusals return the same answer as success, and the person still confirms by email.

`SubscriberIntake` and `SubscriberConfirm` are ports in core: interfaces for starting email confirmation and confirming a signup.
`packages/subscriber-delivery` provides the adapter, the implementation that connects those interfaces to external delivery.
The Worker chooses and supplies that implementation when it starts.

See [hexagonal architecture](/lore/hexagonal-architecture). List signup is separate from [account authentication](/systems/auth).

## The standard

- A person must confirm their email before joining.
- Consent is explicit: the person approves the agent's exact card and contact permission. An agent must not infer permission to subscribe someone from their address or an unrelated request.
- Agent application refusals receive a neutral answer rather than revealing whether an address is on file. Expired confirmation links have deliberate refusal responses. Retired submission endpoints return 410 without capturing or delivering an application.
- Provider details remain outside core; `no-core-adapters` enforces that boundary.
- An agent application needs a fresh page ticket, contact consent, and the person's approval of the exact application data. A ticket works once.
- The normal path saves a ready contact before answering. Delivery runs after the response through `waitUntil`, within a default 25-second budget. The five-minute sweep retries indexed pending delivery with the same submission ID.
- Erase writes the event tombstone before removing the contact. A tombstone failure keeps the erase pending. A deliverer that reads an erase marker refuses delivery.
- Record and sweep-index writes are separate. A failed index write can strand pending delivery or erase.
- An erase during the first request can prevent its ready commit while the uniform response still leaves. These gaps remain open. See [`packages/core/spec/README.md`](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/blob/main/packages/core/spec/README.md#weaker-environments) and [Durability](/systems/durability).
- For a stranded submission, an authorized operator can inspect its ID, then use `intake redeliver` or `intake erase`. A uniform submission response does not prove delivery or confirmation.

### Applicant identity

`joinInterest` accepts optional `name` and `x` fields.
The name trims whitespace and allows 1–100 characters. This keeps preferred names short.
Skipped fields and historical applications omit both keys.

- The X field accepts a handle or profile URL and stores `https://x.com/handle` in lowercase.
  Handles allow 1–15 ASCII letters, digits or underscores, including existing short handles.
  It refuses status, intent and navigation URLs.
- [X documents the 15-character limit](https://help.x.com/en/managing-your-account/x-username-rules) and [the allowed characters](https://help.x.com/en/managing-your-account/change-x-handle). Its current account-renaming guidance requires more than four characters. This field reads existing profiles rather than registering usernames.
- Identity is stored in protected form in the application's `started` event, which records the start of an application.
  It uses the same contact key as the answers. Erasure removes that key and its rows.
- Only the authenticated application reader reads the protected identity. The delivery request is unchanged and carries neither field.
- Capability observers receive identity fields with their values removed.
  Request analytics, trace spans, and logs never receive those values.
  A trace span records an operation's timing and outcome.
- MCP request tracing is disabled in the protocol implementation for modern and legacy protocols.
  The protocol's `tools/call` span records raw parameters before the capability observer can remove sensitive values.

## Operator commands

Set `INTEREST_OPERATOR_TOKEN` through the local environment schema. Keep its value private.

- `rat-stack intake list --submission-id <id>` reads one application.
- `rat-stack intake erase --submission-id <id>` erases local contact data and sealed answers.
- `rat-stack intake redeliver --submission-id <id>` retries a ready application with its original submission ID.

Repeat `--submission-id` to provide an ordered batch. Redelivery processes one ID at a time.

- Only ready contacts without an abuse hold can be sent by default. Erased contacts appear as missing.
- Add `--dry-run` to inspect every named ID without sending or changing state. Eligible rows say `would_send`.
- Add `--include-refused` only for explicitly approved IDs whose refusal came from a verified availability failure.
  This per-call option repairs named refused contacts to ready before delivery. It never permits held or accepted contacts.
- The live batch stops at the first skipped, refused, or retry outcome. The result lists IDs not attempted.
- Each row contains the pre-run state in `previousState` and the resulting `state`.
- The response contains submission IDs, outcomes, and states. It contains no email addresses or answers.

The operator route is `POST /operator/interest/applications/redeliver`. It uses the same bearer token as erasure.

If the command fails, read application states before retrying. A failed request can have completed part of the batch.

A scorer outage alone saves a ready contact without sending. The response tells the person that confirmation is delayed.

Non-holding signals can accompany that outage: `ticket_instant`, `no_answers`, `jev_off`, and `jev_clear`.
Real abuse holds and unknown signals keep the contact held, even with a scorer outage.

Use redelivery after the outage is fixed. The saved submission ID stays unchanged.

Rate refusals return a busy message and save nothing. The agent waits one minute and retries once.

## How to check

- Read `apps/site/src/interest/routes.ts` for email confirmation, `retired-routes.ts` for 410 responses, and `packages/core/src/join-intake.ts` for agent applications. The only published signup capability is `joinInterest`.
- Run `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/core test` for lifecycle behavior and `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site test` for submission and confirmation integration tests. `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/subscriber-delivery test` checks the adapter contract.
- With an authorized test address, approve an agent application, receive the confirmation email, follow its link, and confirm. Source and local tests alone do not prove inbox delivery or the external list state.
- Check [OpenAPI](/openapi.json) for `joinInterest` and read the agent view of [/tokenmaxx](/tokenmaxx) for the application steps. Do not bypass confirmation.

# /systems/learn

Source: .brain/areas/learn.svx
SHA-256: ab773be270919720f9fd373875f40a121f6551b4224ba2f543de8bd2643a9c20

# Learn mode presents concepts at useful depths

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

Learn mode explains the technology and principles used in real work. [The learn skill](/skills/learn) controls when the agent presents an explanation. The operator enables the mode and can stop it at any time.

The build derives a concept deck from public lore, system pages, and skills. Cards preserve page titles, summaries, terms, references, and links. Explicit prerequisite metadata supplies prerequisite ids.

A page that is not a concept, such as an announcement, sets `learn: false` in its frontmatter. The build leaves it out of the deck and logs its id.

A card can also teach with three optional fields:

- **`plain`**:
  - Source: Page frontmatter
  - Content: One line in plain words, shown before the claim.
- **`snippet`**:
  - Source: `.brain/data/learn-cards/<id>.ts`
  - Content: The smallest idiomatic TypeScript for the idea.
- **`diagram`**:
  - Source: Page frontmatter
  - Content: Plain text, at most 30 columns and 12 rows of one-column characters.

A capability is one named action with shared value definitions and a server-side implementation.
Four capabilities serve the deck and learning events. Two local capabilities serve display preferences:

- **`learnDeck`**: List the public cards.
- **`learnCard`**: Read one card at a requested depth.
- **`learnNext`**: Select explanations for concepts in play.
- **`learnRecord`**: Record an explicit learning event.
- **`learnPreferences`**: Read local display preferences. Local only.
- **`learnSetPreferences`**: Change local display preferences. Local only.

`learnNext` and `learnRecord` treat omitted progress as empty version 1 progress.

XState owns the learning lifecycle as a state machine: named states and the events that permit movement between them.
Effect describes the work with typed failures and required services. A service is a named interface for one job.

Selection follows deck order when context is absent. A public context term selects its owner and resolves unintroduced prerequisites first. A shown walkthrough introduces a prerequisite. Dismissed prerequisites count as satisfied; dismissed cards stay silent.

- New concepts receive a walkthrough.
- Introduced concepts receive a line, or a paragraph after seven days.
- Familiar concepts receive a line after seven days.
- Fluent concepts stay silent until asked or after ninety days of inactivity.
- Dismissed concepts stay silent.

The command-line interface (CLI) and MCP tools use a local progress adapter, an implementation that connects learning operations to local files.
MCP means Model Context Protocol. Its stdio connection uses the process's standard input and output to carry tool calls.

The learning cartridge provides the adapter through `@rat-stack/learn/local`.
A cartridge is a package for one job, with its implementation and required infrastructure.
The CLI supplies filesystem access and the default directory.

Public HTTP and MCP calls operate on supplied progress. The public server stores no progress. The default local directory is `~/.rat-learn/`.

- **`log.jsonl`**: Authoritative append-only learning events.
- **`cards.jsonl`**: Rebuildable concept progress.
- **`tasks.jsonl`**: Rebuildable concept ids and presentation depths.
- **`README.md`**: Store shape and recovery instructions.
- **`preferences.json`**: Display width, visual style, and snippet length. A missing file means narrow inline text with full snippets.

### Feedback sign-in

Feedback is separate from learning progress. A person signs in through Better Auth and approves an agent's code on their phone.
The agent receives a credential that permits `learnFeedback` only. The database stores feedback against the approving person.

- **`learnFeedbackStart`**: Return a short code, verification URL, lifetime, and polling interval.
- **`learnFeedbackPoll`**: Report pending, approval, denial, expiry, or polling too fast.
- **`learnFeedback`**: Validate the credential and card, then store the agreed feedback.

The phone page is `/learn/approve`. It shows the code and requires sign-in before approval.
The stock `/auth/device/token` endpoint is disabled because it issues a full sign-in session.

Feedback credentials are separate signed values. They cannot authenticate a normal Better Auth session.

The device machine reflects the provider's stored approval facts. Its declared Effect actors inspect the grant and issue the credential.
The credential machine checks signature, audience, expiry, and the current grant before it returns an author.

Learn owns the `FeedbackAuthor` [port](/lore/hexagonal-architecture). Mischief provides its auth adapter inside each request.
Learn imports no auth provider.

`AUTH_ENABLED` defaults to false. Off removes sign-in routes, the phone page, feedback HTTP operations, and feedback MCP tools.
The D1 database and signing-secret foundation stay declared to keep state and resource ownership.
On adds Better Auth table migrations and the Worker bindings that use them.

Feedback writes are not replay-idempotent. Each successful call stores a new row.
An uncertain write needs a storage check before another attempt.

## The standard

- The operator opts in. The skill stops when the operator opts out.
- Feedback requires a signed-in person's approval. Denial and expiry issue no credential.
- A feedback credential grants no authority to any other capability.
- Feedback credentials never enter local progress files, feedback text, or published examples.
- Questions require separate opt-in. The agent asks at most one check-in per long session.
- Selection does not record a presentation. The agent records `shown` after presenting.
- Events contain concept ids and learning metadata. They contain no code, paths, names, or prompts.
- Public deck requests contain no local progress.
- The local log remains the authority. The adapter validates it before every operation.
- Identical events append once. A writer lock protects each operation.
- Derived copies can be replaced. An incomplete source log fails without writes.
- Cards preserve source text. The build accumulates reference and prerequisite errors.
- Every card needs a public reference. Only `learn: false` removes a page from the deck, and the build logs each one.
- The build compiles every snippet with the real `tsc` and the Effect diagnostics. It collects every failure before it stops.
- A missing snippet or diagram is a coverage warning. The build reports the counts.
- `rat-stack-patterns/learn-snippet-idiom` keeps snippets on the service idiom: operations, a namespaced key, `static layer` with `Service.of`, and `Effect.provide` at the edge.
- Preferences stay on the machine. No request carries them.
- Property tests check depth and merge. A generated history model checks events and elapsed time.

Effect Schema describes accepted values and their runtime checks.
The event schema defines the available observations:

packages/core/src/learn-model.ts at b4d6b8f499e57bc76914ad70df3a0c99751ae28c; lines 66-80; highlighted none. Title: Explicit learning events.

```typescript
export const LearnEventSchema = Schema.Union([
  Schema.Struct({
    at: LearnTimestampSchema,
    depth: LearnDepthSchema,
    id: ConceptIdSchema,
    kind: Schema.Literal("shown"),
    version: Schema.Literal(1),
  }),
  Schema.Struct({
    at: LearnTimestampSchema,
    id: ConceptIdSchema,
    kind: Schema.Literals(["used", "got-it", "skipped", "dismissed"]),
    version: Schema.Literal(1),
  }),
]);
```

## How to check

Build the CLI and start its local stdio MCP:

```sh
pnpm turbo run build --filter=@rat-stack/cli
node apps/cli/dist/cli.js mcp --devtools
```

Through an MCP client:

1. Call `learnDeck` and choose `lore.effect-basics`.
2. Call `learnNext` with that id and timestamp 100. Omit progress.
3. Confirm the returned depth is `walkthrough` in a fresh store.
4. Call `learnRecord` with a version 1 `shown` event at 100 and depth `walkthrough`.
5. Call `learnNext` at 101. Omit progress again.
6. Confirm the returned depth is `line`. The local log supplies the progress.
7. Inspect `rat_list_calls` for three successful learning calls.

Use a fresh test directory through `RAT_LEARN_DIRECTORY`. These timestamps are test fixtures. Use current Unix timestamps in milliseconds for real presentations.

Without MCP, use the same local adapter through the CLI:

```sh
node apps/cli/dist/cli.js learnNext \
  --context '{"at":100,"ids":["lore.effect-basics"]}'
node apps/cli/dist/cli.js learnRecord \
  --event '{"at":100,"depth":"walkthrough","id":"lore.effect-basics","kind":"shown","version":1}'
node apps/cli/dist/cli.js learnNext \
  --context '{"at":101,"ids":["lore.effect-basics"]}'
node apps/cli/dist/cli.js learnPreferences
```

Confirm `learnPreferences` prints narrow inline text in a fresh directory. Check one event in `log.jsonl`. Repeat the record command and confirm that the event count stays one. Confirm outbound deck requests contain only an empty JSON body.

With feedback sign-in enabled in a test composition:

1. Call `learnFeedbackStart` and open its verification URL while signed out.
2. Sign in on the phone, check the code, and approve feedback access.
3. Poll with `learnFeedbackPoll`, respecting its interval.
4. Call `learnFeedback` with a real public card id and the agreed text.
5. Confirm the returned id and the stored person's id.
6. Check that the credential cannot authenticate a normal session or authorize another capability.
7. Repeat with denial and expiry. Confirm neither grants feedback access.
8. Disable the flag. Confirm the routes, OpenAPI operations, and MCP tools are absent.

The tests use memory auth for the HTTP seam. They do not establish deployed D1 health.
The schema limits feedback to 2,000 characters, card ids to 200, and credentials to 4,096.
These are initial input bounds, not measured traffic limits.

Run the implementation checks:

```sh
pnpm --filter @rat-stack/learn test
pnpm --filter @rat-stack/auth test
pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site generate
pnpm turbo run check test build --concurrency=1
```

Read `/_content/learn.json` after deployment. Confirm it includes this system page and the learn skill. Build success does not establish deployment health.

# /systems/motion

Source: .brain/areas/motion.svx
SHA-256: 07c81391e3f89e9a7e4980c856b798dcf1c48ca92a5ae44822ce2c3bd66472d2

# Motion

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

`@rat-stack/motion` moves values over time in a Foldkit app. Its core is four TypeScript modules in `packages/motion/src/*.pure.ts`. They import only each other, so another project can copy them at a pinned commit.

- **Easing**: Robert Penner's ten curve families come in three variants each: in, out and in-out.
- **CSS easing**: `linear`, `cubic-bezier()`, `steps()` and keywords such as `ease-in-out` follow the CSS spec.
- **Tween**: a value moves between two endpoints over a duration along one easing. The `sample` function reads the value at any time. A retarget starts a new tween from the sampled value, so the value never jumps.
- **Spring**: a value of any dimension follows a target with stiffness, damping and mass. The `critical(frequency)` preset arrives without overshoot.
- **Interpolation**: numbers, tuples, colours in OKLab, and 2D transforms split into translate, scale and rotate.

The spring takes fixed steps of 1/120 s. It carries the leftover time to the next frame. When it comes to rest, it snaps exactly onto the target.

packages/motion/src/spring.pure.ts at 5fa5df1543b8122a678722d5465ae65fc8a4bf2d; lines 245-259; highlighted 252-254. Title: Each substep checks for rest, so the snap happens at the same instant at any frame rate.

```typescript
  const span = Math.min(MAX_STEP_MS, Math.max(0, elapsed));
  const ticks = into.remainder + span / SUBSTEP_MS;
  const substeps = Math.floor(ticks + SUBSTEP_GRID_TOLERANCE);

  for (let substep = 0; substep < substeps; substep += 1) {
    substepInto(into);

    if (atRest(into.config, into.position, into.velocity, into.target)) {
      return snapInto(into);
    }
  }

  into.remainder = Math.max(0, ticks - substeps);

  return into;
```

The Foldkit [adapter](/lore/hexagonal-architecture), `@rat-stack/motion/foldkit`, keeps a clock and the named tweens and springs in the Model. A frame is a `TickedFrame` Message. `Motion.advance` steps every spring and moves the clock. The view samples each tween at the clock time.

packages/motion/src/foldkit.ts at 5fa5df1543b8122a678722d5465ae65fc8a4bf2d; lines 186-202; highlighted none. Title: Frames run only while something moves, and the reduced-motion preference arrives as a Message.

```typescript
export const motionSubscriptions = <Model, Message>(
  options: MotionSubscriptionOptions<Model, Message>
) =>
  Subscription.make<Model, Message>()(() => ({
    motionFrame: Subscription.animationFrameEntry<Model, Message>({
      isActive: options.isAnimating,
      toMessage: (elapsed) =>
        options.toMessage(Message.TickedFrame({ elapsed })),
    }),
    reducedMotion: Subscription.persistentEntry(
      Dom.streamFromMediaQuery({
        mapMatches: (isReducedMotion) =>
          options.toMessage(Message.ChangedReducedMotion({ isReducedMotion })),
        query: REDUCED_MOTION_QUERY,
      })
    ),
  }));
```

Pick a target in the demo at the end of this page, then pick another before the dots arrive. The tween restarts its curve. The spring keeps its speed and turns.

The curve gallery plots every easing.

## The standard

- Every easing starts at 0 and ends at 1. The CSS start jumps are the exception: `steps(n, jump-start)` begins at 1/n, as the spec requires.
- Every curve except back, elastic and bounce never falls. Every out curve mirrors its in curve: `out(t) = 1 - in(1 - t)`.
- `cubicBezier` agrees with an exact bisection reference for any valid control points.
- A tween with a monotonic easing stays between its endpoints. A retarget keeps the sampled value.
- One spring step of a span gives the same state as two steps that split it on the substep grid.
- A critically damped spring from rest settles within six periods, snaps exactly, and never overshoots in one dimension.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, every tween and spring lands on its target at once.
- No Worker graph imports the package, so it adds no startup bytes.

Each rule is an `it.prop` property over generated inputs. Each property also runs against a planted bug, and the suite fails if the property passes it.

packages/motion/test/spring.test.ts at 5fa5df1543b8122a678722d5465ae65fc8a4bf2d; lines 344-355; highlighted none. Title: The frame-rate property must reject an integrator that takes one step per frame.

```typescript
      "the frame-rate property catches an integrator that takes whole frames",
      () =>
        falsifies(
          Arbitrary.all([
            movingSpring,
            integerBetween(1, 6),
            integerBetween(1, 6),
          ]),
          ([from, first, second]) =>
            splitAgrees(wholeFrameEuler, from, first, second)
        )
    );
```

## How to check

- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/motion test` runs the properties and the planted bugs.
- `packages/motion/test/vendoring.test.ts` fails if a core module imports anything except another core module, or names a browser global.
- `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site typecheck` prints the Mischief startup size against its ceiling.
- Open [/systems/motion](/systems/motion) with reduced motion turned on. The dots and curves show their end state.

   Robert Penner. The MIT and 3-Clause BSD terms for the easing equations; used for the curve set. Accessed 2026-11-02.

2. [CSS Easing Functions Level 1](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-easing-1/)
   W3C. The cubic-bezier() and steps() definitions and the named presets. Accessed 2026-11-02.

3. [A perceptual color space for image processing](https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/)
   Björn Ottosson. The OKLab matrices used for colour interpolation. Accessed 2026-11-02.

# /systems/prompts

# One prompt serves people and agents

New on /news: [tla-ts 0.0.9 adds TLC's -continue](/news).

## What it does

A prompt is a saved set of instructions for an agent.
A capability is one named action with shared value definitions and a server-side implementation.
A projection builds a callable interface from capabilities.

- `/prompts` lists published prompts.
- Each detail page shows the full prompt, a copy control, and its credit.
- Markdown is the default representation. Browsers request HTML.
- `listPrompts` and `getPrompt` expose the same source through capability projections.

## The standard

- `.brain/resources/prompts/` owns the source. The content build owns derived assets.
- Title, description, and body must contain text. Validation reports independent failures together.
- Core owns the `PromptLibrary` port, an interface for listing and reading prompts.
- Content and command-line adapters implement that interface for their data sources.
- The public catalogue requires no identity or mutable database record.
- Existing Worker infrastructure serves the assets. No prompt execution or scheduling occurs here.
- Foldkit Messages and Commands own clipboard interaction. Prompt text remains unchanged.

## How to check

1. Run the full check, test, and build gate.
2. Open `/prompts/hill-climb` and copy its text.
3. Disable JavaScript. Read the full prompt and its credit.
4. Request `/prompts` without an HTML Accept header. Check the Markdown list.
5. Call `listPrompts`, then call `getPrompt` with a returned slug.
6. Check that an unknown slug returns `UnknownPrompt`.

See [use-a-prompt](/skills/use-a-prompt).

## Sources

1. [Prompt capabilities and reader pages](https://github.com/joelhooks/rat-stack/pull/45)
   GitHub joelhooks/rat-stack. Source ownership, shared contracts, adapters, and copyable pages. Accessed 2026-10-07.
